title: Tooling: local ComfyUI/SDXL art backend on /mnt/d for artgen
description:
## Problem / goal
Concept rounds run on OpenRouter (google/gemini-2.5-flash-image). Problems seen on real issues: it ignores the requested aspect ratio (sim-73n.3 panels, sim-rdl.7.7 reactor frame), leaves white margins and needs a green background keyed out, can't hold one silhouette across many variants (the 19 bricks in sim-usq.1), can't tile seamlessly (sim-rdl.10 background layers), and costs about $0.04 per image. The user wants a local ComfyUI pipeline with SDXL, plus LoRAs for the graffiti line-art style (art/style.md), to give the art team better control.

## Decisions (user, 2026-10-02)
- **Everything goes on the external drive `/mnt/d` (D:\, 1.4 TB free):** a ComfyUI instance and/or a shared model repository. Download the exact models needed there.
- **Crash constraint:** when the user runs ComfyUI and WSL with the agents at the same time, the agents crash. The setup must avoid this; see the notes.
- The user already has the SDXL model in a local Windows ComfyUI install (location unknown; not in the usual Documents/AppData places). Reuse it rather than downloading it again where possible.
- OpenRouter stays as a fallback and for quick exploration.

## Behaviour
1. **Model repository on D:** e.g. `D:\ai\models\{checkpoints,loras,controlnet,vae,ipadapter,...}`, which ComfyUI uses through `extra_model_paths.yaml`, so Windows ComfyUI and any WSL ComfyUI share one copy. Move or link the user's existing SDXL checkpoint into it.
2. **Starter models** (download exactly these, record name, URL, hash and licence in `D:\ai\models\MODELS.md`): the SDXL base checkpoint (existing), the SDXL VAE, a ControlNet for SDXL (lineart and/or canny, to hold a silhouette), an IP-Adapter for SDXL (style reference), the LayerDiffuse nodes and weights (native transparent output), and 1–2 flat-vector / cel-shaded LoRAs picked by a test, not up front. Custom nodes: ComfyUI-Manager, LayerDiffuse, ControlNet aux preprocessors, IP-Adapter plus, and a seamless-tiling node.
3. **ComfyUI server reachable from WSL:** artgen talks to it over the HTTP API (`/prompt`, `/history`, `/view`, `/upload/image`), with the URL configured, e.g. `ART_COMFY_URL`.
4. **artgen backend:** `artgen gen --backend comfy --workflow <template>`. API-format workflow JSON templates live in a `workflows/` dir: `txt2img`, `img2img_ref` (IP-Adapter), `silhouette` (ControlNet from a picked sprite's outline), `transparent` (LayerDiffuse), `tile_bg` (seamless). The output goes into the same `round-N/vK.png`, `meta.json` (model, LoRAs, seed, steps, workflow name, $0 cost) and contact sheet as the OpenRouter path, so the concept-artist, art-director and producer flow doesn't change. Add `art: backend:` / `comfy:` keys to `.claude/workflow.yaml` and document them in the art-pipeline skill.
5. **Bake-off before switching:** regenerate the sim-usq.1 r1/v4 titanium brick base and one other class from its outline (silhouette workflow), plus one sim-rdl.10 tiling cloud layer. Put them on a contact sheet next to the Gemini rounds for the user to judge. Switch the default backend only if the user approves.
6. **Later, separate task:** train a project graffiti-style LoRA (kohya or ai-toolkit, SDXL, fits in 12 GB) from roughly 15–30 user picks once enough exist.

## Out of scope
The LoRA training itself (item 6), Flux models (12 GB only runs quantised versions, and slowly), and changing any game code.

## Notes for the coder
- Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti, 12 GB VRAM. The WSL VM has 15 GB RAM (no `.wslconfig`, so the default is half the host's RAM). SDXL needs about 8 GB VRAM plus several GB of system RAM.
- **Crash hypothesis (verify, don't assume):** host RAM contention. Several Claude agents plus cargo/trunk builds grow the WSL VM while Windows ComfyUI loads SDXL. Options to evaluate: run ComfyUI on **Windows** (outside the VM) with `--lowvram`/`--disable-smart-memory` and call it from WSL over localhost (check that WSL can reach Windows localhost; mirrored networking or the host IP); cap the VM with `.wslconfig memory=`; serialise generation (one comfy job at a time, a lock like `scripts/native-run.sh`'s display lock). Running ComfyUI inside WSL competes with the agents in the same VM and with WSLg's GPU, so it's probably the worse option. Record what was tried and what fixed it.
- artgen currently lives outside this repo (`~/.claude/skills/art-pipeline/scripts/artgen.py`). The pm decides where the backend code lives: vendored into the repo (e.g. `tools/artgen/`) or changed in the skills/agent-workflow source.
- `~/ComfyUI` in WSL is an empty fresh checkout (no models or custom nodes). Remove it or point it at the D: models; don't download models twice.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Model repository on /mnt/d with MODELS.md (name, source URL, sha256, licence for every file); the user's existing SDXL checkpoint reused, not downloaded again
- [ ] ComfyUI with the listed custom nodes runs and is reachable from WSL; generating with it while the agent team works does not crash the agents (document the setup and the cause found)
- [ ] `artgen gen --backend comfy --workflow <t>` writes round dirs, meta.json and the contact sheet in the same format as the OpenRouter backend; the 5 workflow templates are checked in
- [ ] Silhouette workflow: 4 variants from one picked sprite keep its outline (overlay check); transparent workflow gives real alpha with no keying; tile_bg output wraps with no seam
- [ ] Bake-off contact sheet (sim-usq.1 base + 1 class, one sim-rdl.10 cloud layer) shown to the user; the default backend switches only with the user's approval
- [ ] art-pipeline skill and workflow.yaml `art:` keys document the new backend; OpenRouter still works
close_reason: Replaced: ComfyUI now runs natively on Linux (~/Projects/ComfyUI, systemd service), artgen backend in sim-4ws.1/.2, leftover graphs and the Gemini comparison in sim-4ws.3

comments.author: pm@breakout
comments.text: [meta] pm — direction from user 2026-10-03 (spec on hold): (1) artgen should become a reusable standalone tool/project, not breakout-only: prompt → generate → pick → in-game previews, game-agnostic, with breakout and other games linking into the process. Skills dir is one option; a new repo is being considered. (2) User is moving the desktop to Omarchy (Linux) imminently, which likely removes the Windows/WSL ComfyUI + crash constraints; ComfyUI would run natively. Re-spec after the move. Bake-off decision rule agreed: switch default backend per workflow, not globally. Hands-on setup: guided session with the pm.

title: Wire the graffiti behaviour outline frames into bricks (replace coded strips, gentler pulse)
description:
## Problem / goal
The graffiti behaviour outline frames (sim-usq.3, PR #81) are merged:
- `assets/sprites/bricks/outline_{charge,breach,demolition,regen,shield,reactor}.png`
- 168×68 RGBA, drawn around a 160×60 plate, transparent centre

**But no code loads them.** `src/bricks/outline.rs` still draws every outline as coded colour strips (`OutlineStrip`, laid out by `strips()`); its doc says the final art "replaces only the strip children". So this task wires the painted frames in, keeps the behaviour animation, and confirms they read well in game. It's not just a check.

## Behaviour
- **Painted frames:** each special brick draws its painted frame instead of the coded strips. The six frames are reactor, regen, shield, charge, breach and demolition. Plain classes (ceramic, titanium, tungsten) still get none.
  - The frame is centred on the brick, at the plate's scale: 168×68 art drawn at `BRICK_WIDTH × 168/160` by `BRICK_HEIGHT × 68/60`. So the frame's edge sits about 4 art px outside the plate on every side.
  - Its rings (10–15 px in the art) overlap the plate's outer edge a little. That's intended, as long as the plate stays readable.
- **Layering:** brick plate < frame, leaving z room above the frame for the outline particles. Those aren't wired yet; sim-auw adds them later. The frame goes with its brick when the brick is destroyed (it stays a child of the brick).
- **Animation (user 2026-10-03, gentler pulse):** the same pulse rates per style as today, and regen still blinks faster as healing nears. But the frame's brightness ranges **60–100%** (not 25–100%), so the frame and its motif always stay readable. It freezes while paused, as today.
- **Fallback:** if a frame's PNG is missing or fails to load, that style keeps the coded strips; there's no panic.
- Web build shows the same.

## Out of scope
- Changing the art. If a frame hides too much of the plate, a behaviour can't be told apart, or the size is wrong, the coder files an `art` issue under sim-usq (`stage:brief`) with a screenshot for the art-director (for example "thin the demolition ring"). It isn't patched in code.
- Brick plates (sim-23j), ball/paddle/power-up (sim-x72). The outline particle sheets (sim-rdl.7.7 art) are sim-auw.
- New pulse rates or colours.

## Notes for the coder
- Follow the skin pattern in `src/sprites.rs`:
  - Add the six outline handles to `GameSprites`, part of `all()`.
  - Add a skin rule that, once the handle is loaded, gives the `BrickOutline` entity a `Sprite` with the image and frame size, marks it `Skinned`, and hides its `OutlineStrip` children. This mirrors `skin_frame`.
- **Animation:** `animate_outlines` sets each strip's colour from `strip_color(style, weight, lit)`. For a skinned outline, set the frame sprite's colour to white, scaled by brightness, mapping the pulse onto 60–100%.
  - Add a named constant, e.g. `PAINTED_PULSE_LOW = 0.6`, next to `PULSE_LOW`/`PULSE_HIGH`.
  - Keep the coded-strip path unchanged for the fallback.
- Explosive variants map to `outline_charge` / `outline_breach` / `outline_demolition` by `ExplosiveKind`.
- The asset-contract test from sim-23j already pins the six outlines at 168×68.
- Update `outline.rs`'s `//!`: painted frames with a coded fallback.
- Tests: headless checks that each special class maps to the right outline path, that a skinned outline's brightness never drops below 0.6 while pulsing, and that the strips stay as the fallback when the image isn't loaded (as in the existing outline tests).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `cargo run`: every special brick (reactor, regen, shield, charge, breach, demolition) shows its painted graffiti frame, and no coded strips are visible; plain bricks have no frame
- [ ] Screenshot at 1x: all six behaviours are distinguishable at a glance by colour and motif, and the brick plate inside each frame stays readable (not hidden by the ring)
- [ ] Frames are centred on their bricks with an even margin on all four sides
- [ ] Frames pulse visibly but never fade below about 60% brightness; a hit regen brick's frame blinks faster until it heals; frames freeze while paused
- [ ] Breaking a framed brick removes its frame with it
- [ ] Renaming `assets/sprites/bricks/outline_shield.png` and restarting: shield bricks show the coded strips, the others show painted frames, and nothing panics
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the painted frames in the browser
- [ ] `cargo test` includes the class→outline-path mapping, the 60% brightness floor and the strip fallback; clippy and `trunk build` pass

title: Verify graffiti brick sprites in game and pin the brick asset contract with a test
description:
## Problem / goal
The graffiti line-art brick set (sim-usq.1, asset PR #73) has merged. It replaced the 18 brick plates in place, keeping the same paths and the 160×60 size (drawn at 80×30 world):
- `assets/sprites/bricks/<class>_intact.png` and `<class>_cracked.png` for all 7 classes
- `_broken.png` for titanium, tungsten, reactor and regen

`BrickSprite::path` / `damage_path` / `damage_looks` should pick them up with no code change. This task confirms that in the running game, pins the asset contract with a test, and fixes code only if something visibly breaks.

## Behaviour
- Every brick class draws its graffiti intact plate at spawn, with no flat-colour fallback anywhere. That covers ceramic, titanium, tungsten, reactor, explosive (all three variants), regen and shield.
- At 1x on the #0a0e15 background, the seven classes read apart at a glance. The explosive variants are still told apart by their behaviour outlines (charge/breach/demolition).
- **Damage ladder** (sim-rdl.7.9 rules, unchanged): each hit a brick survives moves it along intact → cracked → broken. Each state looks clearly worse than the one before. A regen heal goes back to intact.
- The behaviour outline frames (168×68 art, drawn around the 160×60 plates) still sit evenly around the new plates, with no gap or overlap on one side.
- `reactor_broken.png`'s small transparent edge notches are intended. They show the background through them, not a flat colour block.
- Web build shows the same.

## Out of scope
- Changing the art. If a plate is wrong (classes don't read apart, a damage state doesn't look worse, wrong size), the coder files an `art` issue against sim-usq.1's pipeline (`stage:brief`, parent sim-usq) with a screenshot, and doesn't patch it in code.
- The ball/paddle/power-up and outline reskins (sim-usq.2/.3).
- Changing damage thresholds.

## Notes for the coder
- Likely no gameplay code change. Possible fixes if something breaks: outline offset/size constants in `src/bricks/outline.rs`, or sprite sizing in `src/sprites.rs`.
- Add a headless test that pins the asset contract. For every `BrickSprite` and each of its `damage_looks()`, the file exists under `assets/` and is a 160×60 PNG (read the IHDR width/height bytes, no decoder needed). Do the same for the 6 `outline_*.png` at 168×68.
- For the visual check, use `scripts/native-run.sh --label sim-23j`. A temporary local harness that spawns one row of every class/state is fine, but don't commit it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `cargo run`: a fresh board shows every class with its graffiti intact plate, and no flat-colour brick anywhere
- [x] A screenshot at 1x shows all 7 classes clearly distinct from each other; the three explosive variants are told apart by their outlines
- [ ] Hitting a titanium and a tungsten brick shows intact → cracked → broken, each visibly worse; hitting ceramic, explosive and shield shows intact → cracked; a damaged regen brick heals back to intact
- [ ] Behaviour outlines (reactor, regen, shield, charge, breach, demolition) sit evenly around their plates, with no gap or overlap on any side
- [ ] A broken reactor brick shows its edge notches as transparent (background visible), not a solid block
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the same graffiti plates in the browser
- [x] `cargo test` includes the asset-contract test (every brick plate 160×60, every outline 168×68, all present); clippy and `trunk build` pass
- [ ] Any art defect found is filed as an `art` issue under sim-usq (linked in a comment), not patched in code

title: Art pipeline: local ComfyUI backend for artgen
description:
## Problem / goal
The art pipeline can only generate through OpenRouter. ComfyUI is now running locally (systemd user service, http://127.0.0.1:8188, SDXL base + fp16-fix VAE + boldline/lineart LoRAs + ControlNet-Union promax on a 12 GB 4070 Ti, ~9 s per 1024² image). We want artgen to use it as a second backend, with **the pipeline itself defined by ComfyUI workflow files the user edits in the ComfyUI UI**, not hard-coded in Python.

## Behaviour
- `artgen gen --backend comfy --workflow <api-format.json> ...` runs a saved ComfyUI API-format graph. artgen fills in only nodes titled `artgen:*` (prompt, negative, seed, size, control) and leaves the rest of the graph alone.
- The user can change the pipeline by editing the graph in ComfyUI and re-exporting it (Workflow → Export (API)). No artgen code change is needed.
- Rounds have the same layout as OpenRouter rounds (round-N/v{i}.png, meta.json, index.html). They cost $0 and are limited only by max_rounds.
- ControlNet shape control: artgen draws a silhouette mask from the asset size, or takes a supplied PNG.

## Out of scope
IP-Adapter, img2img/`--ref` for comfy, using the ControlNet mask as an alpha matte, Flux, replacing artgen's background removal, and moving artgen into git.

## Notes
Children: (A) artgen backend plus SKILL.md, a direct edit in ~/.claude/skills/art-pipeline (not version-controlled, so no PR); (B) the breakout repo side: starter graph, SDXL prompt section in style.md, workflow.yaml `art` block, agent docs (normal PR). B depends on A. Reference graph: ~/Projects/ComfyUI/user/artgen-smoke.py.

title: Add ComfyUI workflow-file backend to artgen
description:
## Problem / goal
Add a `comfy` backend to `~/.claude/skills/art-pipeline/scripts/artgen.py` that runs a user-editable ComfyUI API-format workflow file through the local ComfyUI HTTP API.

## Behaviour
- New `gen` flags: `--backend {openrouter,comfy}` (default `openrouter`, so existing calls are unchanged), `--workflow <file.json>` (required for comfy), `--negative` / `--negative-file`, `--seed <int>` (default random; variation i uses seed+i-1), `--size WxH`, `--control <png>`, `--control-size WxH`, `--comfy-url` (default `$COMFYUI_URL` or `http://127.0.0.1:8188`). For comfy, `--model` is optional and only used as a label.
- **Slot convention.** Nodes are matched by `_meta.title`:
  - `artgen:prompt` → `inputs.text`
  - `artgen:negative` → `inputs.text`
  - `artgen:seed` → `inputs.seed` or `inputs.noise_seed`
  - `artgen:size` → `inputs.width` / `inputs.height`
  - `artgen:control` → `inputs.image` (a LoadImage; the PNG is uploaded first via POST /upload/image)
  - `artgen:output` → the SaveImage to read; if there's exactly one SaveImage, it's used without a title.

  `prompt` and `seed` are required. The other slots are optional. Supplying a value for a slot the graph doesn't have, or a graph without a required slot, is a clear error that names the slot. Nothing outside the slots is changed.
- **Silhouette.** `--control-size WxH` draws a control image: white filled rounded rect at the asset's aspect ratio, centred with a margin, on black. It's drawn at the generation size, which defaults to the SDXL ~1 MP bucket closest to that aspect ratio unless `--size` is given. `--control <png>` overrides it. The control image used is saved as `round-N/control.png`.
- **Running.** Variations are submitted one by one, then artgen polls `/history/{id}` with a timeout (default 600 s, `--timeout`) and downloads via `/view` (with the subfolder). A per-variation failure is recorded as `{v, error}` and doesn't stop the round; exit 2 only if every variation fails. If ComfyUI is unreachable, it says the service isn't running (`systemctl --user status comfyui`).
- **Provenance.** `meta.json` gets `backend`, `workflow` (path), `graph` (the full filled-in graph for v1), `negative`, `seeds[]`, `size`, `control` and `cost_usd: 0`. `model` is still present: the `--model` label or `comfy:<workflow stem>`. The contact sheet header shows it. `cost`/`issue_cost` keep working with mixed and older meta files.
- **`artgen comfy-info`** (new subcommand): lists the checkpoints, LoRAs and ControlNets the server reports (/object_info), and with `--workflow` lists the `artgen:*` slots it finds.
- `--ref` with `--backend comfy` → error "not supported for comfy yet".
- Still only stdlib + Pillow (PEP 723 header unchanged).
- SKILL.md: document the backend, flags, slot convention, Export (API) steps, and that comfy rounds count toward max_rounds but not budget_usd.

## Out of scope
The repo-side starter graph, style.md, workflow.yaml and agent docs (sibling task). `--ref` for comfy. Alpha from the mask.

## Notes for the coder
- **Where to edit.** artgen is NOT in the breakout repo, and ~/.claude is not git. Edit in place: no branch, no PR. Before editing, back up artgen.py and SKILL.md to `<file>.bak-<id>`. Put the evidence (test output, generated contact sheet path) in beads comments, not a PR.
- **Seam.** `_generate_one(model, prompt, refs)` (≈l.111-135) returns `(png_bytes, {usage, text})`. Add a comfy equivalent with the same return shape (cost 0) so `job()`/cost summing stay the same. `_request` (l.73-91) dies when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is missing. The comfy path must not need it. `cmd_gen` is ≈l.138-196, argparse ≈l.425-488, `build_sheet` reads `meta['model']` (≈l.249-289).
- **Tests.** Factor the pure functions `fill_slots(graph, values)`, `sdxl_bucket(w,h)` and `silhouette(size, aspect)`. Add `scripts/test_artgen.py` (stdlib unittest) with a fake ComfyUI from `http.server` on port 0. It should cover: /prompt, /history (pending then success, plus a failure variant), /view, and /upload/image.
- **Reference graph.** `~/Projects/ComfyUI/user/artgen-smoke.py` (working SDXL+LoRA graph via the HTTP API, used in the setup smoke test). ControlNet-Union needs `SetUnionControlNetType` before `ControlNetApplyAdvanced`; both exist on the live server.
- **Risk.** ComfyUI caches identical graphs. Distinct seeds avoid that.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `artgen gen --model <openrouter id> ...` without --backend behaves exactly as before (same files and meta fields; an OpenRouter regression test in test_artgen.py passes)
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest` in scripts/ passes with ComfyUI stopped (fake server): slot filling, missing-slot errors, distinct seeds per variation, partial failure recorded + exit 2 on total failure, poll timeout

title: Ship starter ComfyUI sprite graph, SDXL prompt preamble and comfy-aware art agents
description:
## Problem / goal
Give the art team a working, user-editable ComfyUI pipeline in the breakout repo, and teach the art agents to use the comfy backend from the sibling task.

## Behaviour
- `art/comfy/sprite.json`: starter API-format graph with slots titled `artgen:prompt|negative|seed|size|control|output`. It uses SDXL base + `sdxl_vae_fp16_fix`, LoRA `sdxl-boldline` at 0.8, ControlNet-Union promax (lineart/canny type, start strength ~0.8), 30 steps, cfg 6.5, dpmpp_2m karras, and a plain flat background. Load it in ComfyUI, change it, re-export, and artgen uses the change.
- `art/comfy/README.md`: the slot convention, how to load/edit/re-export (Workflow → Export (API)), and that every graph must keep the titled slots.
- `art/style.md`: new `## Prompt preamble (SDXL)` section with fenced **positive** and **negative** tag blocks. Comma tags, no hex codes, no prose; it says the same as the existing preamble. For sprites, use a plain flat light/dark background instead of the #00FF00 key. The art-director owns style.md: the user signs off on the tag text in the PR.
- `.claude/workflow.yaml`: `art:` block with `backend` (default stays `openrouter`) and `comfy: {url, workflow: art/comfy/sprite.json, variations}`.
- Agent docs (`~/.claude/agents/concept-artist.md`, `asset-producer.md`, `art-director.md`, direct edit with backups like the sibling task):
  - **concept-artist.** When `art.backend` is comfy: build the prompt from the SDXL preamble, pass the negative block, and pass `--control-size` from the brief's asset contract. Comfy-specific error hints (service down / missing model / out of memory).
  - **asset-producer.** Copy the round's negative, seeds and workflow file into provenance. Use `process --bg flood` for comfy outputs.
  - **art-director.** Can offer to switch the backend.

## Out of scope
Changing artgen code. Background-only graphs (`background.json`) can come later.

## Notes for the coder
- **Repo side.** One breakout PR: art/comfy/*, art/style.md, .claude/workflow.yaml. The agent docs are outside the repo; record the diff in a beads comment. Start from `~/Projects/ComfyUI/user/artgen-smoke.py` and the ControlNet node wiring from the sibling task's tests.
- **Check before handing to test.** Run artgen on the live service for a 160x60 brick and a paddle with `--control-size`, and attach the contact sheet.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] art/comfy/sprite.json loads in the ComfyUI UI without missing-node errors and shows nodes titled artgen:prompt, negative, seed, size, control, output
- [ ] `artgen comfy-info --workflow art/comfy/sprite.json` lists all six slots
- [ ] `artgen gen --backend comfy --workflow art/comfy/sprite.json --control-size 160x60` with the style.md SDXL tags produces brick-shaped outlined images on a plain background (contact sheet attached to the issue)
- [ ] The same run with `--control-size` for the paddle contract produces a paddle-shaped object, not a character
- [ ] art/style.md has a '## Prompt preamble (SDXL)' section with positive and negative fenced blocks (no hex codes), and the user approved the tag text on the PR
- [ ] art/comfy/README.md explains Export (API) and the required slot titles; .claude/workflow.yaml has art.backend (default openrouter) and art.comfy.{url,workflow,variations}
- [ ] With art.backend set to comfy, a concept-artist dry run on a test issue picks the SDXL preamble, passes --negative and --control-size, and produces a round; agent doc diffs are recorded in a beads comment

title: artgen: --ref for comfy via an artgen:ref slot, unload models after each round, leaner ComfyUI service
description:
## Problem / goal
Two things in artgen and the ComfyUI service are needed before the new graphs (sim-4ws.4):
- **Image references:** ref_style.json needs `--ref` to work with the comfy backend, but sim-4ws.1 rejects it.
- **Memory:** ComfyUI keeps SDXL in RAM after a round (~9.4 GB idle seen 2026-10-03). Alongside trunk/wasm-bindgen builds (~10 GB) and the agent team, the 31 GB machine ran out of memory.

## Behaviour
- **`artgen:ref` slot:** a LoadImage node titled `artgen:ref` takes `--ref <png>`. The image is uploaded via POST /upload/image like `artgen:control`. With comfy, `--ref` is allowed only when the graph has that slot; otherwise the error names the slot. Only one `--ref` is allowed for comfy. The used ref is copied to `round-N/ref.png` and recorded in meta.json.
- **Unload after each round:** when a comfy round finishes (success or failure), artgen POSTs `/free` with `{"unload_models": true, "free_memory": true}`. `--keep-loaded` skips that for quick iteration. A failed /free is only a warning.
- **Service:** `~/.config/systemd/user/comfyui.service` ExecStart gets `--disable-pinned-memory`. Back up the unit first, then daemon-reload and restart.
- SKILL.md documents `artgen:ref`, `--keep-loaded` and the memory behaviour.

## Out of scope
The graph files (sim-4ws.4), and IP-Adapter models/nodes (sim-4ws.4).

## Notes for the coder
Same no-PR flow as sim-4ws.1: edit in place with `.bak-sim-4ws.3` backups for artgen.py, SKILL.md and the unit file, and hand off via beads comments (see the [spec] comment on sim-4ws.1). Extend the fake-ComfyUI unit tests for /free and the ref upload.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests (fake server): --ref with a graph that has artgen:ref uploads the image and fills the slot; without the slot it errors naming artgen:ref; two --ref values with comfy are rejected
- [ ] Unit tests: /free is called once after a round (also after a failed round); --keep-loaded skips it; a failing /free only warns
- [ ] Live: after a comfy round, the ComfyUI process RSS drops back to roughly its idle size (< 2 GB), measured with ps before and after
- [ ] systemctl --user cat comfyui shows --disable-pinned-memory; the service is active and a round still succeeds
- [ ] SKILL.md documents artgen:ref, --keep-loaded and the unload behaviour; the .bak files exist

title: ComfyUI graphs: transparent sprites (BiRefNet), seamless tiles, style reference (IP-Adapter)
description:
## Problem / goal
More starter graphs beside `art/comfy/sprite.json`, aimed at Gemini's weak spots: transparent sprites (no keying), seamless tiling backgrounds, and keeping a picked sprite's look across variants.

## Behaviour
- **`art/comfy/transparent.json`:** the sprite.json pipeline (SDXL, boldline LoRA, ControlNet silhouette) on a plain background → ComfyUI's **built-in** background removal (`LoadBackgroundRemovalModel` with BiRefNet → `RemoveBackground` → `JoinImageWithAlpha`) → RGBA SaveImage. **No custom nodes.**
- **`art/comfy/tile_bg.json`:** seamless tiling background or parallax layer using a seamless/circular-padding custom node. No ControlNet. Size slot for wide layers.
- **`art/comfy/ref_style.json`:** IP-Adapter (SDXL) style reference from the `artgen:ref` slot (sim-4ws.3), plus the ControlNet silhouette so the shape still follows the asset contract.
- **Installs:**
  - Custom nodes are installed via ComfyUI-Manager: one seamless-tiling pack and the IP-Adapter pack.
  - Models: BiRefNet weights in `models/background_removal/`, and IP-Adapter SDXL plus its CLIP-vision encoder.
  - Every node pack and model is recorded in `~/Projects/ComfyUI/models/MODELS.md` (name, URL, version/commit, sha256, licence).
- `art/comfy/README.md` describes each graph, its slots and when to use it.

## Out of scope
The Gemini comparison (sim-4ws.5), LayerDiffuse, and LoRA training.

## Notes for the coder
- **Repo side** (graphs, README) goes in one breakout PR. **ComfyUI side** (nodes, models, MODELS.md) is outside git; record it in a beads comment.
- **BiRefNet:** ComfyUI 0.38 supports it natively (`comfy/bg_removal_model.py`, config `comfy/background_removal/birefnet.json`). Find the checkpoint format its loader expects (a Comfy-Org repackaged file on Hugging Face is likely).
- **Custom nodes:** before choosing a pack, check it loads on ComfyUI 0.38 with no import errors in `journalctl --user -u comfyui`. IP-Adapter packs have had maintenance gaps. If none works, post an [escalate] comment rather than vendoring code.
- **RAM:** check that a round with IP-Adapter + ControlNet fits 12 GB VRAM without OOM, and note peak RAM.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] transparent.json: a 160x60-contract round gives RGBA PNGs: corners alpha 0, the sprite opaque, outlines intact (no eaten keyline); artgen verify passes on one
- [ ] tile_bg.json: one output tiled 2x2 shows no visible seam (contact sheet attached)
- [ ] ref_style.json: with --ref <an existing picked brick plate>, 4 variants clearly share its material/style and follow the silhouette (contact sheet attached)
- [ ] All three graphs load in the ComfyUI UI without missing nodes, and artgen comfy-info --workflow lists their artgen:* slots
- [ ] MODELS.md lists every new node pack and model with URL, version/commit, sha256 and licence; journalctl shows no node import errors after restart
- [ ] art/comfy/README.md documents each graph

title: Compare ComfyUI vs Gemini on real art issues and pick a default backend per workflow
description:
## Problem / goal
Decide with evidence where the local ComfyUI pipeline should replace OpenRouter/Gemini. Agreed rule: the default backend switches **per workflow**, and only with the user's approval.

## Behaviour
- **Generate comfy rounds for three real cases**, in a scratch concepts dir (`art/concepts/_comparison/`, not on the real issues):
  1. The **sim-usq.1 titanium brick base** at 160x60 via transparent.json.
  2. **One other brick class** via transparent.json or ref_style.json with the titanium pick as the ref.

Regenerating shipped assets, and changing the issues used as references.

Read-only use of the old rounds. The config change and the concept-artist doc line are part of this task; the doc is an in-place edit with .bak like sim-4ws.2.

title: artgen comfy: fix sim-4ws.1 review nits (unique control upload name, orphan round dir, size-slot warning)
description:
Follow-up to the sim-4ws.1 review nits (see the [review] comment on sim-4ws.1). artgen lives in ~/.claude/skills/art-pipeline/scripts/artgen.py (outside git; edit in place with a .bak-<id> backup, like sim-4ws.1).

1. Unique control upload name. comfy_upload always uploads 'control.png' with overwrite=true. Two comfy rounds with control images running at once (e.g. two issues) can overwrite each other's silhouette before the queued jobs load it. Upload as <issue>-r<N>-control.png (or similar) instead.
2. Orphan round dir. If the control upload fails, cmd_gen dies after out.mkdir(), leaving round-N with only control.png, so the next run numbers its round N+1. Upload before the mkdir (from a temp file), or remove the dir on failure.
3. Size-slot warning. --control-size on a graph with no artgen:size draws the control at the SDXL bucket while the latent stays at the graph's own size, so the aspect ratios can differ. Print a warning to stderr (don't fail).

Filed by the reviewer at the user's request (P4).

- [ ] Two rounds for different issues upload distinct control image names; a unit test (fake ComfyUI) checks the uploaded filename includes the issue and round
- [ ] A failed control upload leaves no round-N directory behind; unit test
- [ ] --control-size against a graph without artgen:size prints a warning naming artgen:size and still runs
- [ ] All existing test_artgen.py tests still pass

title: Rename art-web to game-asset-web with visual/ and audio/ sections, started by agent-team
description:
## Problem / goal
Art review runs through "art-web": a bare `python3 -m http.server 9090` over `art/concepts`, which someone has to start by hand in a tmux window. The sound pipeline (sim-by3) will need listening the same way. The user wants one **game-asset-web** with art under `visual/` and audio under `audio/`. It's the first step toward a browsable library of every game's assets (later).

## Behaviour
- **Server:** `~/.claude/skills/art-pipeline/scripts/asset_web.py`, stdlib only, bound to **127.0.0.1:9090** (same port).
  - `/` is an index page linking **Visual** and **Audio**.
  - `/visual/…` serves `<main>/art/concepts/` (the existing contact sheets, unchanged).
  - `/audio/…` serves `<main>/audio/concepts/`, created if missing. Empty for now.
  - Each section lists its issue folders newest first.
  - `.wav`, `.ogg`, `.mp3` and `.flac` are served with the correct audio MIME types, so `<audio>` players work later.
- **Old links keep working:** `http://localhost:9090/<ID>/…` redirects (302) to `/visual/<ID>/…` when that exists. Beads comments are full of the old links.
- **Started by agent-team:** `agent-team up art` starts a `game-asset-web` tmux window running the server. It isn't started twice; if port 9090 is taken, it's a clear message. `agent-team down art` stops it.
- **Docs:** art-pipeline SKILL.md and `~/.claude/agents/art-director.md` give contact-sheet links as `http://localhost:9090/visual/<ID>/` and name the window `game-asset-web`. The `art-web` name is gone from the docs.
- **Repo:** `/audio/concepts` is git-ignored, like `/art/concepts`.

## Out of scope
The sound pipeline itself (sim-by3), audio contact sheets with players (come with sim-by3), and moving files on disk.

The **cross-game asset library** is also out of scope: browsing across games, search/tags and per-asset provenance (user's long-term direction, see sim-by3). Keep the server's section→folder mapping in one table so more roots or games can be added later.

## Notes for the coder
- **Split handoff:**
  - `asset_web.py` + tests, SKILL.md, art-director.md and `~/.local/bin/agent-team` are outside git. Edit them in place with `.bak-<id>` backups (no-PR flow, see the [spec] comment on sim-4ws.1).
  - The `.gitignore` line goes in a small breakout PR.
- **Today's state:** an `art-web` window (started by the pm on 2026-10-04) runs `python3 -m http.server 9090 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory <main>/art/concepts` in session `team-breakout`. Replace it.
- agent-team already exports `MAIN`/`BEADS_DIR`. Resolve `<main>` the same way, and avoid hard-coding breakout inside asset_web.py: take the roots as arguments.
- **Tests:** stdlib unittest next to `test_artgen.py`. Start the server on port 0 against temp dirs and check the index, `/visual/` and `/audio/` listings, the legacy redirect, audio MIME types, and that paths can't escape their root (`..`).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `agent-team up art` starts a `game-asset-web` tmux window; running it again doesn't start a second server; `agent-team down art` stops it; with 9090 already taken it prints a clear message
- [ ] http://localhost:9090/ shows an index with Visual and Audio sections; each lists its issue folders newest first
- [ ] http://localhost:9090/visual/sim-usq.5/ shows that contact sheet exactly as before
- [ ] The old-style http://localhost:9090/sim-usq.5/ redirects to /visual/sim-usq.5/
- [ ] /audio/ serves <main>/audio/concepts; a test .ogg/.wav is served with an audio/* MIME type and plays in the browser
- [ ] The server binds 127.0.0.1 only, and `..` paths can't escape a section's folder (unit test)
- [ ] art-pipeline SKILL.md and art-director.md link to /visual/<ID>/ and name the window game-asset-web; .bak files exist; /audio/concepts is git-ignored on master

title: Use Steelbreak ball, emitter paddle and power-up sprites
description:
## Problem / goal
The Steelbreak ball, emitter-paddle and power-up sprites (sim-rdl.5.2, merged in #26) are in `assets/sprites/`, but the game still draws those as shapes (after sim-rdl.4: a circle mesh for the ball and a cyan paddle with shape prongs). Render them with the sprites.

## Behaviour
- The ball renders with `ball.png` at 15×15, round, with its steel shading visible.
- The paddle renders as 3 pieces: left prong, stretched field, right prong. Prongs keep a fixed 27 px width; the field fills the gap. It looks seamless at the normal 120 px width and at Super-Sizer's 150 px width, and resizes instantly on pickup and expiry.
- Falling power-ups render with `powerup.png` at 24×24 (one icon for all kinds for now).
- **No gameplay change:** the paddle collider stays one full-width rectangle, and ball and power-up colliders are unchanged. Mouse and keyboard control (sim-rdl.2) behave the same.
- **Missing files:** if a sprite is missing, that object falls back to its sim-rdl.4 shape/colour without panicking.

## Out of scope
A per-kind power-up icon, ball state variants (heated/charged), paddle hit glow/animation, trail effects.

## Notes for the coder
- Handles live in `GameSprites` (sim-rdl.6). Colours and fallbacks stay in `src/theme.rs` (sim-rdl.4).
- Paddle: keep physics on the parent `Paddle` entity; replace sim-rdl.4's shape children with 3 sprite children (markers for prong/field). `super_sizer.rs::update_paddle_width` repositions the prongs (`±(width/2 − 13.5)`) and resizes the field (`width − 54`). The asset-producer's draft below has a worked snippet.
- Ball: replace the `Mesh2d` circle from sim-rdl.4 with a `Sprite`; the collider stays `Collider::circle`.
- Headless tests: keep the width/offset maths in a pure function and unit-test it at 120 and 150.

---
## Asset-producer handoff (original draft, for reference)
## Assets (from PR art/sim-rdl.5.2-ball-paddle-powerup, merges to `assets/sprites/`)

- `assets/sprites/ball.png` — RGBA, 60x60 (4x of the 15px `BALL_SIZE` collider).
- `assets/sprites/paddle_prong_left.png` / `paddle_prong_right.png` — RGBA,
  54x40 each (2x scale; 40 = 2x `PADDLE_HEIGHT`, so each prong is 27 game px
  wide). `paddle_prong_right.png` is an exact horizontal mirror of the left
  (same asset, flipped) — no need to `flip_x` it again at render time.
- `assets/sprites/paddle_field.png` — RGBA, 93x40, **fully opaque by
  design** (it's the pure bright core of the glow, not a silhouette sprite —
  don't expect/require transparency on it). Meant to be stretched
  (`custom_size`) to fill whatever gap is left between the two prongs; it's
  a flat/near-flat fill so any stretch width looks fine, no tiling needed.
- `assets/sprites/powerup.png` — RGBA, 48x48 (2x of the 24px `POWER_UP_SIZE`).

## What this replaces

`ball.png` and `powerup.png` are simple: swap the existing flat-colour
sprites for these textures with a matching `custom_size`.

```rust
// main.rs spawn_run_entities, ball:
Sprite::from_color(WHITE, Vec2::splat(BALL_SIZE)),
// ->
Sprite { image: asset_server.load("sprites/ball.png"), custom_size: Some(Vec2::splat(BALL_SIZE)), ..default() },
```

```rust
// powerups/mod.rs drop_power_up, power-up icon:
Sprite::from_color(power_up_brick.color, Vec2::splat(POWER_UP_SIZE)),
// ->
Sprite { image: asset_server.load("sprites/powerup.png"), custom_size: Some(Vec2::splat(POWER_UP_SIZE)), ..default() },
```

**The paddle is a bigger structural change**, not a texture swap. Today it's
a single entity with one `Sprite::from_color` + one `Collider`, and
`super_sizer.rs::update_paddle_width` resizes that single sprite/collider
directly:

```rust
// main.rs spawn_run_entities, paddle:
Sprite::from_color(RED, Vec2::new(PADDLE_WIDTH, PADDLE_HEIGHT)),
...
Collider::rectangle(PADDLE_WIDTH, PADDLE_HEIGHT),
...
Paddle { width: PADDLE_WIDTH },

// super_sizer.rs update_paddle_width:
sprite.custom_size = Some(Vec2::new(width, PADDLE_HEIGHT));
*collider = Collider::rectangle(width, PADDLE_HEIGHT);
```

The brief calls for 3 visual parts (left prong, right prong, stretchable
field) with **no solid surface between them** — i.e. the paddle's physics
collider should very likely stay a single full-width rectangle (gameplay
shouldn't change — the ball still bounces off the whole paddle span), but
the *visual* needs to become 3 sprites that reposition/resize together as
`Paddle.width` changes (today only on Super-Sizer pickup, 1.25x).

Suggested approach: keep the `Paddle` entity's `RigidBody`/`Collider`/physics
exactly as today (no gameplay change), drop its own visible `Sprite`, and
spawn 3 child entities under it (`Transform` relative to the parent, so they
move with it automatically):

```rust
const PRONG_WIDTH: f32 = 27.0; // 54px asset / 2x

fn spawn_paddle_visuals(parent: &mut ChildSpawnerCommands, asset_server: &AssetServer, width: f32) {
    let field_width = width - 2.0 * PRONG_WIDTH;
    parent.spawn((
        Sprite { image: asset_server.load("sprites/paddle_prong_left.png"), custom_size: Some(Vec2::new(PRONG_WIDTH, PADDLE_HEIGHT)), ..default() },
        Transform::from_xyz(-(width / 2.0 - PRONG_WIDTH / 2.0), 0.0, 0.0),
        PaddleProng, // marker so update_paddle_width can find/reposition it
    ));
    parent.spawn((
        Sprite { image: asset_server.load("sprites/paddle_field.png"), custom_size: Some(Vec2::new(field_width, PADDLE_HEIGHT)), ..default() },
        Transform::default(),
        PaddleField,
    ));
    parent.spawn((
        Sprite { image: asset_server.load("sprites/paddle_prong_right.png"), custom_size: Some(Vec2::new(PRONG_WIDTH, PADDLE_HEIGHT)), ..default() },
        Transform::from_xyz(width / 2.0 - PRONG_WIDTH / 2.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        PaddleProng,
    ));
}
```

`update_paddle_width` (in `super_sizer.rs`) needs to additionally reposition
the left/right prong children (`Transform.translation.x = ±(width/2 -
PRONG_WIDTH/2)`) and resize the field child's `custom_size.x = width -
2*PRONG_WIDTH`, alongside its existing `Collider::rectangle(width,
PADDLE_HEIGHT)` update on the parent. Exact component/marker names are
implementation choice — this is the shape of the change, not a spec to
follow literally.

## Composed-size sanity check (already done during production)

Composited `paddle_prong_left + paddle_field (stretched) + paddle_prong_right`
at both 240x40 (`PADDLE_WIDTH*2` default) and 300x40 (1.25x Super-Sizer
width) — both look correct, no seams, prongs stay fixed-width while only the
field stretches. So `field_width = width - 2*PRONG_WIDTH` at both 120 and 150
game-px paddle widths is the right formula.

## Manifest / provenance

See `art/manifest.toml` (`id = "ball-paddle-powerup"`) and
`art/prompts/sim-rdl.5.2-r{1,2,3}.txt` for the source prompts if
regeneration is ever needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] In a run, the ball shows the steel sphere sprite, the paddle shows two prongs with a glowing field between them, and falling power-ups show the power-up icon.
- [ ] Catching a Super-Sizer power-up widens the paddle with no gap or overlap between the prongs and the field, and it returns cleanly when the effect expires.
- [x] The ball still bounces off the full paddle width, including the edge-angle spin; mouse and keyboard paddle control are unchanged.
- [x] Renaming `assets/sprites/ball.png` makes the ball fall back to its shape rendering without a panic.
- [ ] The web build (`trunk serve`) shows the sprites.
- [x] `cargo test` includes unit tests for the paddle piece layout at widths 120 and 150; clippy and `trunk build` pass.

title: Playfield frame: 1920x1080 scaled world, framed side panels, centred grid with guaranteed side channels
description:
## Problem / goal
The brick grid isn't centred (40 px gap on the left, 15 px on the right, and the ball is 15 px), so the ball can't reliably get up the right side and over the bricks. That matters more now that shield glass only breaks from above. The game also runs in a small fixed 900×650 window with no frame. Goal: a 1920×1080 game world that scales to any window or browser, a centred playfield well framed by wall panels, and a brick grid that always leaves a side channel the ball can pass through.

## Decisions (user interview, 2026-09-29)
- **Resolution:** a 1920×1080 logical world, scaled to fit the window or browser with letterboxing. Gameplay sizes and speeds scale ×1.5 so the feel doesn't change.
- **Layout:** a playfield well about 1440×1080 in the centre, with a ~240 px frame panel on each side. The HUD (score, lives, later the sector) goes in the left panel. The right panel is reserved for the power-up time capsules (sim-rdl.8).
- **Side channels:** at least 3 ball widths on both sides, equal, and enforced for every board, including future level files. It's one named const, so it's easy to tweak.
- **Wall art:** coded placeholder frame now, with a sprite hook that falls back to shapes. A separate art brief covers the painted Steelbreak truss frame.

## Children
1. Core: world size, scaling, playfield well, derived centred grid, HUD into the left panel.
2. Frame panels: placeholder wall art and the sprite hook (after 1).
3. Art brief: painted frame panels (art team; independent, the game falls back to 2's shapes).

title: Scale to a 1920x1080 world with a centred playfield well and a centred, channel-guaranteed brick grid
description:
## Problem / goal
Move the game to a 1920×1080 logical world that scales to any window or browser. Walls sit at the edges of a centred playfield well, and the brick grid is centred and derived from a tweakable side-channel const, so the ball always has a lane up both sides. Part of epic sim-73n.

## Behaviour
- **World and scaling.** The camera shows a fixed 1920×1080 world, scaled uniformly to fit the window with letterbox or pillarbox bars (`theme::VOID`) in the spare space. Resizing the native window or the browser rescales it live; nothing is cropped or stretched. The native window opens at 1280×720 and is resizable. On web the canvas fills the browser viewport.
- **Playfield well.** The playfield is a centred region `PLAYFIELD_WIDTH` × 1080 (about 1440 wide, leaving a ~240 px side panel each side). The physics walls (left, right, top) sit on the well's edges, not the screen edges. The ball is lost below the bottom edge as today. The paddle is clamped inside the well.
- **Scale ×1.5.** Ball, paddle (incl. prongs), bricks and their gaps, ball speed, paddle force/drive, the HUD font and the power-up drop size and fall speed all scale ×1.5 from today's values. The game should look and play the same, just bigger. The existing background sprite covers the well.
- **Centred grid with guaranteed channels.** A single const, e.g. `SIDE_CHANNEL_BALLS: f32 = 3.0` (the minimum clear gap between the outermost brick and each wall, in ball widths), drives the layout. Brick width is *derived*: `(PLAYFIELD_WIDTH − 2·channel − (cols−1)·gap) / cols`. Raising the const shrinks the bricks and needs no other code change. The grid is horizontally centred, so the left and right channels are equal. A board with fewer columns (future level files, sim-a7k.1) stays centred and only gets wider channels.
- **HUD in the left panel.** SCORE and LIVES move into the left side panel, outside the playfield well. Nothing overlaps the bricks.
- **Menus scale.** The menu, settings, pause and game-over UI scale with the window (e.g. `UiScale` from window height ÷ 1080), so they look the same at 1280×720 and at 1920×1080.
- **Mouse control still works** under letterboxing. The paddle follows the cursor's world X (already goes through `viewport_to_world_2d`).

## Out of scope
- Frame/wall art in the side panels (sibling task; this task leaves them as plain clear colour).
- Sector label / time-capsule gauges (sim-a7k.2, sim-rdl.8). They will later go in the panels.
- New sprite art or re-exporting sprites at higher resolution (sprites are drawn with `custom_size`, so they just scale).
- Parallax background (sim-rdl.9).

## Notes for the coder
- Constants live in `src/main.rs` (`WINDOW_WIDTH/HEIGHT`, `WALL_THICKNESS`, `PADDLE_*`, `BALL_*`, `BRICK_*`). Replace the window-sized consts with world/playfield consts (e.g. `WORLD_WIDTH/HEIGHT`, `PLAYFIELD_WIDTH/HEIGHT`). The window resolution is now separate from the world size.
- Today's brick x is `col * (BRICK_WIDTH + 5) + 40 + BRICK_WIDTH/2 − WINDOW_WIDTH/2`. The fixed 40 px offset is the asymmetry bug. Replace it with the centred, derived layout; keep it a pure fn so it's unit-testable.
- Camera: Bevy 0.19 `Projection::Orthographic` with a `ScalingMode` that fits 1920×1080 (e.g. `AutoMin`/`Fixed`) plus a viewport or clear colour for the bars. Check `index.html` CSS so the canvas fills the viewport on web (and Bevy's `fit_canvas_to_parent`).
- `src/sprites.rs` sizes the background to `WINDOW_WIDTH × WINDOW_HEIGHT`. Change it to the well size (tests assert this).
- `controls.rs` `clamp_paddle_x` must use the playfield width. The `BALL_MIN_VERTICAL_FRACTION` anti-stuck clamp is unit-free.
- Paddle feel: accel = force / mass, so scale `PADDLE_FORCE` ×1.5 (or mass ÷1.5). Check that `follow_velocity`'s cap still behaves.
- Many tests use these consts. Keep them const-driven rather than hard-coding new numbers.
- Conflict risk: sim-a7k.1 (level files) also touches brick placement. Land this first.

title: Frame the playfield: coded steel side panels with frame_left/right sprite hook
description:
## Problem / goal
Frame the playfield with walls. The side panels from sim-73n.1 should read as a steel frame (the "artificial walls" around the play area), drawn from theme colours now and swapped for painted art when it lands. Part of epic sim-73n.

## Behaviour
- The left and right side panels are drawn as a Steelbreak steel frame: a panel fill plus a girder or truss edge along the playfield side. The inner edge visibly lines up with the physics wall the ball bounces off.
- The colours come from new `theme::` constants (e.g. `FRAME_PANEL`, `FRAME_GIRDER`), and no colour literals are used.
- Sprite hook: `GameSprites` gains `frame_left` and `frame_right` (`assets/sprites/frame_left.png`, `frame_right.png`), and a skin rule swaps the placeholder shapes for them once loaded (`Skinned`). If a file is missing or broken, the coded frame stays (no panic, nothing invisible), like every other sprite. The right panel may reuse the left image mirrored if only one file exists. This is optional; choose what's simplest.
- The HUD text in the left panel stays readable on top of the frame (the frame is drawn behind the HUD).
- The frame is global, like the walls. It shows in menus as well as in play, and doesn't despawn between runs.

## Out of scope
- The painted frame art itself (art brief sim-73n.3).
- Parallax (sim-rdl.9) and the time-capsule gauges (sim-rdl.8).

## Notes for the coder
- Follow the `src/sprites.rs` pattern: spawn the shape first, then `SkinPlugin` swaps it. `SpritesPlugin` isn't in the headless test app, so test the fallback shape path in `cargo test`.
- Panel geometry comes from the world and playfield consts introduced in sim-73n.1. Don't hard-code 240.
- Keep the frame on a z between the background (−10) and gameplay.

title: Art: painted Steelbreak frame side panels (240x1080 walls)
description:
## Subject
Painted Steelbreak frame panel: the "artificial wall" beside the playfield well. One painting is used for the left panel, and a horizontally mirrored copy is used for the right.

## Use in game
Two static panels, left and right of the playfield. Each covers 240×1080 world units in the 1920×1080 world (sim-73n). The files are painted and shipped at 2× (480×2160), and the game scales them to 240×1080.
- **Playfield edge:** the long edge that faces the playfield (the right edge of the left panel) is a steel girder or wall face. The ball bounces off this line, so it must be straight, vertical and flush with the image edge.
- **Readout channel:** a dark recessed channel runs the full height of the panel, between the outer trusses and the girder edge. The HUD (SCORE, LIVES, later SECTOR) goes in it on the left panel, and the power-up time-capsule gauges (sim-rdl.8) go in it on the right. It must be calm and low-contrast along its whole length so text and gauges can sit anywhere and grow later.
- **Background role:** the panels must read as frame and background. Nothing in them may look like a gameplay object (no ball-like circles, brick-like blocks or glowing pickups).

## Variants
One painting. `frame_right.png` is `frame_left.png` flipped horizontally, with no separate painting. Concept rounds explore the left panel only.

## Frames
None (static).

## References
`art/steelbreak_keyart.png` and `art/steelbreak_concept.png` (trusses, girders, hangar steel), the `art/style.md` steel palette, and the coded placeholder frame from sim-73n.2 (panel fill with a girder edge).

title: Move the brick grid down one brick height for headroom above the bricks
description:
## Problem / goal
There's too little room above the brick grid, so a ball that gets up a side channel has almost no space to travel across the top of the bricks. Move the whole brick layout down by one brick height to give it more headroom. Part of the playfield epic sim-73n.

## Behaviour
- Every brick row sits exactly one `BRICK_HEIGHT` (45 world px) lower than today.
- Horizontal layout, row spacing and side channels are unchanged.
- The gap between the top wall and the top of row 0 grows from 75 to 120 world px.
- Anything placed through the shared grid layout (future level grids from sim-a7k) moves with it.

## Out of scope
Changing brick size, row count, column layout or side channels. Ball speed (sim-a7k ramp task).

## Notes for the coder
- `src/bricks/grid.rs`: `BRICK_TOP_MARGIN = 50.0 * GAME_SCALE` feeds `brick_y(row)`. Make the headroom explicit, e.g. `BRICK_TOP_MARGIN = 50.0 * GAME_SCALE + BRICK_HEIGHT`, or a named `BRICK_HEADROOM` const, so it's one obvious knob.
- Check the existing test that keeps ≥ 250 px between the lowest brick and the paddle top. It should still pass (the playfield is 1080 tall); don't weaken it.
- Update the `//!` doc in `grid.rs` if it states the margin.

title: Art pipeline: ComfyUI style fidelity (graffiti LoRA, ref default, prompt tuning, img2img)
description:
## Problem / goal
The sim-4ws.5 comparison showed ComfyUI doesn't hold the graffiti look as well as Gemini picks unless it's given a shipped reference. Recommendations from that comparison (user approved filing all four, 2026-10-04), in order of payoff:
1. Train a small graffiti LoRA, the biggest lever.
2. Use ref_style for most sprites with a shipped reference.
3. Tune prompts and graphs: hangar and palette tags leak into sprites, cfg too high, try a stronger SDXL finetune.
4. img2img from Gemini picks for variants and recolours.

## Order
.1 tuning → .2 ref default → .3 img2img → .4 LoRA. The LoRA is A/B'd against the tuned ref_style setup. All tasks wait for sim-4ws.5 (per-workflow backend defaults).

## Constraints
- **Future home:** tooling (trainer setup, graphs, artgen slots) must stay game-agnostic. It moves to the future game-dev-tooling repo. The trained LoRA and its dataset belong to breakout.
- **Memory:** 31 GB RAM / 12 GB VRAM, shared with ComfyUI, cargo/trunk builds and the agent team.

title: Tune the SDXL sprite prompt and ComfyUI graphs (tag leaks, cfg, finetune checkpoint)
description:
## Problem / goal
In the sim-4ws.5 comparison, the hangar/palette tags in the SDXL preamble leaked into sprites, and cfg was high. A stronger SDXL finetune than the base checkpoint may hold line-art better.

## Behaviour
- **`art/style.md` SDXL section:**
  - A **sprite** positive block without scene, hangar and lighting-environment tags ("dark hangar palette", key/bounce light phrasing, etc.).
  - The full preamble stays for backgrounds.
  - The negative block gets whatever leaked (e.g. hangar, interior, room, environment).
  - The user approves the tag text on the PR.
- **Graphs:** lower cfg in sprite.json, transparent.json and ref_style.json, chosen from a cfg sweep (e.g. 4.0 / 5.0 / 6.5) on one sprite contract. The chosen value is written into the graphs.
- **Finetune:** download 2–3 candidate SDXL finetunes with a usable licence (flat/illustration/line-art strengths). A/B each against base on the same seeds and prompts. Keep only the winner (or base) and record it in MODELS.md. The graphs use the winner.

## Out of scope
LoRA training (sibling task) and new graphs.

## Notes for the coder
- **Handoff:** style.md and the graph files go through a breakout PR. Checkpoint downloads and MODELS.md are outside git; list them in a [handoff] comment.
- **Disk/RAM:** each SDXL checkpoint is ~7 GB. Delete the losing candidates.
- **Evidence:** contact sheets on game-asset-web (/visual/<id>/).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] style.md has a separate SDXL sprite block with no hangar/scene/lighting-environment tags; the background preamble is unchanged; the user approved the text on the PR
- [x] A cfg sweep contact sheet (same seed/prompt, ≥3 cfg values) is attached, and the chosen cfg is in sprite/transparent/ref_style.json
- [x] A finetune A/B contact sheet (base vs 2–3 candidates, same seeds) is shown to the user; the user's pick is recorded in a comment and is the checkpoint the graphs load
- [x] MODELS.md lists the kept checkpoint (URL, sha256, licence); rejected candidates are deleted from models/checkpoints
- [x] A brick sprite round with the new settings shows no hangar/room background elements (contact sheet)

comments.text:
[spec] pm: reference from the user (2026-10-04), Animagine XL 4.0 prompting guide: https://cagliostrolab.net/posts/optimizing-animagine-xl-40-in-depth-guideline-and-update (and the HF card cagliostrolab/animagine-xl-4.0-zero).
- **Variants:** **Opt**, "crisper line art and more solid background", is for generating, so it's a finetune candidate for sim-7bu.1. **Zero** is the plain pretrained base, recommended for LoRA training and finetuning, so it's a base candidate for sim-7bu.4.
- **Prompt (Danbooru tags, order matters):** subject/count tags → (character, series) → artist tags (after series, never at the end) → general descriptive tags → rating tag (`safe`) mid-prompt → quality tags LAST: `masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres`. Quality tags at the start don't trigger. Optional temporal tags `year 2005`…`year 2025`. For our objects use `no humans`, `simple background`, plus object tags. No hex codes.
- **Negative (from the HF card):** `lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, text, error, missing finger, extra digits, fewer digits, cropped, worst quality, low quality, low score, bad score, average score, signature, watermark, username, blurry`
- **Settings:** Euler a (euler_ancestral), CFG 4–7 (5 recommended), 25–28 steps (28 recommended). SDXL buckets: 1024², 1152×896, 1216×832, 1344×768, 1536×640 and the portrait equivalents.
- ⚠️ **Licence conflict:** the blog says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike); the HF model card says CreativeML Open RAIL++-M. Settle this with the user (and record it in MODELS.md) BEFORE adopting it as a default checkpoint, or before training the graffiti LoRA on Zero.
- **Fit risk:** it's an anime/character model. Test it on objects (brick plate, paddle, frame) in the sim-7bu.1 A/B; it isn't automatically better for this game's sprites.

For .1: include **Animagine XL 4.0 Opt** as one finetune candidate in the A/B, with a separate Danbooru-ordered prompt variant using the settings above (it needs its own tag order, so don't reuse the base SDXL preamble unchanged).

comments.author: pm
comments.text:
[spec] pm: second finetune candidate the coder is trying, per the user (2026-10-04): **ProteusV0.4** (https://huggingface.co/dataautogpt3/ProteusV0.4).
- **What it is:** an SDXL base fine-tune, more general than Animagine (stock + anime data, DPO-tuned). The card says it's strong at faces/skin and handles surreal, anime and cartoon styles. Line-art objects are untested, so the A/B decides.
- **Settings from the card:** DPM++ 2M SDE + Karras, CFG 4–6, 20–60 steps, 1024² (or 1280²).
- **Prompt:** keepwords `best quality, HD, ~*~aesthetic~*~`. It takes our existing SDXL comma-tag preamble without a reorder (unlike Animagine).
- **Negative from the card:** `nsfw, bad quality, bad anatomy, worst quality, low quality, low resolutions, extra fingers, blur, blurry, ugly, wrongs proportions, watermark, image artifacts, lowres, jpeg artifacts, deformed, noisy image`. Merge in our own negative block (no spray, no text, etc.).
- **Licence: GPL-3.0** on the weights. That's unusual for a model. Generated images aren't normally treated as GPL-covered, but a LoRA trained on it (sim-7bu.4) and redistributed would plausibly be GPL. Record it in MODELS.md and tell the user when the A/B is presented.
A/B set for .1 is now: SDXL base vs Animagine XL 4.0 Opt vs ProteusV0.4, same seeds and contracts, each with its own recommended sampler/CFG (also show one run at a shared setting so the comparison is fair).

comments.author: pm
comments.text:
[spec] pm: prompt shape for SDXL, from the user's hands-on ComfyUI test (2026-10-05). **The prose prompts in the pipeline aren't suitable for SDXL; use comma tags.**
- **Why prose fails:** CLIP reads 77 tokens per chunk, and ComfyUI blends the chunks, so long prompts get diluted. Tags at the front of a chunk count the most.
- **Negation backfires:** CLIP doesn't understand "no X", so "no drips, no splatter" ADDS drips and splatter. Everything unwanted goes in the negative prompt only.
- **Shape and colour in the text are ignored:** "aspect ratio 2:9", "portrait" and hex codes do nothing. Size is set by the EmptyLatentImage width/height, using SDXL buckets (the tallest portrait is about 640×1536); crop to extreme ratios like 2:9 afterwards.
- **Explanatory sentences are wasted** ("the graffiti influence is only in the graphic treatment"). CLIP just picks up "graffiti", which pulls toward spray paint.
- **Test case:** the prose prompt in art/prompts/sim-73n.3-r4.txt (station wall panel) vs this tag version, which the user ran with good results:
  positive: `sci-fi station wall panel, retro-futurist, graffiti line-art style, dark navy steel, rounded capsule panels, portholes, sleek pods, bold clean outlines, thick-thin contour lines, offset double outline, flowing curved linework inlaid in metal, crisp edge highlights, muted teal-grey, faded orange, off-white accents, flat colour blocking, hard-surface, clean vector style, vertical composition`
  negative: `spray paint, drips, splatter, overspray, airbrush, soft gradient, paint texture, graffiti tags, lettering, text, watermark, blurry, noisy`
  latent 640×1536.

title: Concept-artist uses ref_style with a shipped reference by default for sprites
description:
## Problem / goal
ref_style.json with a shipped asset as the reference held the graffiti look best in the sim-4ws.5 comparison. Make it the default for sprite concept rounds on the comfy backend.

## Behaviour
- **Picking the reference:** when the brief is a sprite and the comfy backend applies, the concept-artist uses `art/comfy/ref_style.json` and passes `--ref`. The reference is chosen in this order:
  1. A shipped asset of the same family (e.g. another brick plate for a brick, the paddle for paddle parts), using its original full-size concept pick from `art/concepts/<issue>/round-N/vK.png` when available.
  2. Otherwise the shipped PNG itself.
  3. Otherwise the brief's own ref.
- **Overrides:** the brief can name the reference explicitly (`ref:` line), and that wins. A brief can opt out (`ref: none`).
- **Provenance:** the chosen reference and why it was chosen go in round-N/meta.json (already recorded as ref) and in the round's prompt.txt header.
- **Config:** `.claude/workflow.yaml` gets a flag `art.comfy.ref_default: true`.

## Out of scope
Backgrounds and tiles (no ref default) and img2img (sibling task).

## Notes for the coder
- **Handoff:** the concept-artist doc and the art-pipeline SKILL.md are edited in place with .bak (no PR); workflow.yaml goes in a breakout PR.
- Map asset families to their source issues with art/manifest.toml (asset → issue → picked round).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With art.backend comfy (or the per-workflow sprite default comfy), a concept-artist dry run on a brick brief uses ref_style.json with a shipped brick concept pick as --ref, and meta.json/prompt.txt name it
- [ ] A brief with an explicit ref: line uses that file; ref: none uses sprite.json without a ref
- [ ] For a family with no full-size pick, the shipped PNG is used (dry run or unit-level check of the selection logic)
- [ ] workflow.yaml has art.comfy.ref_default; setting it false restores the old sprite.json behaviour
- [ ] Doc diffs recorded in a beads comment; .bak files exist

title: img2img graph and artgen denoise slot: variants and recolours from a picked concept
description:
## Problem / goal
Start from an existing pick (Gemini or ComfyUI) and make close variants or recolours, instead of generating from scratch.

## Behaviour
- **`art/comfy/img2img.json`:** LoadImage (`artgen:ref`) → VAEEncode → KSampler with denoise from a new slot **`artgen:denoise`** → VAEDecode → SaveImage.
  - It has the usual prompt/negative/seed slots and the boldline LoRA.
  - The latent size follows the ref's size, snapped to an SDXL bucket.
- **artgen:**
  - **`--denoise <0..1>`** fills `artgen:denoise` (KSampler `denoise` input). Default 0.45 for img2img. It's an error if the graph has no such slot.
  - `comfy-info --workflow` lists the slot.
  - meta.json records denoise.
- **Docs:** SKILL.md documents when to use img2img: variants of a pick (~0.3–0.5), recolours with a colour prompt (~0.4–0.6).

## Out of scope
Inpainting and masks.

## Notes for the coder
- **Handoff:** artgen.py, its tests and SKILL.md are an in-place skill edit with .bak (no PR); img2img.json and the README go in a breakout PR.
- Extend the fake-ComfyUI tests for the new slot.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests: --denoise fills artgen:denoise; out-of-range values and a graph without the slot give clear errors; existing tests pass
- [ ] Live: img2img from an existing pick at denoise 0.3 gives 4 variants that keep its composition and silhouette; at 0.6 they differ more (contact sheet with both)
- [ ] Live: a recolour prompt (e.g. 'violet' on a titanium plate) at ~0.5 keeps the shape and changes the hue
- [ ] comfy-info --workflow art/comfy/img2img.json lists artgen:ref and artgen:denoise; meta.json records denoise
- [ ] README and SKILL.md document img2img and the denoise ranges; .bak files exist

title: Adopt the user-trained graffiti LoRA (stlbrk_graffiti_v1): record, A/B steps/strength/base, wire into graphs
description:
## Problem / goal
The biggest lever for ComfyUI fidelity is a small LoRA trained on the project's own graffiti art.
**The user has trained it** (2026-10-05, outside the queue): `stlbrk_graffiti_v1`. What's left: record
it, A/B it to find the best training step, strength and base, and put the winner in the default
graphs.

What exists:
- **Trainer:** kohya sd-scripts (commit 690ea7f) in `~/Projects/lora/` (`.venv-kohya`, `train.sh`,
`build_dataset.py`, `sample_prompts.txt`, `train.log`, `dataset_sheet.jpg`).
- **Dataset:** 38 graffiti-era concept picks in `~/Projects/lora/dataset/10_stlbrk/`, each a PNG plus
a `.txt` caption. They come from sim-rdl.10, sim-usq.* and other issues. The trigger token is
`stlbrk_graffiti`, and captions are shuffled with keep_tokens=1.
- **Training settings:** SDXL base 1.0 with the sdxl_vae_fp16_fix VAE. Rank 16, alpha 16, 2000 steps
(6 epochs × 10 repeats), AdamW8bit, unet lr 1e-4, TE lr 3e-5, bf16, buckets 512–1536.
- **Weights:** `~/Projects/ComfyUI/models/loras/stlbrk_graffiti_v1-step00001000`, `-step00001500`,
`-step00002000` and `-final` `.safetensors`.
- The user tried it by hand in ComfyUI and liked the output, but hasn't picked a step or strength
yet. The training session's suggested starting point: 1500 steps at 0.8–1.0 on SDXL base with the
trigger in the prompt. Use 1000 if it looks too rigid, 2000 for crisper edges. Add the IP-Adapter
reference (sim-73n.3 r4/v1) for the double-outline look.

## Behaviour
- **Record (committed):** `art/lora/graffiti-v1/` in breakout holds:
  - A dataset manifest (source concept path → caption, for all 38 images).
  - A copy of `train.sh` and the `sample_prompts.txt`.
  - A README with the hyperparameters above, the sd-scripts commit, the run time from `train.log`,
  and how to retrain.
  - No images or weights.
- **MODELS.md** (`~/Projects/ComfyUI/models/MODELS.md`) gets an entry for the kept LoRA file:
  - The path and sha256.
  - That it was trained locally on SDXL base 1.0 from the project's own art (so the licence follows
  SDXL base, Open RAIL++-M).
  - The trigger token.
- **A/B, stage 1 (grid):** same seeds and prompts on the tuned setup from sim-7bu.1.
  - Bases: SDXL base 1.0 (the training base) and the checkpoint .1 picked, if that's a different one.
  - LoRA: none (baseline), and steps 1000 / 1500 / 2000 at strength 0.6 / 0.8 / 1.0.
  - Three subjects: a brick plate, a frame piece, and a sprite not in the dataset (e.g. a new
  capsule).
  - One contact sheet on game-asset-web, every cell labelled with base, step, strength and seed.
- **A/B, stage 2 (extras):** the user's top 1–2 cells from stage 1, each also run:
  - With the IP-Adapter reference (sim-73n.3 r4/v1).
  - Stacked with the existing line-art LoRAs (`sdxl-boldline`, `lineart-style-xl`) vs. without them.
- **Adopt:**
  - The user's pick goes into the default graphs (`art/comfy/sprite.json`, `transparent.json`,
  `ref_style.json`, `tile_bg.json`): which LoRA file, its strength, and whether the old line-art
  LoRAs stay.
  - `stlbrk_graffiti` becomes the first tag of the SDXL preamble in `art/style.md`.
  - The unpicked step files are deleted from models/loras.
- If the user rejects the LoRA, nothing changes except the record and a comment.

## Out of scope
- Retraining or a v2 (a new task).
- Bases that sim-7bu.1 rejected and deleted.
- ControlNet lineart.
- The ref_style default (sim-7bu.2) and img2img (sim-7bu.3); they're no longer blockers.

## Notes for the coder
- **Handoff:** MODELS.md and the deleted step files are outside git, so log them in a [handoff]
comment. `art/lora/` and the graph and style.md changes go in one breakout PR.
- The graphs already chain a LoraLoader. Add the graffiti LoRA as its own LoraLoader node, or replace
the existing one, according to the stage-2 pick. Keep the `artgen:*` slot titles intact.
- **Overfitting check:** the sprite that's not in the dataset must not look like a copy of a
training image. Point this out on the sheet.
- **Memory:** about 4 bases × steps × strengths is roughly 60 images at about 9 s each, so it's
fine. Don't run it while cargo/trunk builds are going (31 GB RAM, shared).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] art/lora/graffiti-v1/ has the 38-image manifest with captions, train.sh, sample_prompts.txt and a README (hyperparameters, sd-scripts commit, run time); no images or weights are committed
- [ ] The stage-1 A/B contact sheet (no LoRA vs steps 1000/1500/2000 × strength 0.6/0.8/1.0, on SDXL base and on .1's pick if different, 3 subjects including one not in the dataset) is on game-asset-web with every cell labelled
- [ ] The stage-2 sheet (the top picks ± IP-Adapter ref, ± the old line-art LoRAs) was shown to the user and their pick is recorded in a beads comment
- [ ] The default comfy graphs load the picked LoRA file at the picked strength, and the SDXL preamble in art/style.md starts with stlbrk_graffiti (PR); or, if the LoRA is rejected, the comment says so and the graphs are unchanged
- [ ] MODELS.md lists the kept LoRA (path, sha256, base, licence, trigger) and the unpicked step files are deleted from models/loras

comments.author: pm
comments.text:
[spec] pm: reference from the user (2026-10-04), Animagine XL 4.0 prompting guide: https://cagliostrolab.net/posts/optimizing-animagine-xl-40-in-depth-guideline-and-update (and the HF card cagliostrolab/animagine-xl-4.0-zero).
- **Variants:** **Opt**, "crisper line art and more solid background", is for generating, so it's a finetune candidate for sim-7bu.1. **Zero** is the plain pretrained base, recommended for LoRA training and finetuning, so it's a base candidate for sim-7bu.4.
- **Prompt (Danbooru tags, order matters):** subject/count tags → (character, series) → artist tags (after series, never at the end) → general descriptive tags → rating tag (`safe`) mid-prompt → quality tags LAST: `masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres`. Quality tags at the start don't trigger. Optional temporal tags `year 2005`…`year 2025`. For our objects use `no humans`, `simple background`, plus object tags. No hex codes.
- **Negative (from the HF card):** `lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, text, error, missing finger, extra digits, fewer digits, cropped, worst quality, low quality, low score, bad score, average score, signature, watermark, username, blurry`
- **Settings:** Euler a (euler_ancestral), CFG 4–7 (5 recommended), 25–28 steps (28 recommended). SDXL buckets: 1024², 1152×896, 1216×832, 1344×768, 1536×640 and the portrait equivalents.
- ⚠️ **Licence conflict:** the blog says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike); the HF model card says CreativeML Open RAIL++-M. Settle this with the user (and record it in MODELS.md) BEFORE adopting it as a default checkpoint, or before training the graffiti LoRA on Zero.
- **Fit risk:** it's an anime/character model. Test it on objects (brick plate, paddle, frame) in the sim-7bu.1 A/B; it isn't automatically better for this game's sprites.

For .4: consider **Animagine XL 4.0 Zero** as the LoRA base, but only if .1's A/B favoured Animagine and the licence is settled. Otherwise train on the checkpoint .1 picked.

title: Re-run the ComfyUI vs Gemini comparison and switch the art pipeline to ComfyUI

because untuned ComfyUI lost on sprite/transparent/tile. After the tuning (sim-7bu.1) and the
user-trained graffiti LoRA (sim-7bu.4), find out whether ComfyUI now holds up. **The user's goal
(2026-10-05) is to run the art pipeline locally on ComfyUI for everything** if it does.

title: Art refinement loop: refine a pick, variants of a pick, refine shipped art (img2img on ComfyUI)
description:
## Problem / goal
The art pipeline can only make new concept rounds; rework means generating from scratch with the
picks passed as `--ref`. The user (2026-10-05) wants a **refinement loop**: take an existing image
and refine it or make variants, spending more steps and CFG on fewer images. This is only worth it
on local ComfyUI, where rounds cost $0. It builds on sim-7bu.3, which provides the img2img graph and
`artgen --denoise`.

## Behaviour
Three ways in, all handled by the art-director and run by the concept-artist on the comfy backend
(even when the workflow's normal backend is OpenRouter):

1. **Refine a pick** (at stage:pick): "refine v3: thicker outlines, less orange". The next round is
img2img from that image plus the user's notes, so it keeps the composition.
2. **Variants of a pick** (at stage:pick): "4 more like v3". img2img at low denoise with new seeds
and no new notes. Meant for brick families, recolours and alternate frames.
3. **Refine shipped art:** "refine assets/…/titanium.png" (or any manifest entry). The art-director
opens a new art issue:
   - Its brief is the original asset's brief and contract (from art/manifest.toml): same size, same
   files.
   - Its source image is the **full-size concept pick** behind the asset when the manifest or
   pick.json points to one, otherwise the shipped PNG upscaled to an SDXL bucket.
   - The brief needs the user's normal approval. It then runs the same concept → pick → produce →
   PR path, and the asset PR replaces the shipped files.

**Settings are asked each time** (the user's choice). For every refine or variants request, the
art-director asks for denoise, steps and CFG, plus the image count (default 4):
- It suggests values: the graph defaults from sim-7bu.1, refine denoise about 0.4–0.6, variants
about 0.25–0.35.
- It says in one line what each knob does.
- It records the answer as `[refine] r<N>/v<k> mode=refine|variants denoise=<d> steps=<s> cfg=<c>
n=<k> — <user's notes verbatim>`, then hands the issue to stage:concept (+rework).

**artgen:**
- **`--steps <int>` and `--cfg <float>`** override the KSampler inputs on the node titled
`artgen:sampler`. It's an error if the graph has none.
- The default graphs (sprite, transparent, ref_style, tile_bg, img2img) get that title.
- meta.json records steps and cfg.

**Concept-artist:**
- For a `[refine]` comment, it runs `art/comfy/img2img.json` with `--ref <that round's vK.png>` and
the comment's denoise, steps, cfg and n.
- The prompt is the SDXL tag preamble + the subject tags + the notes turned into tags. Unwanted
things go in the negative prompt (see the sim-7bu.1 prompt-shape note).
- The round sheet shows the source image next to the results.

**Round limits:**
- Refine and variants rounds don't count toward `art.max_rounds`.
- They have their own `art.max_refine_rounds` (default 10 per issue). Reaching it escalates as
usual.
- Budget is unaffected (comfy costs $0).

## Out of scope
- Inpainting and masks (refining just part of an image).
- Upscaling models.
- A pick/refine UI in game-asset-web; requests go through the art-director conversation.
- Refining with OpenRouter.

## Notes for the coder
- **Handoff:** artgen.py, its tests, SKILL.md and the art agent definitions (art-director,
concept-artist) are in-place skill/agent edits with .bak files and a [handoff] comment (no PR), as
in sim-4ws.1. The graph title changes, workflow.yaml `art.max_refine_rounds` and the art/comfy
README go in a breakout PR.
- New comment tag `[refine]` in the art-pipeline skill's tag list; the asset-producer must ignore
it.
- Extend the fake-ComfyUI tests: --steps/--cfg fill artgen:sampler, missing-slot and out-of-range
errors.
- Write it game-agnostic (no breakout paths hard-coded in artgen); it moves to the game-dev-tooling
repo later.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests: --steps/--cfg fill the artgen:sampler KSampler; a graph without that slot and out-of-range values give clear errors; meta.json records steps/cfg; existing tests pass
- [ ] Live, refine a pick: on an art issue at stage:pick, 'refine vK: <notes>' makes the art-director ask for denoise/steps/cfg/n with suggested values, post a [refine] comment, and the next round is img2img from vK that keeps its composition; the sheet shows source + results
- [ ] Live, variants: 'N more like vK' gives N close variants (same silhouette, small differences) from different seeds
- [ ] Live, shipped art: 'refine <asset>' opens a new art issue whose brief carries the original contract and source image; after the user's pick the asset PR replaces the shipped files and artgen verify passes
- [ ] Refine rounds don't count toward art.max_rounds; art.max_refine_rounds (default 10) is in workflow.yaml and enforced
- [ ] SKILL.md documents the three entry points, the [refine] tag and the denoise/steps/cfg ranges; .bak files exist
