  border.
- `assets/sprites/bricks/outline_shield.png` — cyan metal frame, brightest
  glow bars on the top and bottom edges.

**No `outline_reactor.png`** — dropped from this issue's scope by the user
(revisit later, possibly with a particle-engine approach instead of a
static sprite). The reactor/power-up brick keeps whatever placeholder
outline **sim-rdl.7.4** implements.

## Important: sim-rdl.7.4 doesn't exist in the codebase yet

I checked (`grep -rln "outline\|Outline" src/` → no matches) — as of this
writing sim-rdl.7.4 (the coded placeholder behaviour outlines this issue's
brief says these sprites "replace") is still `stage:ready`, unimplemented.
So there's no existing outline-rendering code path for me to point you at.

This means one of two things depending on pickup order:

1. **If sim-rdl.7.4 lands first**: it will have introduced *some* outline
   rendering mechanism (component + spawn/update system) for all 6 special

   doesn't actually matter visually. One frame each — any pulsing/blinking

Either way, this issue's job is narrowly "make these 5 outline textures
available and drawable on the matching brick class" — the actual gameplay
behaviours the outlines represent (charge/breach/demolition/regen/shield
mechanics) are owned by a separate pm spec, same as sim-bu6/sim-fng for the
brick classes themselves.

title: Levels: packaged campaign levels (text-grid now, pluggable JSON/HTTP later)
description:
## Problem / goal
The game has no level concept: every run is one random board (sim-rdl.7.1) and clearing it ends the game. Add a finite campaign of packaged levels. Each level defines its brick layout (rows/columns, which bricks, their health, power-ups, explosive effects), its ball speed and its power-up count. Clearing a level moves to the next "sector".

## Direction (user, 2026-09-28)
- **Pluggable.** Levels will eventually be JSON definitions loadable over HTTP, bundling their own resources: skins/images, possibly code for special win conditions or timed rounds. The direction isn't fixed yet.
- **Iterate on the format.** Start with a hand-editable text-grid file, author real levels through PM interviews to see how it feels, then move to RON/JSON.
- **Keep the internal level model (`LevelDef`) independent of the file format**, so text-grid, JSON and HTTP loaders all produce the same thing and gameplay never changes when the format does.
- Bricks stay 80×30. A level uses 1–10 columns (centred) × 1–10 rows; `.` cells make shapes.
- Between levels: a ~2 s "SECTOR 02 // <name>" card. The HUD shows the sector.

## Children
- .1 LevelDef model + text-grid format + loader; the run plays campaign level 1
- .2 Campaign progression, sector card, HUD sector label, per-level ball speed
- .3 Author the starter campaign via PM interview (content)

## Later (not yet filed)
- RON/JSON format producing the same `LevelDef` (derive serde on it now so this is cheap).
- Loading level packs over HTTP (web and native).
- Per-level skins/resources (backgrounds, brick sprite overrides) via the `GameSprites` path (sim-rdl.6).
- Rule plugins: custom win conditions, timed rounds. Open question: Lua scripting is native-only (see CLAUDE.md), so code plugins need a wasm-compatible approach, or data-driven rules.

title: Level files: LevelDef model, text-grid .level format and asset loader
description:
## Problem / goal
Introduce levels as data. A format-independent `LevelDef` model, a first text-grid file format that you can edit by hand, and a Bevy asset loader, so the run's board comes from a level file instead of being hard-coded. Future JSON/HTTP loaders will produce the same `LevelDef`.

## Behaviour
- Level files live in `assets/levels/*.level`. Their order comes from a manifest, `assets/levels/campaign.txt` (one file name per line; `#` comments), because the web build can't list directories.
- A run plays the **first** level in the manifest (progression is .2).
- Ships with `assets/levels/01-random.level`: 7 rows × 10 of `?` with `powerups: 6`, which reproduces today's random board (sim-rdl.7.1), so gameplay is unchanged until real levels are authored (.3).
- **Text-grid format:**
  ```
  # comments start with #
  name: Rainbow Bands
  speed_factor: 1.5      # optional; ball speed = 300 x factor; default 1.8 (today's 540)
  powerups: 6            # optional; N extra random bricks get a power-up; default 0
  legend:                # optional; add or override symbols for this file
    k = titanium hits=4
    v = ceramic powerup
  grid:
  XXXXXXXXXX
  CCCCCCCCCC
  ..TTTTTT..
  ```
- **Built-in legend:**
  - `C` ceramic, `T` titanium, `G` tungsten (gold)
  - `X` explosive charge, `B` explosive breach, `D` explosive demolition
  - `R` regen, `S` shield glass
  - `P` power-up (reactor) brick
  - `?` a weighted-random class (the sim-rdl.7.1 weights)
  - `.` empty
- **Legend attributes:** a class name (`ceramic|titanium|tungsten|explosive:charge|explosive:breach|explosive:demolition|regen|shield|reactor|random`), optional `hits=N` (1–9, overrides the class default), optional `powerup` (this brick drops a power-up, kind picked from the weighted registry).
- **Grid rules:**
  - 1–10 rows. Every row has the same width, 1–10 columns.
  - The grid is centred horizontally under the top wall at today's top offset.
  - At least one brick. Any class, including shield glass, may appear.
- **Invalid files:** unknown symbol, ragged rows, too big, bad attribute, or no bricks. The game logs an error naming the file, line and column, and falls back to the built-in random board; it never panics.
- **Hot reload (native):** saving a level file while the game runs applies it the next time a run starts (Start / Play again), not mid-board.

## Out of scope
Progression between levels, sector card and HUD (.2), per-level skins, JSON/RON, HTTP loading, custom win conditions or timers, an in-game editor.

## Notes for the coder
- `src/levels/` module with its own `Plugin`:
  - `LevelDef { name, speed_factor: Option<f32>, extra_powerups, grid: Vec<Vec<Option<CellDef>>> }`
  - `CellDef { class: ClassSpec /* Fixed(BrickClass) | Random */, hits: Option<u8>, powerup: bool }`
  - Derive `serde::{Serialize, Deserialize}` now so the later JSON format is nearly free.
- The parser is a pure `fn parse_level(&str) -> Result<LevelDef, LevelError>` (line/col in errors), unit-tested heavily. Wrap it in a Bevy `AssetLoader` for extension `level`. The manifest is a tiny second loader, or a plain-text asset.
- Board building: `fn build_board(&LevelDef, &mut impl Rng) -> Vec<(BrickCell, BrickClass, hits, powerup)>` resolves `?` and the `powerups: N` extras, then spawns through the existing brick spawn path (sim-rdl.7.1's `BrickClass`, `BrickCell`, `BrickHealth`, power-up marker).
- Ball speed: today the `BALL_SPEED` const drives serve and renormalisation. Make it a `BallSpeed` resource = 300 x the level's `speed_factor` (default = `BALL_SPEED_SCALE` 1.8 = today's 540; sim-a7k.4 later makes the default ramp per round). Independent of GAME_SCALE.
- The level must be loaded before `start_run` spawns bricks. Load the handles at startup (menu time); if not loaded yet or failed, use the fallback board.
- Assets on web come via trunk `copy-dir` (sim-rdl.6). Keep headless tests independent of files by testing `parse_level`/`build_board` directly and injecting a `LevelDef` resource.
- Update CLAUDE.md with the module layout and the format summary. Also add `docs/levels.md` with the format reference.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the shipped `campaign.txt` → `01-random.level`, a run looks and plays like today's random board (7×10, exactly 6 power-up bricks).
- [x] Replacing `01-random.level`'s grid with a hand-written shape (e.g. a 5×8 diamond using `.`, `C`, `T`, `X`, `S`) shows exactly that shape, centred, on the next Start.
- [ ] A legend entry like `k = titanium hits=4` produces a titanium brick that needs 4 hits; `v = ceramic powerup` produces a ceramic brick that drops a power-up when broken.
- [ ] `speed_factor: 2.0` serves the ball at 600 world px/s (visibly faster); omitting it keeps today's 540.
- [x] A file with an unknown symbol, ragged rows or 11 rows logs an error naming the file/line/column and the game falls back to the random board without panicking.
- [ ] Native: editing the level file while the game runs changes the board at the next Start / Play again.
- [ ] The web build (`trunk serve`) loads the level from `assets/levels/`.
- [ ] `cargo test` includes parser tests (valid file, each error kind, legend overrides, `?` and `powerups: N` resolution with a seeded rng); clippy and `trunk build` pass; `docs/levels.md` documents the format.
- [ ] The damage sprite ladder (sim-rdl.7.9) uses the brick's own max hits (`BrickMaxHits`, from the level's `hits=N`), not `class.max_hits()`: a `tungsten hits=1` brick spawns showing the intact plate, and a `titanium hits=4` brick shows cracked / broken at its own thresholds. A headless test pins this.

title: Campaign progression: advance levels with a sector card and HUD sector label
description:
## Problem / goal
Turn a single board into a campaign: clearing a level moves to the next one in `campaign.txt`, and clearing the last one wins.

## Behaviour
- A run starts at the first level in `campaign.txt`. Start and Play again always start from level 1.
- **Clearing a level that isn't the last:**
  - The game freezes and a centred card shows `SECTOR 02 // <level name>` (sector = 1-based level index, two digits) for ~2 s.
  - Then the next level's board appears.
  - The ball is anchored on the paddle, waiting for click/Space.
- **Carry over / reset between levels:**
  - Score and lives carry over.
  - Falling power-ups are removed and active power-up effects end (paddle back to normal width).
  - Ball speed switches to the new level's speed (its `speed_factor`, or the per-round ramp from sim-a7k.4).
- Clearing the last level shows the existing win screen ("YOU WIN!" with the final score).
- Losing all lives on any level shows the existing game-over screen.
- The HUD shows `SECTOR 01` (top-right, Steelbreak HUD style) during play.
- Pausing during the sector card is allowed; the card timer freezes while paused.

## Out of scope
Level select, saving progress, bonus lives, per-level skins, score multipliers.

## Notes for the coder
- Add a `CurrentLevel(usize)` resource (reset in `start_run`), and a level-transition phase: e.g. a `PlayState::LevelClear` sub-state with physics paused (`game_state.rs` already pauses `Time<Physics>` outside `Playing`), or a timer resource. Gameplay systems already gate on `PlayState::Playing`.
- Today `ball_movement` calls `end_run(Won)` when `broke_brick && brick_query.is_empty()`. Route that through "level cleared", which decides next level vs `end_run(Won)`.
- Board teardown/spawn between levels: despawn remaining level entities (falling power-ups, burst flashes), respawn bricks from the next `LevelDef` via .1's `build_board`, re-anchor the ball (sim-rdl.1's `anchored()`). Fire a `LevelStarted` event so subsystems (power-ups) reset per level. Don't reuse `RestartGame`, which also implies score/lives reset.
- Tests: inject a 2-level campaign of tiny `LevelDef`s (1 brick each) and drive clear → card → level 2 → clear → Won.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] With a 2-level campaign, clearing level 1 shows "SECTOR 02 // <name of level 2>" for about 2 s, then level 2's board with the ball anchored on the paddle.
- [ ] Score and lives are the same after the transition as before it; any falling power-up is gone and a widened paddle is back to normal width.
- [ ] Level 2's speed (`speed_factor`) applies after the transition.
- [ ] Clearing the last level shows "YOU WIN!" with the total score; losing all lives on level 2 shows "GAME OVER".
- [x] Play again after either ending starts at level 1 with score 0 and 3 lives.
- [x] The HUD shows "SECTOR 01" on level 1 and "SECTOR 02" on level 2.
- [ ] Pausing during the sector card freezes it; resuming continues it.
- [ ] `cargo test` covers the 2-level flow (clear → card → next → win) and the carry-over/reset rules.

title: Ball speed ramps per round: speed factor 1.5 +0.1 per round, capped at 2.5
description:
## Problem / goal
Every round should play a little faster. The ball's speed is `300 × speed factor`. The factor starts at 1.8, which is today's 540 world px/s (the `BALL_SPEED_SCALE` the user set in PR #43), rises 0.1 per round and caps at 2.5 (750). The level system owns the round counter. The defaults are a starting point, to be tuned when the starter levels are written (sim-a7k.3). Part of the levels epic sim-a7k.

## Behaviour
- **Round** = the campaign level (sector) being played, counted from 1. Start and Play again reset to round 1.
- **Default speed factor for round n:** `min(1.8 + 0.1 × (n − 1), 2.5)`. So round 1 = 1.8 (540), round 2 = 1.9 (570), and round 8 onward = 2.5 (750).
- The speed is used for the serve and for the constant-speed renormalisation (the ball's speed stays constant within a round, as today).
- **Level override:** a level file may set `speed_factor: <x>` to replace the ramp value for that level. Without the key, the ramp applies.
- **Separate from sizing:** this factor is independent of `GAME_SCALE`. Sizes, gravity and fonts never change between rounds.
- The four tuning values are named consts in one place: base speed 300, start 1.8 (today's `BALL_SPEED_SCALE`), step 0.1, max 2.5.

## Out of scope
- Speeding up within a round (by time or hits).
- Showing speed in the HUD.
- Changing `GAME_SCALE`.
- Final tuning of the defaults (sim-a7k.3).

## Notes for the coder
- sim-a7k.1 (PR #43) adds `BALL_SPEED_SCALE = 1.8` and turns the speed into a level-driven resource (`BallSpeed`). This task makes that resource's default come from `speed_factor(round)`, a pure, unit-tested fn.
- The round index comes from sim-a7k.2's campaign progression (the current sector). Reset it on `RestartGame` (its own observer, per the `RestartGame` convention).
- At 750 px/s with a 22.5 px ball, check for tunnelling through bricks and the paddle; enable Avian swept CCD on the ball if needed.
- Paddle follow (`follow_velocity`) may need to keep up at higher speeds. Note any tuning in the PR.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit test of `speed_factor(round)`: 1 → 1.8, 2 → 1.9, 5 → 2.2, 8 → 2.5, 20 → 2.5 (cap)
- [ ] Round 1 plays at today's speed (540 world px/s, the served ball's measured speed within 1%)
- [ ] Clearing level 1 and serving on level 2 gives a ball speed of 570. A headless test drives the progression and reads the ball's speed after the serve.
- [ ] A level file with `speed_factor: 2.0` serves at 600 regardless of its round; without the key the ramp value applies
- [ ] Play again (or Start after Main menu) resets to round 1 speed
- [ ] Ball, paddle and brick sizes are identical on every round (`GAME_SCALE` untouched)
- [ ] At the cap (750), the ball doesn't pass through bricks or the paddle in a manual play-through of a fast level
- [ ] `cargo test`, clippy and `trunk build` pass
close_reason: Ball speed ramps per round: 1.8 +0.1, capped at 2.5 (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/80)

title: Outline particles: subtle sparks orbiting special bricks' frames
description:
## Problem / goal
The behaviour outline particle sheets (`assets/particles/outline_{explosive,regen,shield,reactor}.png`, 128x32, 4 frames of 32x32, greyscale, tinted in code; graffiti versions from sim-usq.4) are shipped but not drawn. Add a subtle ambient effect on top of the painted frames from sim-0sp.

## Behaviour
- **Orbit marquee:** each special brick (explosive kinds, regen, shield, reactor) has **2–4 sparks** travelling along the edge of its 168x68 frame, drawn above the frame.
- **Tint** in the brick's class hue (explosive red, regen green, shield cyan, reactor violet #b58cff; take them from `theme.rs`).
- **Per-class personality:**

  | Class | Motion |
  |---|---|
  | Explosive (all 3 kinds share a sheet; they may differ in rate) | fast and jittery |
  | Regen | slow and calm |
  | Shield | smooth glide |
  | Reactor | pulsing (speed or brightness swells) |

- **Damaged bricks orbit faster.** Regen speeds up until it heals, matching the faster frame blink from sim-0sp; reactor speeds up after its first hit. Bricks that die in one hit never show it.
- **Lifetime:** particles stop and vanish with the brick (break, blast, level clear, run end), freeze while paused, and follow a brick that moves (e.g. Collapse, sim-rjt).
- **Performance:** a board full of specials stays smooth.

## Out of scope
Changing the sheets or frames, any Settings toggle, and the static frames themselves (sim-0sp).

## Notes for the coder
- **Blocked by sim-0sp** (painted frames).
- Use bevy_enoki effects per class (`outline_<class>.particle.ron`), following the `particles/mod.rs` patterns. Path motion along a rounded rect is probably a small custom system moving emitter entities, or child emitters on the frame.
- Atlas: `TextureAtlasLayout::from_grid(UVec2::new(32, 32), 4, 1, None, None)`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Native run: every special brick shows 2–4 sparks orbiting its frame in its class hue, drawn above the frame; plain bricks show none (screenshot)
- [ ] The four classes are distinguishable by motion: explosive fast/jittery, regen slow, shield smooth, reactor pulsing (short recording)
- [ ] A hit regen brick's sparks orbit faster until it heals; a hit reactor brick's sparks orbit faster
- [ ] Breaking or blasting a special brick removes its sparks at once; pausing freezes them
- [ ] Andromada (or a board with 30+ specials) holds the same frame rate as with the effect off (FPS readout or log before/after)
- [ ] Headless test: spawning a special brick attaches its orbit emitter; despawning the brick leaves no orphan emitter entities
close_reason: Outline sparks travelling special bricks' frames (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/102)

title: Use Steelbreak hangar background
description:
## Asset (from PR art/sim-rdl.5.3-hangar-background, merges to `assets/sprites/`)

`assets/sprites/hangar_bg.png` — RGB (opaque, no alpha), exactly 1800x1300
(2x of `WINDOW_WIDTH`x`WINDOW_HEIGHT` = 900x650), 1412 KB.

## What this replaces

`src/sprites.rs` already has exactly the plumbing needed — `SpritesPlugin`
loads one full-window background image and spawns it as a `Sprite` sized to
`(WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT)` at `BACKGROUND_Z` behind everything:

```rust
const BACKGROUND_PATH: &str = "sprites/background.png";
```

This is the wiring: just repoint that constant at the new file.

```rust
const BACKGROUND_PATH: &str = "sprites/hangar_bg.png";
```

The existing test (`startup_loads_the_background_and_spawns_it_behind_everything`)
asserts against `BACKGROUND_PATH` itself, not a literal string, so it keeps
passing unchanged.

`assets/sprites/background.png` (the file `BACKGROUND_PATH` currently
points at) was a placeholder from an earlier round and has no other
reference in the codebase (`grep -rn background.png src` finds only this one
constant) — it's fine to delete once `hangar_bg.png` is wired in, but that's
your call / the pm's, not mine to make.

## Notes carried over from the brief (for context, not extra work)

- The image is deliberately low-contrast in its upper portion and the
  top-left ~300x120 game-px corner is darkened further (I added a soft
  vignette there myself during production — see `art/manifest.toml` — since
  the picked concept's leftmost ceiling lamp sat right in the HUD text
  corner and was too bright as generated). No code-side dimming/overlay is
  needed for HUD readability; the asset already accounts for it.
- No parallax/second layer — the brief's optional second layer wasn't used
  (round 1 didn't suggest needing one), so this is a single static
  full-window sprite exactly like the current `background.png` wiring.

## Manifest / provenance

See `art/manifest.toml` (`id = "hangar-background"`) and
`art/prompts/sim-rdl.5.3-r1.txt` for the source prompt if regeneration is
ever needed.

title: Use Steelbreak intact brick sprites for all 7 brick classes
description:
## Problem / goal
The Steelbreak brick sprites for all 7 classes are in `assets/sprites/bricks/`: ceramic, titanium, tungsten and reactor from sim-rdl.5.1 (#23), and explosive, regen and shield from sim-rdl.5.4. The game still draws bricks as flat colours. Render every class with its **intact** sprite.

## Scope change (user, 2026-09-28)
Brick damage will be shown by particles (particles epic, first task), not by cracked sprites. This task uses **only the `*_intact.png` sprites**; the `*_cracked.png` files stay unused. This task also absorbs sim-fng (the explosive/regen/shield sprites), since it is the same brick setup.

## Behaviour
- All 7 classes render with `assets/sprites/bricks/<class>_intact.png` at 80×30 (shield glass is `shield_intact.png`, reactor is the power-up brick).
- Damage indication (interim): a brick below full hits is tinted darker (sprite colour tint), as today's flat colours are. The particles task removes this tint when it lands.
- Behaviour outlines (sim-rdl.7.4) and the shield-glass flash still show.
- No gameplay change.
- If a sprite file is missing, that brick falls back to its flat class colour (no panic, no invisible brick).

## Out of scope
Cracked sprites, particles, outline sprites (sim-8j0).

## Notes for the coder
- Reuse sim-rdl.7.1's `BrickClass`. Load the 7 handles once into `GameSprites` (sim-rdl.6) keyed by class, with no `asset_server.load` in `on_ball_collision`. Reactor is decided in one place only.
- Keep sprite selection a pure function `(class) -> SpriteKey` and unit-test it. The headless tests have no `AssetServer`.

---
## Asset-producer handoffs (original drafts, for reference; ignore the cracked-sprite parts)
## Assets (from PR art/sim-rdl.5.1-steelbreak-bricks, merges to `assets/sprites/bricks/`)

8 files, all RGBA PNG, exactly 160x60 px (2x of the in-game 80x30 brick):

- `assets/sprites/bricks/ceramic_intact.png` / `ceramic_cracked.png`
- `assets/sprites/bricks/titanium_intact.png` / `titanium_cracked.png`
- `assets/sprites/bricks/tungsten_intact.png` / `tungsten_cracked.png`
- `assets/sprites/bricks/reactor_intact.png` / `reactor_cracked.png` (the violet power-up brick)

Each plate fills its 160x60 canvas edge to edge (only the rounded corners are
transparent), so at render time `custom_size: Some(Vec2::new(80.0, 30.0))`
maps 1:1 onto the existing `BRICK_WIDTH`/`BRICK_HEIGHT` collider (no size
changes needed there).

## What this replaces

`spawn_bricks` in `src/main.rs` (around line 304-326) currently does:

```rust
let colors = [RED, ORANGE, YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE];
...
Sprite::from_color(colors[row % colors.len()], Vec2::new(BRICK_WIDTH, BRICK_HEIGHT)),
```

and `on_ball_collision` (around line 358-384) darkens the flat colour on a
non-breaking hit:

```rust
sprite.color = sprite.color.darker(CRACKED_DARKEN);
```

Neither of those needs to survive: brick "damage" should become a texture
swap (intact -> cracked) rather than a colour darken, and the row-based
5-colour palette should become the 4 material classes above.

## Suggested wiring

1. Add a `BrickClass` enum (`Ceramic`, `Titanium`, `Tungsten`, `Reactor`) and
   a `BrickClass` component, assigned per-brick at spawn time in
   `spawn_bricks` (any distribution is fine — the brief doesn't pin one down
   — but note the **reactor class must line up with the existing power-up
   bricks**: `assign_power_up_bricks` in `src/powerups/mod.rs` already picks
   6 random bricks at the start of each run and gives them `PowerUpBrick`
   with `POWER_UP_BRICK_COLOR` (`#b58cff`, violet) and
   `POWER_UP_BRICK_HITS` = 2. The simplest wiring: any brick carrying
   `PowerUpBrick` renders as `reactor_*`, independent of whatever class
   distribution the non-power-up bricks use — don't duplicate the "is this
   a reactor" decision in two places.
2. A helper like `fn brick_texture(class: BrickClass, cracked: bool) -> &'static str`
   (or a `HashMap`/`match` returning the asset path) driven by `BrickHealth`
   for the cracked flag (`health.0 < initial_health`), used at spawn time and
   in `on_ball_collision`'s "still has health left" branch to swap
   `sprite.image` (instead of `sprite.color = sprite.color.darker(...)`).
3. Reactor-specific: brief says "the reactor core is the power-up brick from
   sim-rdl.3 (it takes 2 hits in game; its cracked state shows after the
   first hit)" — that already matches `POWER_UP_BRICK_HITS = 2` and the
   existing "still has health left -> show damage" branch, so no health
   logic changes needed, just swap the visual there too.
4. `Sprite::from_color` -> `Sprite { image: asset_server.load(path), custom_size: Some(Vec2::new(BRICK_WIDTH, BRICK_HEIGHT)), ..default() }`.
5. `CRACKED_DARKEN` constant and the `.darker(...)` call become dead once the
   texture swap lands — remove them.

## Suggested Bevy snippet

```rust
#[derive(Component, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum BrickClass { Ceramic, Titanium, Tungsten, Reactor }

impl BrickClass {
    fn asset_path(self, cracked: bool) -> &'static str {
        match (self, cracked) {
            (BrickClass::Ceramic, false) => "sprites/bricks/ceramic_intact.png",
            (BrickClass::Ceramic, true) => "sprites/bricks/ceramic_cracked.png",
            (BrickClass::Titanium, false) => "sprites/bricks/titanium_intact.png",
            (BrickClass::Titanium, true) => "sprites/bricks/titanium_cracked.png",
            (BrickClass::Tungsten, false) => "sprites/bricks/tungsten_intact.png",
            (BrickClass::Tungsten, true) => "sprites/bricks/tungsten_cracked.png",
            (BrickClass::Reactor, false) => "sprites/bricks/reactor_intact.png",
            (BrickClass::Reactor, true) => "sprites/bricks/reactor_cracked.png",
        }
    }
}

// at spawn:
commands.spawn((
    Sprite {
        image: asset_server.load(class.asset_path(false)),
        custom_size: Some(Vec2::new(BRICK_WIDTH, BRICK_HEIGHT)),
        ..default()
    },
    Transform::from_xyz(x, y, 0.0),
    RigidBody::Static,
    Collider::rectangle(BRICK_WIDTH, BRICK_HEIGHT),
    Brick,
    class,
    BrickHealth(1),
    DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame),
));

// on damaging hit (still alive), in on_ball_collision:
sprite.image = asset_server.load(class.asset_path(true));
```

Note `on_ball_collision` doesn't currently have `Res<AssetServer>` or
`&BrickClass` in its query — both need adding to the system params.

## Manifest / provenance

See `art/manifest.toml` (`id = "bricks-steelbreak"`) and
`art/prompts/sim-rdl.5.1-r1.txt` / `sim-rdl.5.1-r3.txt` for the source
prompts if regeneration is ever needed.


### sim-fng
## Assets (from PR art/sim-rdl.5.4-brick-classes, merges to `assets/sprites/bricks/`)

6 files, all RGBA PNG, exactly 160x60 px (2x of the in-game 80x30 brick),
same plate silhouette/bevel as the 4 classes from sim-rdl.5.1:

- `assets/sprites/bricks/explosive_intact.png` / `explosive_cracked.png` —
  red plate, yellow/black hazard-chevron corners.
- `assets/sprites/bricks/regen_intact.png` / `regen_cracked.png` — green
  plate, fine vein/lattice etching. **Note:** the intact vein pattern is
  fine hairline etching; the cracked state's fracture lines are
  deliberately darker/thicker/harder-edged and cut straight across the
  veins (the art-director specifically flagged the risk of confusing the
  two) — if you ever need to detect "is this brick cracked" from the image
  itself (you shouldn't; use `BrickHealth`/game state), don't use "has thin
  lines" as a heuristic.
- `assets/sprites/shield_intact.png` / `shield_cracked.png` — translucent
  cyan tempered-glass panel, hex-cell refraction pattern; cracked = a
  radiating shatter-web centred on an impact point, denser than the other
  two classes' fracture style, plus the same chipped corner.

## Relationship to sim-rdl.5.1 / sim-bu6

This is the **same brick system** as sim-rdl.5.1 (ceramic/titanium/tungsten/
reactor) — these 3 are additional classes on the identical plate
silhouette, not a separate mechanism. **sim-bu6** (still at `stage:spec` as
of this writing) is the coder issue for the first 4 classes and already
proposes the `BrickClass` enum / `asset_path(class, cracked)` pattern this
project should use. Whoever implements either issue should almost
certainly do **both in the same pass** — extending one `BrickClass` enum to
7 variants is far less churn than landing two separate enums or editing the
same match statement twice back-to-back. I haven't added a hard beads
dependency between them (that's a sequencing call for the pm), but please
read sim-bu6's notes first if you're picking this one up alone.

If sim-bu6 already landed by the time this is picked up: just add 3 more
`BrickClass` variants (`Explosive`, `Regen`, `Shield`) and 6 more arms to
whatever `asset_path` match/lookup it introduced, pointing at the file names
above.

## New gameplay behaviour (explicitly NOT art's job)

The brief notes explosive/regen/shield have their own gameplay rules
(explosive breaks neighbours, regen heals if not finished quickly, shield
only breaks from above/after a combo) — those rules are owned by a
separate pm spec, not this art issue. This issue is purely "make these 3
classes render," the same scope as sim-bu6. Don't infer or implement the
gameplay behaviour from the visual design here.

## Manifest / provenance

See `art/manifest.toml` (`id = "bricks-steelbreak-2"`) and
`art/prompts/sim-rdl.5.4-r{1..6}.txt` for the source prompts if
regeneration is ever needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] In a run, bricks of all 7 classes (ceramic, titanium, tungsten, power-up/reactor, explosive, regen, shield glass) show their Steelbreak intact sprites, not flat rectangles.
- [x] Damaging a multi-hit brick keeps its intact sprite, tinted darker (no cracked sprite); a regen brick healing back to full loses the tint.
- [x] Temporarily renaming `assets/sprites/bricks/ceramic_intact.png` makes ceramic bricks fall back to flat colour without a panic.
- [ ] The web build (`trunk serve`) shows the sprites too.
- [x] `cargo test` includes unit tests for the sprite-selection function; clippy and `trunk build` pass.
close_reason: All 7 brick classes draw their Steelbreak intact sprite, shipped (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/36) — web-build sprite rendering still worth a manual browser check per PR notes

description:
## The ask (user, 2026-09-30), lowest priority
Add sound to the game. The user asked for 'P5'; beads' lowest priority is P4, so it's filed as P4 backlog. The user is extending the agent workflow with a **sound-engineer** role, which will own this. Don't spec or release it before that role exists.

## Notes for later
- Browsers block audio until the player clicks or presses a key. The web loading screen (sim-jbt.1) deliberately has no click-to-launch gate; revisit that if menu music should start straight away.
- Natural hook points already exist: `BrickDamaged`, `BrickDestroyed`, `BrickExploded`, `PowerUpCollected`, the paddle and wall collisions, and `AppState`/`PlayState` transitions. Audio can observe these the same way particles do (gameplay fires events, presentation observes).
- Native and web both need the chosen audio backend (bevy_audio or bevy_kira_audio) checked on wasm.

## Sound pipeline direction (user, 2026-10-04)
Still parked (not specced, not released); these are decisions so far, not a spec.
- **Generation reuses the local ComfyUI** (`~/Projects/ComfyUI`, systemd service on 127.0.0.1:8188), the same way the art pipeline does. Candidates: Stable Audio Open (SFX and ambience) and ACE-Step (music). The pattern from sim-4ws carries over: user-editable ComfyUI workflow files with `artgen:*`-style named slots, provenance in meta.json, rounds and picks.
- **Listening and picking happen through the asset web page**, like art review. Audio contact sheets with players on the page, organised in rounds the way art is.
- **Rename art-web → `game-asset-web`.** Its root gets `visual/` (today's art/concepts content) and `audio/` (sound rounds). Today art-web is a plain `python3 -m http.server 9090` over `art/concepts` in a tmux window (not started by `agent-team up`).
- **Longer term, a game-agnostic asset library.** The user wants every art and audio asset browsable in one place and reusable as a reference for later games. This fits the earlier direction (sim-0ph, 2026-10-03) that artgen should become a standalone, game-agnostic tool that games link into. The game-asset-web tool will probably need revisiting for this: browsing across games and issues, search/tags, and provenance (prompt, seed, workflow) per asset.

title: Art: graffiti capsule icon per power-up (Super-Sizer, Collapse)
description:
## Subject
One graffiti line-art power-up capsule per kind: a shared capsule shell with a per-kind arrow glyph and accent colour inside. Super-Sizer and Collapse for now.

## Use in game
- **Falling pickup:** a broken power-up brick drops it, it falls down the well, and the paddle catches it. Drawn at 36×36 world px (`POWER_UP_SIZE` = 24 × GAME_SCALE 1.5).
- **Time capsule icon:** shown in the right side panel next to the timer gauge (`capsules.rs`, `ICON_SIZE` 32). The same image is used in both places.
- **Readability:** it must read against the dark void (#0a0e15), both moving through the well and still in the panel. The two kinds must be told apart at 32 px by glyph shape alone, with colour as a second cue. It must not look like a brick or the ball.
- **Replaces:** the single shared `assets/sprites/powerup.png` (the graffiti purple gem in a steel frame from sim-usq.2 r2/v6), which every kind uses today. Collapse (sim-rjt) currently has only a code tint.

## Variants
Same shell, same size and silhouette, with a different glyph and accent:
1. **Super-Sizer** (widens the paddle): two bold arrows pointing outward from a short horizontal bar (◀▬▶). Accent: emitter cyan #4fd8ff.
2. **Collapse** (the remaining bricks fall down their columns): a short stack of 2-3 blocks with a bold downward arrow beside or through it. Accent: warm orange #ffab4d / #d98c64.
3. **Blank shell**, no glyph: the base for future power-ups. One new glyph per kind later.

## Frames
1 (static).

## References
- art/style.md: graffiti line-art. Dark keyline plus a light/warm inner offset line, flat colour blocks, hard white glints, cold key light from the upper left and warm bounce from the lower right. No spray effects, no lettering.
- Shell: a rounded space-age capsule or pill pod in structural steel (#16202c) with a bright rim, roughly square overall so it fills a 48×48 box.
- Current assets/sprites/powerup.png (graffiti, sim-usq.2 r2/v6): match its line weight and framing. Its purple gem is replaced by the per-kind glyph.
- Match the graffiti brick plates and ball from sim-usq for line weight.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] assets/sprites/powerups/super_sizer.png, assets/sprites/powerups/collapse.png and assets/sprites/powerups/shell.png (blank): RGBA, exactly 48x48, transparent background, same shell silhouette and position in all three
- [x] At 32x32 on #0a0e15 the two glyphs are told apart by shape alone (outward arrows vs falling blocks), and each has its accent colour (cyan #4fd8ff / orange #ffab4d)
- [x] Graffiti line-art per art/style.md: dark keyline, light or warm inner line, hard highlights; no spray effects, no lettering
- [x] Doesn't read as a brick or the ball at 36x36 in the well
- [x] Prompt and pick recorded in art/manifest.toml; the coder issue for wiring a sprite per PowerUpKind (keeping powerup.png as the fallback) is filed at stage:spec

title: Dev console (native debug) for live tuning, with a shipped tuning file
description:
## Problem / goal
Tuning values are compile-time consts spread across modules, so every gameplay tweak needs a recompile. Goal: tune ball, paddle, bricks and power-ups live in a native dev build, and save the result as the shipped defaults.

## Decisions (user, 2026-10-03)
- An **egui slider panel** (bevy_egui 0.42, no inspector), toggled with ` (backtick). Compiled only into native debug builds, never into release or web. The game keeps running while it's open, and typing in a field doesn't drive the game.
- Value groups: ball speed (incl. the sim-a7k.4 ramp), paddle feel, bricks, power-ups.
- **Persistence:** a Save button writes `assets/game.tuning.ron`. Every build (native and web) loads it at startup. The file ships from day one with today's values and is the source of truth for shipped defaults.
- **Debug actions:** skip level, win/lose run, spawn a chosen power-up, set lives (incl. infinite), rebuild the board with current values.
- **New tunables, designed here:** explosive blast radius and chaining per kind, and a drop chance for ordinary bricks. Defaults reproduce today's behaviour exactly.
- Level overrides (`speed_factor:`, `hits=`, `powerups:`) still beat tuning defaults.

## Slices
.1 Tuning resource + file → .2 ball/paddle/lives read it (after sim-a7k.4) and .3 bricks/power-ups read it → .4 new tunables → .5 panel shell + ball/paddle + Save → .6 panel bricks/power-ups → .7 debug actions.

## Out of scope
GAME_SCALE and world/brick geometry, the world inspector, any console in release/web, and Lua hooks.

title: Tuning resource and shipped game.tuning.ron (all builds)
description:
## Problem / goal
Add a runtime `Tuning` resource and a tuning file that every build loads. Nothing reads it yet; behaviour is unchanged.

## Behaviour
- New `src/tuning.rs`. `Tuning` has nested `ball` / `paddle` / `bricks` / `powerups` structs. `Tuning::default()` is built from today's consts, and every struct has `#[serde(default)]` so partial or old files load.
- `assets/game.tuning.ron` is committed with the defaults. A `TuningAsset` loader (extension `tuning.ron`, so it doesn't clash with bevy_enoki's `ron` loader) is registered in `main()` like `LevelsPlugin`. A sync system copies Loaded/Modified into the resource. Native hot reload works through file_watcher.
- A missing file or parse error logs a warning and keeps the compiled defaults.
- The web loading splash (`web_splash.rs`) also waits for the tuning asset to finish loading or fail.

## Out of scope
Any consumer of Tuning, and the panel.

## Notes for the coder
Analyst map in the sim-dj6 comments. Move `ron` from dev-dependencies to dependencies (already in the tree). Init `Tuning` in `add_game` so headless tests get the defaults; the loader goes in `main()` only.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cargo test: a test parses assets/game.tuning.ron and asserts it equals Tuning::default()
- [ ] A file containing only some fields loads, and the missing ones take their defaults (test)
- [ ] Native: editing a value in game.tuning.ron while cargo run is open updates the Tuning resource (log line or test via asset events)

title: Ball, paddle and lives read Tuning
description:
## Problem / goal
Move the ball, paddle and lives consts behind `Tuning` so they can be tuned live.

## Behaviour
- **Ball:** `Tuning.ball` = {per_factor 300, start factor 1.8, ramp step and max (from sim-a7k.4), min_vertical_fraction 0.3}. `BallSpeed::for_level` / `spawn_board` read it. A level's `speed_factor:` still wins. The min-vertical clamp in `ball_movement` reads it every frame.
- **Paddle:**
  - `Tuning.paddle` = {width 180, mass 3, damping 4, force 10500, follow_gain 20, max_follow_speed 3000, max_gap_per_frame 0.8}.
  - Force, follow and width are live: `update_paddle_width` uses the tuned base width, and Super-Sizer multiplies it.
  - Mass and damping are re-applied to the paddle when Tuning changes.
- **Lives:** `Tuning.starting_lives` = 3, read by `start_run` and the HUD.
- With the defaults, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Out of scope
Geometry consts (BALL_SIZE, PADDLE_HEIGHT, prongs), and the panel.

## Notes for the coder
**Blocked by sim-a7k.4 (speed ramp PR #80).** Rebase on it. `follow_velocity` gets a params struct, so update its tests. Watch the system-param count on start_run/advance_after_card.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cargo test passes with no changed expected values (defaults equal today's consts)
- [ ] Tests: changing Tuning.paddle.force changes paddle acceleration on the next frame; changing mass/damping updates the paddle's Mass/LinearDamping; changing width resizes the paddle and collider (with and without Super-Sizer)
- [ ] Test: Tuning.ball start factor is used for a level without speed_factor; a level with speed_factor ignores it

title: New tunables: explosive blast radius/chaining per kind, ordinary-brick drop chance
description:
## Problem / goal
Two values the user wants to tune don't exist yet. Design them as Tuning fields whose defaults reproduce today's behaviour exactly.

## Behaviour
- **Blast radius per explosive kind:**
  - `Tuning.bricks.blast` = {breach: {radius 1, chains true}, charge: {radius 1, chains true}, demolition: {radius 1, chains false}}. Check `resolve_blast` and set each `chains` default to match today.
  - **Shape:** breach is a plus/diamond (Manhattan distance ≤ r); charge and demolition are a square ring (Chebyshev distance ≤ r). At r=1 that is exactly today's offset tables in `reach()`.
  - **Chains:** chains=false means bricks the blast destroys don't set off further blasts, even if they're explosive. This matches today's per-kind rules.
  - The blast VFX scale with the radius.
- **Ordinary-brick drop chance:**
  - `Tuning.powerups.drop_chance` = 0.0, a 0..1 chance that breaking a non-reactor brick drops a power-up capsule (via `PowerUpSpawner`). Reactor bricks drop as today.
  - It's counted in the run's drop count, and blast kills also roll for it.

## Out of scope
Panel controls (sibling task), new explosive kinds, and visual marking of which bricks will drop.

## Notes for the coder
`src/bricks/explosive.rs` reach() (≈l.51-66) and resolve_blast; the drop path is in `src/powerups/mod.rs` drop_power_up. Use the game's existing RNG resource or a seeded RNG so tests are deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cargo test passes unchanged with defaults (all explosive tests keep their expected neighbour sets)
- [ ] Test: breach radius 2 destroys bricks at Manhattan distance ≤2 and no others; charge radius 2 destroys the 5x5 square
- [ ] Test: with demolition chains=false, an explosive brick inside its blast doesn't detonate; with chains=true it does
- [ ] Test: drop_chance 1.0 makes every ordinary brick break drop a capsule; 0.0 never does; reactor drops unchanged
- [ ] Native: setting breach radius 2 in game.tuning.ron gives a visibly larger blast with matching VFX

title: Dev console panel: shell, ball and paddle sections, Save
description:
## Problem / goal
The native-debug-only egui panel that edits Tuning live.

## Behaviour
- **Build gating:** a cargo feature `dev` (in `default`) pulls in optional `bevy_egui 0.42` from the non-wasm target table only. The code is gated `#[cfg(all(feature = "dev", debug_assertions, not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]`. `src/dev_console/mod.rs` has a `DevConsolePlugin` added in `main()`.
- **Toggle and input:** ` toggles the panel and the game keeps running. While egui wants keyboard or pointer input, gameplay input (Space/click serve, P/Esc pause, R, A/D/arrows, mouse-follow paddle) is ignored.
- **Sections:** Ball (start factor, ramp step/max, min-vertical fraction, plus a 'current BallSpeed' slider that writes BallSpeed directly for instant feel) and Paddle (all Tuning.paddle fields, starting lives). Sliders write ResMut<Tuning>.
- **Buttons:**
  - **Save** writes the full Tuning as pretty RON to `assets/game.tuning.ron` (native fs, asset root path). The hot reload that follows is a no-op.
  - **Reset to defaults** sets every value back to its compiled default.

## Out of scope
Brick and power-up sections, and debug actions (sibling tasks).

title: Dev console: debug actions (skip/win/lose, spawn power-up, lives, rebuild board)
description:
## Problem / goal
Debug actions for testing runs quickly.

## Behaviour
- A `DevAction` event with observers in a module that isn't egui (headless-testable; compiled only into native dev debug builds and `cfg(test)`):
  - **SkipLevel** (only in Playing): despawns all bricks silently (no score, no drops), then triggers `LevelCleared`. On the last level, the run is won.
  - **WinRun / LoseRun:** `end_run` with the GameOutcome.
  - **SpawnPowerUp(kind):** a falling capsule above the paddle through the real pickup path. Extract a `pub(crate)` spawn fn from `drop_power_up`, which `test_spawn_power_up` reuses.
  - **SetLives(n)** and **InfiniteLives(bool):** a dev flag checked where a lost ball ends the run; the HUD shows ∞.
  - **RebuildBoard:** respawns the current level's board with current Tuning; score is kept and the ball is re-anchored.
- The panel gets an Actions section with a button for each action (kind picker for SpawnPowerUp).

## Out of scope
Level select, scripted test scenarios.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Headless tests on test_support::app(): SkipLevel advances to the next level (and wins after the last); a second SkipLevel during LevelClear does nothing; WinRun/LoseRun reach GameOver with the right outcome
- [ ] Test: SpawnPowerUp(SuperSizer) spawns a capsule that the paddle collects and the effect applies

title: Concept art: Enochian realm key art (nephilim battle, element bricks)
description:
## Subject

Hero key art for the Enochian re-theme of this breakout clone: realm I, "The Watchers'
Camp" (element earth). One 16:9 painterly frame showing the whole gameplay fiction at
once — the titan-brick ranks, the ship-paddle, and the ball of divine light mid-arc.

## Use in game

Establishes the canonical look for all five realms and every subsequent asset. Used as
the title/menu backdrop, the realm-I loading plate, and the reference every later
concept is judged against. The mechanic it must make legible: bricks are ranks of
nephilim titans floating in formation; the paddle is an ancient warship; clearing the
last brick translocates the ship to the next realm, where the battle is already raging.

Because it doubles as the style proof, it has to survive being viewed at 1x and at
thumbnail size in a contact sheet.

## Variants

4 variations in round 1 on `google/gemini-2.5-flash-image`, all from one prompt. If a
variant is picked, one refinement round on `google/gemini-3-pro-image` with the pick
passed as `--ref` for fidelity. Expect 4 more frames there.

Successor pieces in the same lane, filed separately once this look is locked:
element brick sheet (4 distinct silhouettes), the translocation beat (realm I → II),
and the ship design at gameplay scale.

## Frames

Static. No animation frames in this issue. The ball's arc is painted as a single
trajectory streak, not a sprite sequence.

## References

`art/style.md` is binding — palette, prompt preamble, Do/Don't all come from it.

Composition and register anchors, in priority order:
- `art/enoch_concept/ref_crop_watchers.png` — primary. Muted teal-sage colossus over an
  umber valley, one tiny mortal for scale. Closest to the intended register.
- `art/enoch_concept/nephilim-600nw-2505030389.png` — bone-cloud scale, gold cloud-break.
- `art/enoch_concept/360_F_988089084_sFoLE85aCf9sTdaMsogUiwpajtCuxAQe.png` — fire realm,
  ember colossus (reserve for realm IV).
- `art/enoch_concept/ai-generated-8464195_640.png` — encampment with giants looming,
  held for the translocation piece.

`ref_crop_axe.png` is a costume/material study for the titans, not a composition anchor.

All references are licensed stock previews: private mood only, never shipped or
published. The generated art derives from them and must not reproduce any watermark,
agency footer, or logo badge.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] 16:9 widescreen frame, minimum 1920x1080, saved as PNG
- [ ] no text, lettering, sigils, logos, watermarks, borders, signatures or UI overlays anywhere in the image
- [ ] matches the art/style.md palette: muted earthen frame with a single divine gold source; no neon, no chromatic bloom, no glossy specular
- [ ] no violet or magenta (reserved for realm V)
- [ ] brick ranks read as clearly separable rectangular blocks, not organic blobs, and are countable as rows at 1x
- [ ] the four element hues stay distinguishable at 1x if element variants appear
- [ ] the warship is present, small, bottom-centre, and legible as the paddle at gameplay scale
- [ ] the ball of light and its arc into the titan ranks are visible as one trajectory
- [ ] something deliberately small is in frame for scale, placed low
- [ ] clean dark space in both top corners for HUD overlay
- [ ] survives thumbnail viewing in the contact sheet without losing the read
- [ ] no reference watermark or badge reproduced from any source image
- [ ] picked variant recorded via `artgen pick`, prompt copied to art/enoch_concept/prompts/, round dir has meta.json

title: Use Steelbreak explosive/regen/shield brick sprites
description:
## Assets (from PR art/sim-rdl.5.4-brick-classes, merges to `assets/sprites/bricks/`)

6 files, all RGBA PNG, exactly 160x60 px (2x of the in-game 80x30 brick),
same plate silhouette/bevel as the 4 classes from sim-rdl.5.1:

- `assets/sprites/bricks/explosive_intact.png` / `explosive_cracked.png` —
  red plate, yellow/black hazard-chevron corners.
- `assets/sprites/bricks/regen_intact.png` / `regen_cracked.png` — green
  plate, fine vein/lattice etching. **Note:** the intact vein pattern is
  fine hairline etching; the cracked state's fracture lines are
  deliberately darker/thicker/harder-edged and cut straight across the
  veins (the art-director specifically flagged the risk of confusing the
  two) — if you ever need to detect "is this brick cracked" from the image
  itself (you shouldn't; use `BrickHealth`/game state), don't use "has thin
  lines" as a heuristic.
- `assets/sprites/shield_intact.png` / `shield_cracked.png` — translucent
  cyan tempered-glass panel, hex-cell refraction pattern; cracked = a
  radiating shatter-web centred on an impact point, denser than the other
  two classes' fracture style, plus the same chipped corner.

## Relationship to sim-rdl.5.1 / sim-bu6

This is the **same brick system** as sim-rdl.5.1 (ceramic/titanium/tungsten/
reactor) — these 3 are additional classes on the identical plate
silhouette, not a separate mechanism. **sim-bu6** (still at `stage:spec` as
of this writing) is the coder issue for the first 4 classes and already
proposes the `BrickClass` enum / `asset_path(class, cracked)` pattern this
project should use. Whoever implements either issue should almost
certainly do **both in the same pass** — extending one `BrickClass` enum to
7 variants is far less churn than landing two separate enums or editing the
same match statement twice back-to-back. I haven't added a hard beads
dependency between them (that's a sequencing call for the pm), but please
read sim-bu6's notes first if you're picking this one up alone.

If sim-bu6 already landed by the time this is picked up: just add 3 more
`BrickClass` variants (`Explosive`, `Regen`, `Shield`) and 6 more arms to
whatever `asset_path` match/lookup it introduced, pointing at the file names
above.

## New gameplay behaviour (explicitly NOT art's job)

The brief notes explosive/regen/shield have their own gameplay rules
(explosive breaks neighbours, regen heals if not finished quickly, shield
only breaks from above/after a combo) — those rules are owned by a
separate pm spec, not this art issue. This issue is purely "make these 3
classes render," the same scope as sim-bu6. Don't infer or implement the
gameplay behaviour from the visual design here.

## Manifest / provenance

See `art/manifest.toml` (`id = "bricks-steelbreak-2"`) and
`art/prompts/sim-rdl.5.4-r{1..6}.txt` for the source prompts if
regeneration is ever needed.

title: Agent workflow tuning: less friction, fewer tokens
description:
## Problem / goal
The agent pipeline works (99 issues, 72 closed, ~1.8 days lead time) but loses time and tokens to friction found in a survey: beads-only sync PRs are ~35% of the git log, 29 bounces across 99 issues (mostly master conflicts), `merge: auto` is contradicted by a `gh pr merge*` deny so merges stall, the tester/coder allowlist is missing common commands, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md carry duplicated boilerplate into every agent call, and the web build is only compile-checked.

## Behaviour
Children fix each item. Success = no `chore(beads)` PRs, no permission prompts in a coder-to-tester run, pr-manager can merge green PRs through a guarded wrapper, fewer bounces, smaller agent context, and a wasm smoke test in CI.

## Out of scope
- Switching to the Flywheel swarm model, multi-model mega-plans, or fungible agents on main.
- Anything in the Godot demo project (frogger).

## Notes for the coder
Some children touch files outside the repo (`~/.claude/agents/*.md`, `~/.claude/skills/*`, `~/.local/bin/*`). Those are not in git; note the exact edits in the PR description and the pm/user applies them.

title: Beads sync: switch to trunk-direct and skip CI for .beads-only pushes
description:
## Problem / goal
`beads.sync_commit: pr` makes every spec/approval/hygiene change a `chore/beads-sync-*` PR with its own CI run (~35% of the git log). master is protected, but `enforce_admins` is false, so the repo owner can push to it directly. Switch to `trunk-direct`, and stop CI rebuilding and redeploying Pages for beads-only commits.

## Behaviour
- `.claude/workflow.yaml`: `beads.sync_commit: trunk-direct`.
- `.github/workflows/build.yml`: add `paths-ignore: ['.beads/**']` to the `push` trigger (not to `pull_request`, so required checks still run on PRs).
- The pm commits `chore(beads): sync ...` straight to master and pushes. If the push is rejected (non-fast-forward), it runs `beads-sync-merge`/`br sync --merge` flow, rebases, and retries once.
- Docs: update `docs/agent-workflow.md` and the pm/`beads-queue` text so they stop describing the PR path as the default.

## Out of scope
- Moving beads state off git or gitignoring `issues.jsonl`.
- Changing branch protection.

## Notes for the coder
- `~/.claude/agents/pm.md` lines ~75-77 and `~/.claude/skills/beads-queue/SKILL.md` line ~24 live outside the repo; list the edits in the PR description.
- Direct pushes by the pm need `git push` (already allowed in `.claude/settings.local.json`). Keep the force-push denies.
- Confirm a beads-only push to master does not trigger the `deploy-pages` job.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] workflow.yaml shows `sync_commit: trunk-direct`
- [ ] A push touching only `.beads/**` does not start the Build workflow (verified from the Actions run list)
- [ ] A PR touching `.beads/**` plus code still runs `native`, `test`, `web`
- [ ] A pm spec-approval cycle ends with a direct master commit and no `chore/beads-sync-*` PR
- [ ] A fresh clone's `br sync --import-only` shows the same issues as the DB

title: Guarded pr-merge wrapper so pr-manager can merge green PRs
description:
## Problem / goal
`workflow.yaml` says `merge: auto` and pr-manager runs `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`, but `.claude/settings.local.json` denies `gh pr merge*` for every agent and the repo has `allow_auto_merge: false`. Merges therefore stall or are done by hand. Add a guarded wrapper, modelled on `~/.local/bin/beads-sync-merge`, that pr-manager may run while raw `gh pr merge` stays denied.

## Behaviour
New script `pr-merge <pr-number>` (next to `beads-sync-merge`) that squash-merges with `--delete-branch` and refuses unless ALL hold:
- PR is open and not a draft; base is the trunk from `.claude/workflow.yaml`.
- Every required status check (`native`, `web`; `test` too) completed successfully.
- GitHub reports it mergeable and the head SHA matches what was checked.
- No unresolved review threads and no `changes requested` review.
- The issue is at `stage:pr` and has no `needs-human` label.
- `gates.merge` in workflow.yaml is `auto`.
It prints the merge SHA for the `[merged]` comment. Add `Bash(pr-merge *)` to the allowlist; keep the `gh pr merge*` deny. pr-manager's merge step calls the wrapper.

## Out of scope
- Enabling GitHub auto-merge or changing branch protection.
- Letting any other role merge.

## Notes for the coder
- Reuse the structure of `~/.local/bin/beads-sync-merge` (jq-free `q` helper, `die`, trunk detection).
- `~/.claude/agents/pr-manager.md` step 6 (lines ~46-48) is outside the repo; list the edit in the PR description. Store the script in `scripts/` in the repo and symlink/copy it into `~/.local/bin`.
- Repo is PUBLIC; be strict, fail closed on any API error.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Script refuses a draft PR, a PR with a failing/pending check, a PR with conflicts, a PR with an unresolved thread, and a non-trunk base (each a tested case with the exact error)
- [ ] Script merges a green, non-draft PR and prints its SHA
- [ ] `gh pr merge` run directly by an agent is still denied
- [ ] pr-manager merges a green PR end to end with no permission prompt
- [ ] With `gates.merge: human` the script refuses

title: Committed settings.json allowlist plus destructive-command guard hook
description:
## Problem / goal
Permissions live only in uncommitted per-worktree `.claude/settings.local.json` copies, and they've drifted. Findings (2026-10-04):
- **The coder's worktree has no settings file at all:** no allows, so prompts, and no force-push deny.
- **The main checkout's file was invalid JSON** (a stray brace after a hand-added `pr-merge` line). It was hotfixed by the pm on 2026-10-04, but nothing validates these files.
- **The force-push glob denies (`git push * --force*`) also match `--force-with-lease`.** sim-ikx.4 needs that on task branches, and a deny always beats an allow.
- **No hooks.**

## Behaviour
- **Committed `.claude/settings.json`** (so every worktree and the main checkout get it):
  - **Allows** what every role uses:
    - cargo build/check/test/clippy/fmt, `trunk build*` / `trunk serve*`
    - `br *`
    - git `status/diff/log/show/fetch/add/commit/push/rebase/checkout/switch/branch/worktree/stash list/range-diff/merge --ff-only`
    - `gh pr *` (except merge) and `gh run *`, `gh api` GET reads
    - `scripts/native-run.sh*`, `scripts/window-close.py*`, `scripts/web-smoke.sh*`, `xdotool *`, `import *`
    - `python3 scripts/*`, `uv run *`, `curl -s* http://127.0.0.1:8188/*` and `http://localhost:9090/*`
  - **Denies:** `gh pr merge*`.
  - **Hook:** registers the guard as a PreToolUse Bash hook.
  - **No** force-push globs (the hook handles force pushes) and **no** `pr-merge` allow.
- **Guard hook `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.py`** (stdlib Python). It reads the hook JSON from stdin and splits compound commands (`&&`, `;`, `|`, `cd … &&` prefixes). It blocks with exit code 2 and a clear one-line reason:
  - `git push` with `--force`, `-f` or a `+refspec`, **anywhere**
  - `git push --force-with-lease` / `--force-if-includes` when the target, or the current branch, is `master`/`main`
  - `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f*`, and whole-tree discards (`git checkout -- .`, `git restore .`). Single files stay allowed: `git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl` is part of the pm's safe-pull procedure.
  - `rm -r`/`rm -rf` on `/`, `~`/`$HOME`, any `.git` or `.beads` path, or any path outside the current repo/worktree root and outside `/tmp` / `$TMPDIR`
  - `br delete`

  It **allows** `git push --force-with-lease origin <task-branch>` on a non-trunk branch, and every ordinary git/cargo/br/gh command.
- **Per-worktree `settings.local.json` keeps only role- or machine-specific rules:**
  - The pr-manager keeps `pr-merge *`.
  - The main checkout drops the obsolete `beads-sync-merge *` (beads sync is trunk-direct now).
  - Force-push globs are removed everywhere (now the hook's job).
  - The coder gets no local file, or a minimal one.
- **Validation:** a check (in the hook's test suite and in CI's `test` job, or a tiny script) parses `.claude/settings.json` as JSON. Local files are git-excluded, so the pm validates them by hand after edits.

## Out of scope
The global `~/.claude/settings.json` and permission modes (`AGENT_TEAM_PERMISSION_MODE`), and loosening any write permission beyond the repo.

## Notes for the coder
- **Today's local files:** main checkout (13 allow / 5 deny incl. `pr-merge`, `beads-sync-merge`), tester/reviewer/concept-artist (11/5), pr-manager (12/4), coder (none). The asset-producer worktree path from agent-team doesn't currently exist.
- Settings precedence: a deny in any file wins. Make sure no leftover local force-push deny blocks `--force-with-lease`.
- **sim-ikx.4 depends on this task** (the coder's force-with-lease after rebasing).
- **Tests:** a table of sample commands → expected block/allow for the hook, covering every rule above, both force-push variants, compound commands, and the pm's `git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl`.
- **Handoff:** the repo side (settings.json, hook, tests, docs/agent-workflow.md note) is a normal PR. The local-file edits in each worktree are out of git: apply them with `.bak-sim-ikx.3` backups and list them in the PR body.
- Touched: .claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/**, docs/agent-workflow.md, CI test job (optional), <worktrees>/.claude/settings.local.json
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] .claude/settings.json is committed, parses as JSON (checked by a test/CI step), and Claude Code starts in a worktree with no settings errors
- [x] Hook test table passes: blocks git push --force / -f / +refspec, --force-with-lease to master, reset --hard, clean -f, checkout -- ., restore ., rm -rf on /, ~, .git, .beads and outside the repo/tmp, br delete; allows --force-with-lease on a task branch, git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl, and ordinary git/cargo/br/gh commands, including inside && chains
- [ ] A blocked command shows a one-line reason in the agent's transcript (shown once live)
- [x] gh pr merge is denied for every role; pr-merge works for the pr-manager and is not allowed for the other roles
- [ ] The coder worktree is covered (committed settings apply); a coder → tester run on a small issue produces zero permission prompts (count recorded)
- [x] Local settings.local.json files hold only role/machine rules, no force-push globs, no beads-sync-merge; every local file parses as JSON; .bak-sim-ikx.3 backups exist

title: Fewer bounces: rebase before handoff and avoid overlapping parallel issues
description:
## Problem / goal
Bounces cost the most round-trips in the pipeline. Measured 2026-10-04:
- **30 `[bounce]`s across 116 issues** (24 issues bounced).
- **23 of 30 (77%) are master conflicts.**
- **Who bounced:** reviewer 15, **pr-manager 12**, tester 2. Most conflicts appear *after* handoff, while a PR waits in review/test/pr and another PR lands on master.
- The conflicting files are spread out (bricks/mod.rs, main.rs, CLAUDE.md, manifest.toml…): no single hotspot to restructure.

So the fix is to **avoid overlapping work** and **make conflict bounces cheap**, plus catch conflicts that already exist at handoff.

## Behaviour
1. **Rebase before handoff (coder):**
   - Before moving to `stage:review`: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/<base>`, re-run the project checks, then push.
   - A conflict the coder can't resolve cleanly → `[escalate]`, never push a broken state.
   - Rebasing an already-pushed branch needs `git push --force-with-lease` on the coder's own task branch only. Check the role's settings allow exactly that; plain `--force` stays denied.
2. **Touched files in every spec (pm):**
   - "Notes for the coder" gets a **`Touched:`** line listing the files/modules the task is expected to change (paths or globs, e.g. `src/bricks/**, src/main.rs, CLAUDE.md`).
   - Specs without it (older ones): the coder writes its own estimate into the `[claim]` comment.
3. **Never start overlapping work (coder), user decision: always wait.**
   - When picking a `stage:ready` issue, compare its `Touched:` set with the changed files of every open PR at `stage:review`, `stage:test` or `stage:pr` (`gh pr diff <n> --name-only`).
   - If they intersect, **don't claim it**. Take the next non-overlapping ready issue.
   - If every ready issue overlaps, the coder **waits**. Its one-line tick report says so, e.g. `waiting: sim-x overlaps PR #N (src/main.rs)`, so the idle reason is visible.
   - Rework (bounced issues) is exempt: rework-first still applies.
4. **Light re-check for rebase-only reworks, user decision: yes.**
   - When a rework only resolves a master conflict (no logic change), the coder marks its `[handoff]` comment **`[rebase-only]`** and includes `git range-diff <old-base>..<old-head> <new-base>..<new-head>`.
   - **Reviewer:** reviews only the conflict resolution in the range-diff. Any logic change beyond resolving the conflict → full review as usual.
   - **Tester:** skips the re-test when CI is green on the new head and no resolved file lies in an area named in the acceptance criteria; otherwise re-tests only the affected AC.
   - Both note `[rebase-only]` in their pass comments.
5. **Measure:** during queue hygiene, the pm records the bounce count and causes for the next ~15 closed issues and compares it to the 30/116 (23 conflicts) baseline. Count `[bounce]` comments and classify conflict/rebase vs other, as in this spec's baseline.

## Out of scope
Merge queues, changing branch protection, serialising all work to one agent, and auto-resolving conflicts in later roles.

## Notes for the coder
- **Out-of-repo edits** (not in git; edit in place with `.bak-sim-ikx.4` backups and list the diffs in the PR description, as sim-ikx.1 did): `~/.claude/agents/coder.md`, `reviewer.md`, `tester.md`, `pm.md` (spec template: `Touched:` line), `~/.claude/skills/beads-queue/SKILL.md` (claim rule, `[rebase-only]` tag), and the role `.claude/settings.local.json` files in the worktrees (force-with-lease for the coder only).
- **In repo:** `docs/agent-workflow.md` describes rules 1–4. Normal PR.
- Touched: ~/.claude/agents/{coder,reviewer,tester,pm}.md, ~/.claude/skills/beads-queue/SKILL.md, docs/agent-workflow.md, <worktrees>/.claude/settings.local.json
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] coder.md has the fetch → rebase → re-check → push step before stage:review, and escalation on an unresolved conflict; the coder's settings allow git push --force-with-lease on its task branch and still deny plain --force
- [ ] pm.md's spec template has a 'Touched:' line in Notes for the coder
- [ ] Overlap test: with an open stage:review PR touching src/main.rs, a ready issue whose Touched: includes src/main.rs is not claimed while a non-overlapping ready issue is; with only overlapping issues ready, the coder's tick report says 'waiting: <id> overlaps PR #N (<files>)'
- [ ] Rework items are still taken first even if they overlap
- [ ] A rebase-only rework carries [rebase-only] + range-diff in its handoff; the reviewer's pass comment shows a range-diff-only review; the tester skips or limits the re-test per the rule (shown on one real or staged case)
- [ ] beads-queue SKILL.md documents the overlap rule and the [rebase-only] tag; docs/agent-workflow.md describes rules 1–4; .bak-sim-ikx.4 files exist
- [ ] After ~15 more closed issues, the pm posts the bounce count and causes compared to the 30/116 (23 conflict) baseline

So rule 1's force-with-lease works once ikx.3 lands. There's no need to add a force-with-lease allow to the coder's local settings; the committed settings.json + hook cover it.

title: Web smoke test: load the wasm build in headless Chromium
description:
## Problem / goal
The web build is only compile-checked (`trunk build`). Wasm-only breakage (asset paths, panics at startup or on entering a level, loader errors) passes CI, deploys to GitHub Pages and is only found by hand.

## Behaviour
- **CI job `web-smoke`** (needs `web`):
  - Downloads the `web-dist` artifact (already built with `--public-url /<repo-name>/`; no rebuild).
  - Serves it under that same prefix and loads it in headless Chromium via Playwright, with software WebGL2 (SwiftShader / `--use-angle=swiftshader`, since GitHub runners have no GPU).
- **Phase 1, menu:**
  - Wait for the game's `steelbreak-ready` event (`#splash` gets `.done`). Timeout 90 s.
  - `#splash.failed` or a timeout fails the test.
  - Take screenshot `menu.png`.
- **Phase 2, level:**
  - Start a run with the keyboard (focus the canvas; the menu's focused Start button activates on Space/Enter).
  - Wait for a new web-only event **`steelbreak-level-started`**.
  - Let it run about 5 s. Take screenshot `level.png`.
- **Failure conditions,** throughout both phases:
  - any console `error`
  - any console message containing `panic`
  - any uncaught exception or unhandled rejection
  - any failed request (HTTP ≥ 400 or network error)

  Exception: entries in a small committed allowlist (`scripts/web-smoke.allow`, one regex per line, each with a comment saying why).
- **Artifacts:** both screenshots and the console log are uploaded, even on failure.
- **Deploy gate:** `deploy-pages` needs `web-smoke`, so a build that fails the smoke test is never deployed.
- **Local run:** `scripts/web-smoke.sh [dist-dir]` runs the same check. It builds with `trunk build --release --public-url /breakout/` if no dist is given, and writes screenshots to a temp/output dir. It uses `/usr/bin/chromium` when present, and gets Playwright without a global install (e.g. pinned `npx playwright-core` via the mise Node, or a uv-run Python script).
- **Not a required check yet:** `web-smoke` is not added to the branch-protection required checks. A follow-up beads task is filed to add it after 7 days of stable runs.

## Game change (small, wasm-only)
Dispatch `steelbreak-level-started` on `window` when `LevelStarted` fires, next to the existing `steelbreak-ready` dispatch in `src/web_splash.rs` (or a sibling), cfg-gated to wasm32. Native is unaffected.

## Out of scope
Driving real gameplay (serving the ball, hitting bricks), visual regression/diffing, audio output, and making the check required now.

## Notes for the coder
- **Today's state:**
  - `web` job: `trunk build --release --public-url "/${{ github.event.repository.name }}/"` → `actions/upload-artifact@v4` name `web-dist`. `deploy-pages` needs `web` today.
  - The loader is `web/loader.js` + `index.html` (`#splash`, `.done` / `.failed`).
  - The `push` trigger has `paths-ignore: ['.beads/**']` (sim-ikx.1). Keep it.
- **Local machine is Omarchy (Arch):** `/usr/bin/chromium` exists, but **Playwright is not installed** (the old draft assumed it was). Node and uv are available via mise. In CI: `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` or equivalent, cached.
- **Startup time:** SwiftShader is slow, so give the menu phase a generous timeout. Keep the job under about 4 minutes.
- **Benign noise:** expect some (e.g. favicon 404, AudioContext autoplay notices). Use the allowlist, not a looser matcher.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] scripts/web-smoke.sh passes on current master locally and writes menu.png and level.png (level.png shows the first level's board)
- [x] The web-smoke CI job passes on a PR, takes < ~4 min, and uploads menu.png, level.png and the console log as artifacts
- [x] deploy-pages needs web-smoke (visible in build.yml and in the run graph of a master push)
- [x] Throwaway branch with a broken asset path (e.g. a renamed sprite or level file): the job fails on the failed request and still uploads artifacts
- [ ] Throwaway branch with a deliberate panic on entering a level: phase 1 passes, phase 2 fails on the panic
- [x] Throwaway branch with a startup panic: phase 1 fails (splash .failed or a panic message)
- [x] scripts/web-smoke.allow exists with a comment per entry; the job doesn't pass because of an over-broad pattern (each entry matches one known message)
- [x] steelbreak-level-started is dispatched only on wasm; native builds and cargo test are unaffected
- [x] A follow-up beads task exists to add web-smoke to required checks after 7 stable days
- [x] Documented in docs/agent-workflow.md and scripts/README.md (how the tester runs it locally)

title: Fresh-eyes checks: pm polish pass via a spec-reviewer subagent, coder self-review via /code-review low
description:
## Problem / goal
Borrow two cheap ideas from the Agent Flywheel:
- **Polish issues before release.** Planning tokens are the cheapest place to buy correctness.
- **A fresh-eyes self-review before handoff.**

In both cases the check runs **in a separate context** from the one that wrote the work (the user's
choice, 2026-10-06), so it isn't the author grading itself.

## Behaviour
**1. pm polish pass, using a new `spec-reviewer` subagent**
- **New agent `~/.claude/agents/spec-reviewer.md`:**
  - Read-only: `br show/list/search`, Read, Grep and Glob. No writes to beads or files.
  - A cheaper model (sonnet).
  - Input: the issue ids just drafted. Output: one JSON block of findings per issue.
  - **Each finding has:** the issue id, the criterion number (if it's about a criterion), a `kind`
  and a one-line suggestion. The kinds are:
    - `untestable`: no concrete command, UI action, value or output to observe.
    - `missing-section`: Problem / Behaviour / Out of scope / Notes, or an empty
    acceptance_criteria.
    - `overlap`: duplicates or collides with an open issue (give its id).
    - `dependency`: a missing or contradictory `br dep`.
    - `oversized`: probably more than about 400 changed lines, so it should be split.
    - `contradiction`: behaviour vs. a criterion, or vs. another issue.
- **Tool hints:** it runs `br lint <ids>` and `bv --robot-suggest --suggest-type duplicate` and
`--suggest-type dependency`, filtered to the drafted ids.
  - It treats their output **as hints only**: bv's keyword-matched dependencies are often wrong
  (e.g. it re-suggested sim-7bu.4 → .2, which was removed on purpose).
  - It ignores bv's label suggestions.
- **pm.md:** a new step between "Create" and "Approval gate":
  - Spawn spec-reviewer on the new ids.
  - Fix what's real, or note why a finding doesn't apply.
  - Post `[polish] found=<n> fixed=<m> — <one line>` on each issue.
  - Then go to the approval gate as before.
  - One polish round per batch; it never blocks the gate.

**2. Coder self-review with `/code-review low`**
- **coder.md:** a new step after "Checks" pass and before "Push & draft PR":
  - Run the built-in `code-review` skill **at low effort, explicitly** (`low`; the skill otherwise
  reuses the last level) on the task branch's diff against its base.
  - For in-place edits outside git (skills, agent files), review `diff -u <file>.bak <file>`
  instead.
  - Fix the real findings. If any code changed, re-run `checks:`.
  - Post `[self-review] found=<n> fixed=<m> skipped=<k> — <one line; reason for each skip>`.
  - It isn't a gate: findings may be skipped with a reason, and the reviewer still does the real
  review.
- **beads-queue skill:** add `[polish]` and `[self-review]` to its comment-tag list.

## Out of scope
- Multi-model plan synthesis.
- More than one polish or self-review round per issue.
- Making either step a blocking gate.
- Changes to the reviewer or tester roles.

## Notes for the coder
- **Every edit is outside the repo:** `~/.claude/agents/pm.md`, `coder.md`, the new
`spec-reviewer.md`, and `~/.claude/skills/beads-queue/SKILL.md`.
  - Make them in place, with `.bak-sim-ikx.7` copies first, and no PR (as in sim-ikx.1 and
  sim-4ws.1).
  - Put the diffs in a `[handoff]` comment.
- The pm and coder sessions that are already running only pick up the change when restarted
(`agent-team down/up`). Say so in the handoff.
- Match the style of the existing agent files: frontmatter with `name`, `description`, `tools`,
`model`, then short numbered steps.
- **Seeded test for criterion 1:** create a throwaway issue (`--labels test-fixture`, no stage
label) with `- [ ] code is clean`, no Out of scope section, and a title that duplicates an open
issue. Run spec-reviewer on it, paste the JSON into a comment on sim-ikx.7, then close the fixture

title: Make Lua scripting (bevy_mod_scripting/lua54) native-only so the wasm build compiles
description:
## Problem
bevy_mod_scripting 0.21 with the `lua54` feature is currently an unconditional dependency in Cargo.toml. `lua54` builds mlua's bundled Lua C sources, which do not compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so `trunk build` (the primary distribution target) and the CI `web` job / GitHub Pages deploy fail.

## Approach
Same pattern as the existing avian2d/getrandom target gating (no gameplay changes):
1. Cargo.toml: move `bevy_mod_scripting = { version = "0.21.0", features = ["lua54"] }` out of `[dependencies]` into `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`.
2. src/main.rs: gate `mod script_manager;` and `.add_plugins(script_manager::ScriptPlugin)` with `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` (or give ScriptPlugin a no-op wasm impl so main.rs stays ungated).
3. Optional: also put it behind a Cargo feature (e.g. `scripting`, default-on) so native builds can opt out with `--no-default-features`. Note that a feature alone isn't enough: trunk would still enable it for wasm unless the dependency is also target-gated.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` (native) still includes and runs ScriptPlugin/BMSPlugin.
- `trunk build --release` succeeds and the game runs in the browser without scripting.
- CI `native` and `web` jobs are green on master, and the Pages deploy succeeds (https://frederickbrock.github.io/breakout/).
- CLAUDE.md "wasm enablement" note updated to mention scripting is native-only.
