title: Web loading screen: Steelbreak splash with download progress, error state, title, favicon and preview card
description:
## Problem / goal
On the web build (GitHub Pages) the page stays completely black while the game downloads and starts. Today that's about 20 MB gzipped, 18 s on a good connection. A player who doesn't know to wait assumes the game is broken. Show a branded loading screen with real progress, a clear error if loading fails, and a page that looks finished (title, icon, link preview).

## Behaviour
- **Splash, shown instantly:** the page's first paint is a Steelbreak splash, never black. It shows:
  - the key art (dimmed or cropped so the text reads) with the title **STEELBREAK**,
  - a progress bar with `12.3 / 20.5 MB`,
  - a status line,
  - a controls hint: `Mouse or ← → to move · Click / Space to launch · P to pause`.
- **Progress:** the bar tracks the wasm download. If the server doesn't report a total size, the bar switches to an animated indeterminate state with MB loaded so far (never stuck at 0%).
- **Status:** the line reads `Downloading…`, then `Starting…` once the wasm is compiled and Bevy is booting and loading its assets.
- **Hand-over:** the splash fades out only when the game has drawn its main menu. There's no black gap between the splash and the game.
- **Failure:** if the download or start fails (network error, unsupported browser or no WebGL2), the splash shows a readable message (`Couldn't start the game: <reason>`) and a **Reload** button, instead of hanging or going black.
- **Page polish:**
  - The tab title is `Steelbreak`.
  - A favicon, e.g. the steel ball or an emitter crop. Any small Steelbreak icon works.
  - Open Graph and Twitter card meta: title, one-line description and the key art as the preview image, with an absolute URL on `https://frederickbrock.github.io/breakout/`. A shared link then shows the art.
- It works on the GitHub Pages sub-path (`/breakout/`) and under `trunk serve` at `/`.

## Out of scope
- Making the download smaller (sibling P2 task).
- A click-to-launch gate and audio unlock.
- The native window title.
- In-game loading screens between levels.

## Notes for the coder
- `index.html` is tiny today (a trunk `rel="rust"` link, `copy-dir assets` and CSS). trunk 0.21 supports `data-initializer="loader.js"` on the rust link, with hooks `onStart`, `onProgress({ current, total })`, `onComplete`, `onSuccess(wasm)` and `onFailure(error)`. Use it for the bar and the error state. The wasm is served gzip-encoded, so `total` can be missing or refer to the compressed size. Handle both.
- "Game drew its main menu": the splash must stay up until Bevy has actually rendered, because asset loading happens after wasm start. Suggested approach: a tiny **wasm-only** system (cfg `target_arch = "wasm32"`, via `web-sys`/`js-sys`, no gameplay change) that, on the first frame in `AppState::MainMenu`, sets a DOM flag or calls a JS function that fades and removes the splash. The splash should also be removed on `onFailure`. Keep the native build untouched.
- Key art source: `art/steelbreak_keyart.png` (1920×1080, 2.4 MB) is **untracked** in the main checkout (`/home/frede/projects/breakout/art/`). Don't ship 2.4 MB on the critical path. Commit a compressed web copy, e.g. `web/splash.jpg` at 1280 wide and ≤ 300 KB, and copy it with a trunk `rel="copy-file"` or `copy-dir`. The same image or a 1200×630 crop can serve as `og:image`.
- Keep the CSS and JS inline or in small files. The splash must render before any large download starts.
- The page background stays `#080b0f` (theme void) so the splash→game hand-over doesn't flash.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] On a throttled connection (DevTools "Fast 4G"), opening the Pages URL shows the Steelbreak splash (art, title, controls hint) within about 1 s; the page is never plain black
- [ ] During download the bar advances and shows MB loaded. With the total unknown it shows an indeterminate animation plus MB loaded, never stuck at 0.
- [ ] The status changes from `Downloading…` to `Starting…`, and the splash fades out only once the main menu is visible, with no black gap
- [ ] Blocking the `.wasm` request in DevTools shows `Couldn't start the game: …` with a Reload button, and Reload retries
- [x] The tab shows the title `Steelbreak` and a favicon
- [ ] A link-preview checker (e.g. opengraph.xyz) on the Pages URL shows the key art, the title and the description
- [x] Works both under `trunk serve` (`/`) and on GitHub Pages (`/breakout/`); no 404s in the network tab
- [ ] The native `cargo run` is unaffected; `cargo test`, clippy and `trunk build --release` pass

title: Shrink the web wasm download (wasm-opt, strip, size-tuned wasm-only cargo profile)
description:
## Problem / goal
The web build ships a **132 MB** wasm (measured on GitHub Pages 2026-09-30: 20.5 MB gzipped over the wire, about 18 s to download). `index.html` disables wasm-opt (`data-wasm-opt="0"`), and the release build appears to carry debug info. Make the download much smaller so the game starts much sooner, without touching native builds or gameplay.

## Behaviour
- The deployed wasm is much smaller: target at least **50% less** over the wire than 20.5 MB gzipped, and ideally a few MB. Record raw and gzipped sizes, before and after, in the PR.
- The web game plays exactly as before (menus, physics, particles, sprites, levels).
- Native `cargo run` and `cargo build --release` behave and perform as before.
- CI still builds and deploys Pages. Note the CI time before and after (size optimisation and LTO are slower). Keep it reasonable.

## Out of scope
- The loading screen (sibling task).
- Splitting or streaming the wasm.
- Asset compression (assets are 1.9 MB).
- Dropping Bevy features to save size. Suggest it in the PR, but only do it if it's risk-free.

## Notes for the coder
- Levers, most likely first:
  - `strip` / `debug = false`
  - `opt-level = "z"` or `"s"`
  - `lto = true`
  - `codegen-units = 1`
  - `panic = "abort"`, if Bevy on wasm is fine with it
  - trunk `data-wasm-opt="z"` (binaryen)
- **Don't slow down native release:** put the size settings in a dedicated cargo profile (e.g. `[profile.wasm-release] inherits = "release"`) and point trunk at it (`data-cargo-profile="wasm-release"` on the rust link, or `--cargo-profile` in CI). Check how the `trunk build --release` in `.github/workflows/build.yml` (with `--public-url`) picks it up.
- wasm-opt can need `--enable-bulk-memory` / `--enable-nontrapping-float-to-int` for current Rust wasm output. Check trunk 0.21's `data-wasm-opt-params`.
- Measure with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{size_download}'` (raw) and `curl -sI -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip'` (wire), or DevTools.

- [x] PR records the wasm size before and after (raw and gzipped). The gzipped size after is ≤ 10.25 MB (at least 50% below 20.5 MB).

- [ ] Web smoke test (`trunk serve --release` or Pages): main menu → start → serve → break bricks, including an explosive and a particle effect → pause → game over all work as before, with no console errors
- [x] Native `cargo build --release` uses unchanged settings (the size profile applies only to the web build); `cargo run` plays as before
- [x] CI's web job still passes and deploys; PR notes its duration before and after
- [x] `cargo test`, clippy and `trunk build --release` pass

title: Background energy: breathing glow and rare lightning strikes in the parallax nebula (animated mask)
description:
## Problem / goal
User, 2026-10-03, on the sim-rdl.10 concepts: "the lightning in the background could be particles or image color mask that bring the background alive. Imagine that with some heavy industrial music in the background." The parallax (sim-rdl.9) is static art drifting slowly. This task brings the nebula's lightning alive with an animated **glow/lightning mask**: a slow breathing glow plus rare, sudden strikes. It stays ambient and never competes with gameplay.

## Behaviour
- **Glow layer:** a lightning/glow mask, aligned pixel for pixel with the L1 cloud layer, drawn on top of L1 and below L2. It drifts with L1: same speed (16 px/s down), same wrap, always in register with the clouds' forks. It's clipped to the well, like every parallax layer.
- **Breathing:** the mask's brightness rises and falls slowly and continuously. The period is about 4–6 s; it runs between about 15% and 35% of full brightness.
- **Strikes:** every 6–15 s (random interval), a strike runs: a quick flicker of 2–4 bright flashes over about 0.3–0.6 s, up to full brightness, then a fade back to breathing over about 1 s. Intervals and flash counts vary, so it never feels like a metronome.
- **Calm brick area:** at peak flash, the bricks, ball and HUD still read clearly. The peak brightness is capped so that the composited brick area stays under the style.md contrast cap. The art dims the forks behind the brick rows; the code caps the overall maximum.
- **Colour:** the mask is white/greyscale, tinted in code by one theme constant (`theme::NEBULA_GLOW`). Its value is taken from the picked sim-rdl.10 art's lightning colour. Until that art lands, use a cream-white placeholder.
- **Ambient only (user):** it doesn't react to gameplay. Like the parallax, it runs on real time, on every screen, including pause and game over, and through restarts.
- **Missing mask:** no glow layer and no panic; the parallax is unchanged.
- **Placeholder (until the sim-rdl.10 mask lands):** the coder commits `assets/parallax/space_l1_glow.png` at the contract size, with a few outlined forked bolts on transparent. The producer's mask overwrites it later with no code change.
- Works on web.

## Asset contract (added to sim-rdl.10)
`assets/parallax/space_l1_glow.png`:
- 1440×2160 RGBA: white, with alpha = glow intensity, transparent elsewhere
- aligned pixel for pixel with `space_l1.png` and vertically seamless, like it
- at most 1 MB

## Out of scope
- Particle sparks or arcs along the forks: a possible follow-up if the mask alone feels too static.
- Reacting to blasts or other game events.
- Music sync: a future hook once the game has audio.
- Animating L0, L2 or the planet.
- The art itself (sim-rdl.10).

## Notes for the coder
- Builds on sim-rdl.9's `src/parallax.rs`:
  - Add the glow as one more entry in the `LAYERS` table, with L1's speed and a z between L1 and L2. It reuses `tile_offset` / `tile_slices` / `crop_to_well`.
  - Add a per-layer `glow: bool` (or a separate `GlowLayer` marker) for the intensity animation.
- **Intensity as a pure fn** (e.g. `fn glow_intensity(t, &StrikeSchedule) -> f32`):
  - breathing plus a strike envelope;
  - the schedule comes from a seeded rng, refilled as strikes pass;
  - unit-test the bounds (never above the cap, never below the breathing floor), that strikes happen at the scheduled times, and that it's smooth outside flashes.
- Drive it with `Time<Real>`, like the drift. Apply it as the sprite's colour alpha, multiplied with the tint.
  - Alpha blending of a white-on-transparent mask is enough.
  - An additive `Material2d` is optional, only if it looks clearly better and works on webgl2.
- Docs: the `parallax.rs` `//!` doc, plus one line in the CLAUDE.md cross-cutting parallax note.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `cargo run`: on the main menu, the nebula's lightning visibly breathes (slow brightening and dimming) and, within about 15 s, a strike flickers 2–4 times and fades back
- [ ] The glow stays in register with the cloud layer's forks while drifting, including across a wrap (no slipping or seam)
- [ ] Over about 2 minutes, strike intervals vary (not evenly spaced); between strikes, the glow never drops to fully off
- [ ] Screenshot at the peak of a strike during play: the bricks, ball and HUD stay clearly readable; the brick area stays calm
- [ ] It keeps animating on the pause menu and the game-over screen, and through Play again
- [ ] Renaming `assets/parallax/space_l1_glow.png` and restarting: no glow, no panic, the parallax is otherwise unchanged
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the breathing and strikes in the browser
- [ ] `cargo test` includes unit tests for `glow_intensity` (cap and floor bounds, strike timing from a seeded schedule); clippy and `trunk build` pass; the placeholder mask is 1440×2160 RGBA and at most 1 MB

title: SDXL prompt hygiene on the comfy path: no prose feedback, no negations in positive tags
description:
## Found while reworking sim-7bu.1 (05:50 [spec] amendment, 'flag, don't widen')
The concept-artist agent (step 5) already builds **comfy** prompts from style.md's SDXL tag preamble + subject comma tags, so the main path is tag-form. Prose still reaches CLIP in these places:
- **Rework rounds**: art-pipeline 'Prompt building' step 4 appends *the user's feedback verbatim*. On comfy that is prose, and it gets diluted across CLIP's 77-token chunks; 'no X' in feedback adds X.
- **art-pipeline 'Prompt building' step 3** lists isolation constraints as negations (no text, no border, no shadow on the background, no scenery) and the #FF00FF key. That's fine for Gemini, but the skill gives no SDXL variant, so it relies on the agent file's override.
- **style.md SDXL isolation tags** contain 'no scenery' (positive). Being A/B'd in sim-7bu.1, which may drop it.
- **artgen** passes whatever prompt file it gets; nothing warns on prose or negation in a comfy prompt (e.g. a lint: sentences / 'no ' tokens / hex codes / >75 tokens).
- **ref kind** (backend_by_workflow ref: comfy): check that the ref prompt path also uses tags.

## Ask (for the pm to spec)
Tag-form rules for comfy rework feedback (translate it to tags plus negative additions), an SDXL section in art-pipeline Prompt building, and an optional artgen prompt lint for --backend comfy.

Source: sim-7bu.1 / PR #115.

title: Brick neighbour combos: adjacent materials produce effects and power-ups (e.g. fire + glass)
description:
## The ask (user, 2026-09-30), very high-level idea for an epic
Bricks behave according to which bricks are next to them. Instead of power-ups being random, combinations of neighbouring materials produce effects. Example: a **fire (explosive) brick next to a glass (shield) brick** results in a power-up that does X.

Draft placeholder: the pm interviews the user before this is broken into tasks.

## Facts found (master, 2026-09-30)
- Every brick has a `BrickCell { row, col }` and a `BrickClass`. The explosive module already resolves neighbourhoods on a `BrickCell`-keyed grid snapshot (`resolve_blast`: 4-orthogonal and 8-around), so a neighbour lookup exists as a pattern.
- Power-ups currently come only from reactor bricks. `attach_reactor_power_ups` picks a kind from the weighted `PowerUpSpawner` on `RestartGame`. New power-ups follow the self-contained plugin pattern (`powerups/super_sizer.rs`).
- Levels (sim-a7k) are hand-authored grids, so a level designer could place combos deliberately.
- The behaviour outlines (sim-rdl.7.4, sim-8j0) are the visual language for "this brick does something"; combos may need their own cue.

## Open questions for the interview
- When does a combo trigger: when one of the pair breaks, when both break, or passively while they're adjacent (auras)?
- What counts as adjacent: 4-orthogonal or 8-around?
- The combo table: which material pairs (or triples) give which effect? Does it replace reactor power-ups or add to them?
- How does the player learn the combos (visual link between the pair, a codex, the sector card)?
- Should the random board generate combos on purpose (a guaranteed number per board)?
- Relationship to the brick-rearranging power-up idea (filed alongside): rearranging could create or break combos.

title: Refactor: split main.rs by feature, move tests to sibling files, slim CLAUDE.md (reduce merge conflicts)
description:
## Problem / goal
Merge conflicts keep growing as the code grows. PR #34 (sim-pdp.1) was bounced by the pr-manager for a real conflict after #32/#33 merged, with conflicts in `src/main.rs`, `src/bricks/*.rs` and `CLAUDE.md`. The causes, measured on master at 86489d4:
- `src/main.rs` is 1,737 lines. About 955 of them are `test_support` and `mod tests`, and 8 of the last 15 merged PRs touched it. Ball, paddle, collision, run start, HUD and the shared test helpers all live in the one file.
- `CLAUDE.md` was touched by 9 of the last 15 PRs, because every PR documents itself in the same paragraphs.
- Inline `mod tests` blocks: parallel branches each add tests at the end of the same block, so they conflict even when the features are unrelated (seen in #34).

The user asked for a behaviour-neutral refactor. It lands after all current in-flight work and before the next story is picked up.

## Behaviour
No gameplay, visual or API change. The same tests pass, with the same count, before and after.
1. **Split `src/main.rs` by feature** into modules, for example `ball.rs` (movement, serve/anchor, approach), `paddle.rs` (movement, pieces), `collision.rs` (`on_ball_collision` and the brick events), `run.rs` (`start_run`/`end_run`, score/lives, HUD) and `test_support.rs`. `main.rs` keeps `main()`, `add_game` and module wiring only.
2. **Move each module's tests to a sibling file**: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` with the body in `<module>/tests.rs`, so tests keep private access. At minimum do this for `main.rs` (now split), `bricks/explosive.rs`, `powerups/mod.rs`, `menu/mod.rs`, `bricks/mod.rs` and `sprites.rs`. Also apply it to any module over about 150 lines that has inline tests.
3. **Move module details from `CLAUDE.md` into each module's own `//!` doc comment.** `CLAUDE.md` keeps commands, conventions, the cross-cutting mechanisms, and a short module index with one line per module that points to the file. New modules add one index line, not a paragraph.
4. **Add a short "Conventions for parallel work" section to `CLAUDE.md`**: tests live in `<module>/tests.rs`; new features get their own module and `Plugin` rather than growing `main.rs`; document in the module's `//!` comment.

## Out of scope
Any behaviour change, renaming public items beyond the module move, a lib/bin crate split, and the `tests/` integration-test folder.

## Notes for the coder
- **Sequencing** (the user's instruction): all current in-flight work lands first. That is sim-73n.1, sim-bu6 (#36), sim-rdl.7.4 (#35) and sim-pdp.1 (#34), plus closing sim-rdl.7.2/7.3. The pipeline then pauses, this refactor lands, and the paused stories resume. Dependencies enforce this: this issue is blocked by the in-flight issues, and the not-yet-started code stories are blocked by this issue.
- **pm:** any code story released to `stage:ready` before this issue closes must also get `br dep add <story> <this-issue>`.
- Do it as pure moves where possible, one commit per step, so reviewers can check with `git diff --color-moved` / `git log --follow`.
- Afterwards, anyone with an open branch merges master right away. The hope is that there are none, given the pause.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `src/main.rs` contains only `main()`, `add_game` and module wiring (well under 300 lines); ball, paddle, collision, run/HUD and `test_support` live in their own modules.
- [ ] Every module listed in the spec keeps its tests in a sibling `tests.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`); no inline `mod tests {` block remains in a file over about 150 lines.
- [x] `cargo test` passes with the same number of tests as master before the refactor (record both counts in the PR).
- [x] No behaviour change: the diff is moves plus the required `mod`/`use`/visibility edits (check with `git diff --color-moved`); the native game plays as before (smoke test: serve, break bricks, pause, game over).
- [x] `CLAUDE.md` module section is a one-line-per-module index; the per-module detail now lives in each module's `//!` doc comment; a "Conventions for parallel work" section exists.
- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `trunk build` pass.

title: Particles: integrate bevy_enoki as the VFX layer (brick damage, ball, paddle, explosions)
description:
## Problem / goal
Integrate a 2D particle engine, [bevy_enoki](https://github.com/Lommix/bevy_enoki) 0.7 (Bevy 0.19, CPU-simulated and GPU-instanced, runs on web), as the game's VFX layer. Brick damage is shown by particles instead of images: intact sprites always, with spark/smoke emitters and shatter bursts. The ball, paddle, explosions and shield glass get particles too, and the engine is set up for future exploration.

## Decisions (user, 2026-09-28)
- **Damage style:** a brick always shows its intact sprite. A hit fires a spark burst, a damaged brick emits smoke/sparks scaled by damage, and a break fires a shatter burst. Cracked sprites and colour darkening are dropped.
- **First round:** brick hit/damage/break, ball trail + bounce sparks, paddle impact, explosions + shield deflect.
- **Where:** on trunk, in slices (not an experiment branch).
- **Tuning:** the coder drafts effects in `assets/particles/*.particle.ron` in the Steelbreak palette. The user tunes them live (hot reload, `enoki2d_editor`).

## Children
- .1 Engine foundation + brick damage/break particles (replaces darkening/cracked)
- .2 Ball trail, bounce sparks, paddle impact
- .3 Explosion blasts + shield-glass deflect particles

## Later ideas
Power-up pickup/active glows, sector-clear celebration, hangar ambience (dust, sparks from the trusses), custom `Particle2dMaterial` shaders.

title: Add bevy_enoki and show brick damage/break with particles (replaces darkening and cracked sprites)
description:
## Problem / goal
Add the bevy_enoki particle engine and use it to show brick damage, replacing the colour darkening (and the planned cracked sprites).

## Behaviour
- **Hit:** every hit that damages a brick without breaking it fires a short spark burst (~10–20 particles, ~0.3 s) from the contact point, in the brick class's seam/glow colour (`art/style.md` brick-class table).
- **Damaged state:** a brick below full hits keeps its **intact** sprite and gets a continuous emitter attached: light smoke plus occasional sparks, heavier the more damage it has taken (e.g. tungsten at 2/3 hits smokes lightly, at 1/3 heavily). Regen healing back to full removes the emitter.
- **Break:** destroying a brick fires a shatter burst (~20–40 shards, ~0.6 s, affected by gravity) in the brick's face colour, from the brick's centre.
- **Darkening removed:** the `CRACKED_DARKEN` colour change is removed, and cracked PNGs are not used.
- **Pause and exit:** particles freeze while paused (no motion, no new spawns) and continue on resume. Leaving the run (game over, main menu) removes all particle spawners.
- **Web:** works in the web build (`trunk serve`).
- **Performance:** a live-particle budget (a constant, e.g. 1500) caps continuous emitters, so a board full of damaged bricks can't tank the frame rate on the WSLg software renderer.

## Out of scope
Ball/paddle effects (.2), explosions/shield (.3), custom shaders, deleting the unused cracked PNGs.

## Notes for the coder
- Add `bevy_enoki = "0.7"`. It pulls `getrandom 0.3` with `wasm_js`; confirm `trunk build` still works with our `.cargo/config.toml` `getrandom_backend` cfg.
- `src/particles/` with its own `Plugin`: `EnokiPlugin` plus a `ParticleEffects` resource of effect handles (`assets/particles/*.particle.ron`).
  - Register it from `main()`, like the sprites plugin, not `add_game`, because the headless `MinimalPlugins` tests have no renderer.
  - Gameplay stays renderer-free: it fires events (e.g. `BrickDamaged { entity, pos, class, hits_left, max_hits }`, the existing `BrickDestroyed`) and the particles plugin observes them. Headless tests assert the events.
- One-shot bursts: spawn `ParticleSpawner` + `ParticleEffectHandle` + `OneShot` (despawn after).
- The damage emitter is a child of the brick, so it despawns with it. Set the emission rate from `hits_left / max_hits`.
- Pause: bevy_enoki ticks on `Time`. Freeze it while `PlayState::Paused` (e.g. toggle `ParticleSpawnerState`, or a scaled time). Pick the least invasive and document it in CLAUDE.md.
- Particles carry `DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame)` or are children of run entities.
- sim-bu6 and sim-fng render intact sprites with an interim darker tint for damage; this task removes that tint.
- Document in CLAUDE.md: effect files, the event → effect mapping, and "gameplay fires events, particles observe".
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Hitting a titanium or tungsten brick without breaking it shows a spark burst at the contact point in that class's glow colour; the brick keeps its intact look (no darkening, no cracked sprite).
- [x] A damaged brick visibly smokes/sparks, and a tungsten brick at 1 hit left smokes more than at 2 hits left.
- [x] Breaking any brick shows a shatter burst of shards in its face colour that fall with gravity.
- [x] A regen brick that heals back to full stops smoking.
- [x] Pausing freezes all particles; resuming continues them. Going to the main menu leaves no particle spawners (test counts `ParticleSpawner` entities after leaving the run).
- [x] Editing `assets/particles/brick_break.particle.ron` while the game runs changes the effect without a restart (native).
- [ ] The web build (`trunk serve`) shows the particles.
- [x] `cargo test` covers the damage/destroy events headlessly; clippy and `trunk build` pass.

title: Particles: ball trail, bounce sparks and paddle impact flare
description:
## Problem / goal
Give the ball and paddle particle feedback.

## Behaviour
- **Ball trail:** while the ball is in flight, a short trail of fading steel-blue (`#a9dcff`) particles follows it (~0.25 s lifetime). No trail while it's anchored on the paddle.
- **Bounce sparks:** every ball bounce off a wall, brick or the paddle fires a small spark burst (~6–10 particles) at the contact point. Bricks already get their own hit/break effects from .1; the bounce spark is extra and subtle.
- **Paddle impact:** when the ball hits the paddle, a cyan emitter-field flare (`#4fd8ff`) spreads along the paddle's top edge from the hit point (~0.3 s). It scales with paddle width (Super-Sizer).
- **Pause:** effects freeze while paused, like .1.

## Out of scope
Ball state variants (heated/charged trails), speed-dependent trail length, screen shake.

## Notes for the coder
- Trail: a continuous spawner as a child of the ball, active only when the ball isn't `Anchored` (sim-rdl.1).
- Bounce/paddle contacts come from `on_ball_collision`. Fire events (`BallBounced { pos, surface }`, `PaddleHit { pos }`) and let the particles plugin observe them. Walls are the static wall entities.
- Reuse .1's plugin, effect registry, budget and pause handling.

title: Particles: explosive blasts per variant and shield-glass deflect glints
description:
## Problem / goal
Make explosions and shield-glass deflects read through particles instead of placeholder quads/flashes.

## Behaviour
Each of the three explosive variants gets its own blast effect, shaped like its rule:
- **Charge:** a round burst of red/orange sparks (`#ff3b3b`, `#ffab4d`) reaching the 8 surrounding cells.
- **Breach:** a "+"-shaped blast shooting along the 4 orthogonal directions.
- **Demolition:** a big, heavier burst with debris and lingering smoke.

In all blasts:
- Chained explosions each play their own blast, in chain order. A small visible delay (~0.05 s per chain step) is fine if it reads better, but gameplay resolution stays in one frame (sim-rdl.7.3).
- **Shield-glass deflect:** a hit that doesn't break the shield throws off a burst of cyan glass glints (`#4fd8ff`, `#b8f6ff`) at the contact point. This replaces the current `ShieldFlash`. Shield glass breaking uses .1's shatter burst in glass colours.
- Effects freeze while paused.

## Out of scope
Screen shake, sound, blast light on the background.

## Notes for the coder
- sim-rdl.7.3 fires an explosion event (`BrickExploded { cell, pos, kind }`). Observe it here; if 7.3 left a placeholder flash, remove it.
- `ShieldFlash` lives in `src/bricks` (7.1). Replace its visual with the particle burst. Keep or remove the component depending on whether gameplay tests need it, and update those tests accordingly.
- Reuse .1's registry, budget and pause handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Destroying a charge, a breach and a demolition brick each shows a distinct blast effect matching its shape (round / plus-shaped / large with smoke).
- [x] A chain of explosions shows a blast at every exploding brick.
- [ ] Hitting shield glass from below shows a burst of cyan glints at the contact point (no flat flash); breaking it from above shows a glass shatter.
- [x] Effects freeze while paused.
- [x] `cargo test` passes (updated for the ShieldFlash change); clippy and `trunk build` pass.
close_reason: Explosive blast and shield-glass glint particles shipped (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/55)

title: Gameplay feel: mouse control, anchored serve, power-up bricks, Steelbreak look
description:
## Problem / goal
Make the game feel like a real Breakout and adopt the Steelbreak look: mouse paddle control (optional, in Settings), a serve where the ball starts anchored on the paddle, power-ups that live inside specific 2-hit bricks instead of dropping at random, and the Steelbreak sci-fi industrial art direction replacing the Enochian one.

## Children
- T1 anchored serve (click / Space to launch)
- T2 mouse paddle control + Settings toggle
- T3 power-up bricks (2 hits, drop on break)
- T4 Steelbreak palette restyle (shapes)
- A1 Steelbreak sprite set (art pipeline)

title: Anchor the ball to the paddle and launch it on click or Space
description:
## Problem / goal
The ball currently spawns mid-screen already moving, at run start and after every lost life. The player should control the serve.

## Behaviour
- At the start of a run and after every lost life (with lives remaining), the ball sits centred on top of the paddle and moves with it (including when Super-Sizer changes the paddle width).
- While anchored, the ball does not move on its own and nothing collides with it.
- Left mouse click or Space launches it upward at `BALL_SPEED`, at 45° toward the side the paddle is currently moving (right if the paddle is still).
- Click / Space while the ball is already in flight does nothing.
- Launch input is ignored while paused.

## Out of scope
Auto-launch timer, a sticky/catch power-up, aiming the launch.

## Notes for the coder
- Add an anchored marker/state on the ball (e.g. `Anchored` component). While anchored keep it out of the simulation (zero `LinearVelocity`, or `RigidBodyDisabled` / kinematic) and snap it to the paddle each frame; gate with `run_if(in_state(PlayState::Playing))`.
- Replace the reset to (0,0) with a velocity in `ball_movement` (`src/main.rs`) and the initial `LinearVelocity` in `spawn_run_entities`.
- `ball_movement` must skip the speed renormalization / min-vertical clamp while anchored (velocity is zero).
- Tests: headless via `test_support::tap(KeyCode::Space)`; mouse via `ButtonInput<MouseButton>` (add a small helper next to `tap` if needed). `MinimalPlugins` test app may need `ButtonInput<MouseButton>` initialised.
- Space is not otherwise bound in gameplay today; P/Esc own pause.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Starting a run shows the ball resting on top of the paddle; moving the paddle carries the ball with it.
- [x] Left-clicking launches the ball upward; pressing Space also launches it.
- [x] After losing a life with lives remaining, the ball is anchored on the paddle again (not mid-screen).
- [x] Clicking or pressing Space while the ball is in flight does not change its trajectory.
- [x] While paused, click and Space do not launch the ball; after resuming it is still anchored.
- [x] `cargo test` includes passing tests for anchored-on-start, launch-on-Space and re-anchor-after-life-lost; `trunk build` succeeds.
close_reason: Merged: ball anchors to paddle and launches on click/Space (PR #11, https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/11)

title: Art: layered graffiti deep-space background for parallax (space, gas clouds, distant planet)
description:
## Subject
A layered deep-space background for the slow-drifting parallax (sim-rdl.9), in the graffiti line-art style: the vast space backdrop, gas clouds, and one planet far off in a corner. It replaces the old hangar idea; there are no trusses, girders or lamps.

## Use in game
Behind the whole playfield and the menus, each layer drifting slowly at its own speed (sim-rdl.9). It must stay dark and calm behind the bricks, ball, paddle and HUD: the background stays under ~12% contrast in the brick area (style.md), and nothing in it may read as a gameplay object. The planet's circle must not look like the ball: it's large, dim and partly cut off by the frame edge.

## Variants (layers, user 2026-10-02)
- **L0 vast space:** near-black void with a star field and faint distant galaxies. Opaque; tiles seamlessly in the drift direction.
- **L1 far gas clouds:** large nebula masses translated into graffiti line art (keyline contours around the cloud forms, flat colour bands instead of photographic wisps, hard highlight strokes on the cloud edges). Transparent; tiles seamlessly.
- **L2 near gas wisps (optional):** thinner, sparser outlined wisps for depth. Transparent; tiles seamlessly; very subtle.
- **L3 distant planet:** one planet in a corner (e.g. lower-right, partly off-frame), far away and dim, outlined and cel-lit from the upper-left key light. Transparent; a single non-tiling image (static, or drifting far slower than the rest). The coder needs to support a non-tiling layer in sim-rdl.9.

## Frames
Static; the motion is done in code.

## Style notes
Graffiti technique from art/style.md (outlines, colour composition, highlights and lighting) with no spray effects. Take the palette from the references' warm/cool split, mapped onto the style palette: rust and orange (warm bounce #ffab4d family), cream, and dusty blue (cold key #a9dcff family) over the void #0a0e15. Keep strong violet and cyan glows out (style.md reserves violet for the reactor and cyan for energy), even though some references use them. Everything is darker and calmer than the references: they set the mood and the cloud shapes, not the brightness.

## References
User mood references (JWST/Hubble-style nebulae, galaxies and deep fields), 10 images:
- source: /mnt/d/reference_images/
- copy (gitignored, served): art/concepts/_refs/sim-rdl.10/ → http://localhost:9090/_refs/sim-rdl.10/ (overview: _overview.png)
Best matches per layer: L0 → OIP-3127668024 (deep field), OIP-1877223488 (galaxies); L1 → OIP-1135991164, OIP-2190757448, OIP-2623612170, OIP-3604196028 (cloud masses and pillars); L2 → OIP-379873680 (filaments). These are mood references only, never shipped and never traced; their licence is unchecked (probably NASA/ESA web thumbnails).
Style: art/style.md, sim-73n.3 r4/v1 (line treatment).

## Asset contract (user, 2026-10-03)
The background only shows inside the **1440×1080 playfield well**: the steel frame panels are opaque and draw on every screen. Art ships at **1x**.
- **Drift: downward.** The tiling layers slide slowly down, as if the playfield climbs through space. So they tile **vertically**: the top edge must continue seamlessly from the bottom edge. They don't need to tile left to right.

| File | Size | Format | Tiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assets/parallax/space_l0.png` | 1440×2160 | opaque | vertical seamless |
| `assets/parallax/space_l1.png` | 1440×2160 | RGBA, transparent | vertical seamless |
| `assets/parallax/space_l2.png` | 1440×2160 | RGBA, transparent, very sparse | vertical seamless |
| `assets/parallax/planet.png` | ~640×640 | RGBA, transparent | none |

- Tiling layers are 2160 tall (two screens), so the repeat isn't obvious at slow speeds.
- **L2 is in scope**, no longer optional.
- **Planet:** a single circle about 480–560 px across, centred in its square canvas with a transparent margin. The code places it lower-right, partly cut off by the right frame edge.
  - It drifts down **near-statically**, far slower than L0. Over many minutes it leaves the bottom and comes back in at the top.
  - The art needs no special treatment for this, but there must be no hard edge or glow halo clipped by the canvas.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Files exist with the exact sizes and formats in the asset contract: `space_l0.png` 1440×2160 opaque; `space_l1.png` and `space_l2.png` 1440×2160 RGBA; `planet.png` about 640×640 RGBA with a transparent margin
- [ ] Each tiling layer stacked twice vertically (top on bottom) shows no visible seam at 1x. `artgen verify` or a stacked preview proves it.
- [ ] Graffiti line-art per art/style.md: outlined cloud forms, flat colour bands, hard highlight strokes, no spray effects. The planet is outlined and cel-lit from the upper left.
- [ ] Composite preview (L0 + L1 + L2 + planet at lower right, cut off by the right edge, with bricks, ball and HUD placeholders on top): the brick area stays under ~12% contrast and nothing reads as a ball, brick or power-up
- [ ] Palette per art/style.md (void #0a0e15, rust/orange #ffab4d family, cream, dusty blue #a9dcff family). No strong cyan. Violet/magenta is allowed only as dimmed nebula glow, clearly dimmer and less saturated than the reactor brick and power-up (style.md exception, user 2026-10-03).
- [ ] Each file is at most 1 MB
- [ ] `assets/parallax/space_l1_glow.png`: 1440×2160 RGBA (white, alpha = glow intensity), aligned pixel for pixel with `space_l1.png` and vertically seamless; the forks behind the brick rows (upper part of the well) are dimmer; at most 1 MB (for sim-lkp)

title: Add mouse paddle control with a Settings toggle
description:
## Problem / goal
Let the player steer the paddle with the mouse, selectable in Settings.

## Behaviour
- The Settings screen gets a "Paddle control: Mouse" / "Paddle control: Keyboard" button showing the current value; activating it (click, or Enter/Space when focused) toggles it. Default: Mouse.
- Mouse mode: the paddle follows the cursor's X position, clamped so it never enters the side walls (respecting the current paddle width).
- Arrow keys and A/D keep working in both modes. In Keyboard mode the mouse does not move the paddle.
- Session-only: the choice resets to Mouse when the app restarts.

## Out of scope
Persisting settings (config file / localStorage), mouse sensitivity, hiding or locking the cursor, gamepad.

## Notes for the coder
- New `ControlSettings` resource (e.g. `src/settings.rs` or under `src/menu/`), default `Mouse`.
- Paddle is `RigidBody::Dynamic` driven by `ConstantForce` in `paddle_movement` (`src/main.rs`). In mouse mode drive `LinearVelocity.x` toward the target X each frame (so Avian still resolves the ball bounce properly) instead of teleporting the Transform.
- Cursor -> world via `Window::cursor_position` + `Camera::viewport_to_world_2d`. Clamp with `Paddle.width` (Super-Sizer changes it) and `WINDOW_WIDTH`.
- Put target-X/clamp maths in a pure function so it is unit-testable headless (no window in tests).
- Reuse `src/menu/` (`menu_button`, focus navigation) from sim-v0i.2 / PR #8; extend `src/menu/settings.rs` (replace "Coming soon").
- Keep the paddle-hit "spin" in `ball_movement` working.
- Launch click (T1) and this both read mouse input only in `PlayState::Playing`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Settings shows "Paddle control: Mouse" by default; activating it switches to "Keyboard" and activating again switches back.
- [x] In Mouse mode, moving the cursor left/right makes the paddle follow it, and the paddle stops at the walls.
- [x] In Keyboard mode, moving the mouse does not move the paddle; arrows and A/D do.
- [x] In Mouse mode, arrows and A/D still move the paddle.
- [ ] In Mouse mode the paddle still bounces the ball, with the edge-angle spin (hitting near an edge sends the ball out at a steeper side angle).
- [x] Works natively and in the web build (`trunk serve`); unit tests for the clamp maths pass.
close_reason: Merged: mouse paddle control with Settings toggle (PR #18, https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/18). Note: AC5 (edge-spin in mouse mode) verified only by unit test, not an independent live capture.

title: Make power-up bricks take 2 hits and drop their power-up on break
description:
## Problem / goal
Power-ups currently drop on a timer from a random brick position. Instead, specific bricks should carry a power-up: the player targets them, they take 2 hits, and the power-up falls when the brick breaks.

## Behaviour
- Each run, exactly 6 of the 60 bricks are chosen at random to be power-up bricks. Each gets its kind from the existing weighted `PowerUpSpawner` registry.
- Power-up bricks look distinct (violet "reactor core" colour, e.g. `#b58cff`) from the start of the run.
- First hit: the brick stays, switches to a visibly cracked/darker look, +10 score.
- Second hit: the brick breaks, +10 score, and its power-up starts falling from the brick's position. Catching it with the paddle works exactly as today.
- Normal bricks still break in one hit.
- The timed random drops are removed; power-ups only ever come from broken power-up bricks.
- Win condition unchanged: the run is won when every brick (including 2-hit ones) is gone.

## Out of scope
New power-up kinds, other multi-hit brick types, level layouts, particles.

## Notes for the coder
- Components e.g. `BrickHealth(u8)` (or `Brick { hits_left }`) and `PowerUpBrick { kind }` (the kind type lives in `src/powerups/mod.rs`).
- `on_ball_collision` (`src/main.rs`) decrements health; only at 0 does it despawn and set `signals.broke_brick`. Swap the sprite colour on the cracked hit.
- Fire an event such as `BrickDestroyed { pos: Vec2, power_up: Option<PowerUpKind> }`; `src/powerups/mod.rs` observes it and spawns the falling power-up (reuse the existing spawn bundle and the per-run gravity ramp). Keeps `main.rs` ignorant of power-up internals.
- Choosing the 6 bricks: in `spawn_bricks` or via a `RestartGame`-time step owned by powerups; needs a weighted `pick()` on `Spawner<T>` (`src/spawner.rs`) without the timer. Remove the timer path from `spawn_power_ups` and update the doc comments and CLAUDE.md sections that describe timed spawns.
- Re-check the `brick_query.iter().count() <= 1` win check in `ball_movement` with 2-hit bricks (a cracked brick is still a brick).
- One ball contact must count as exactly one hit (`CollisionStart` fires once per touch start); add a test that a single bounce off a power-up brick only cracks it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Each new run shows exactly 6 visually distinct (violet) power-up bricks, in different positions across runs.
- [ ] Hitting a power-up brick once leaves it in place with a cracked look and adds 10 points; a second hit removes it and adds 10 more.
- [ ] Breaking a power-up brick spawns a falling power-up at its position; catching it with the paddle applies the effect (Super-Sizer widens the paddle).
- [ ] No power-ups appear except from broken power-up bricks (30 s of play without breaking one produces none).
- [ ] Clearing every brick, including the 2-hit ones, still wins the run.
- [x] `cargo test` includes passing tests for 2-hit break, drop-on-break and exactly-6-per-run.
- [x] Off-by-one win fixed (user-reported on master): with exactly one brick left (normal or cracked) the run continues; the run is won only when breaking the very last brick. Old test `breaking_the_last_brick_wins` encoded the bug and must be replaced.
close_reason: Merged: power-up bricks take 2 hits and drop on break, plus off-by-one win-check fix (PR #12, https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/12). Note: AC 2-5 (crack visual, drop-and-catch, no-timed-drops, 2-hit win) verified only by unit tests, not an independent live capture — worth a manual playthrough.

title: Restyle the game in the Steelbreak palette (shapes)
description:
## Problem / goal
Adopt the Steelbreak sci-fi industrial look (see `art/steelbreak_concept.png`, `art/steelbreak_keyart.png`, palette in `art/gen_concept.py`) in-game now, using coloured shapes, before real sprites arrive from the art pipeline.

## Behaviour
- Background: dark hangar void `#080b0f` (ClearColor), optional panel tone `#0c1118`.
- Ball: steel grey, rendered as a circle (not a square).
- Paddle: cyan emitter `#4fd8ff`, with lighter "prongs" at each end (child shapes).
- Brick rows cycle ceramic `#ff6a4d`, titanium `#a9bacd`, tungsten `#ffab4d`.
- Power-up bricks: reactor-core violet `#b58cff`; cracked variant a darker violet.

- HUD: ink `#dde6f1` values, `#8a9aab` labels, uppercase "SCORE" / "LIVES"; overlay text in the same palette.

## Out of scope
Sprites/images (art pipeline, A1), particles, scanline/vignette post effects, HUD layout redesign.

- Round ball: `Mesh2d(Circle)` + `MeshMaterial2d<ColorMaterial>`; collider stays `Collider::circle`. Headless tests use `MinimalPlugins` — make sure mesh/material assets don't break `test_support::app()` (spawn may need `Assets<Mesh>` / `Assets<ColorMaterial>` guarded or initialised).

title: Load sprite assets from assets/ (native + web), proven with a placeholder background
description:
## Problem / goal
The game draws only coloured shapes and has no image-asset loading, so the Steelbreak sprites (art epic sim-rdl.5) have nowhere to land. Put the loading path in place on both targets, proven with one real slot: the play-area background.

## Behaviour
- New `assets/` directory at the repo root, following the art pipeline's layout: sprites live at `assets/sprites/<name>.png`.
- A placeholder `assets/sprites/background.png` (900×650, a plain dark Steelbreak gradient `#080b0f` → `#0c1118`, committed) is drawn behind everything in the play area on the main menu and in game. sim-rdl.5.3 (hangar background) later just overwrites this file; no code change needed.
- Native (`cargo run`): the background loads from `assets/`. Editing the PNG while the game runs updates it on screen within a couple of seconds (hot reload).
- Web (`trunk build` / `trunk serve`): `assets/` is copied into `dist/` and the background renders in the browser, with no 404s in the console for `.meta` files or the PNG.
- If the file is missing, the game still runs (the dark clear colour shows) and doesn't panic.

## Out of scope
Swapping bricks, ball, paddle or power-ups to sprites (the asset-producer files a coder issue per art task), texture atlases, loading screens, the real hangar art.

## Notes for the coder
- One place for handles: a `GameSprites` resource (e.g. `src/sprites.rs`, its own `Plugin`) loaded at `Startup` through `AssetServer`. Later sprite swaps add fields there. If sim-rdl.4 has landed, sit alongside `src/theme.rs`.
- Background: `Sprite` with that handle, `custom_size` 900×650, `Transform` z well below the game (e.g. -10), global rather than `DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame)`, so the menus show it too.
- Headless tests: `test_support::app()` runs on `MinimalPlugins` with no `AssetServer`. Register the sprites plugin from `main()` (like `ScriptPlugin`), not from `add_game`, or make it tolerate the missing asset server. `cargo test` must not need the PNG or a window.
- Web: add `<link data-trunk rel="copy-dir" href="assets" />` to `index.html`. Set `AssetPlugin { meta_check: AssetMetaCheck::Never, .. }` via `DefaultPlugins.set(...)`, otherwise Bevy requests `*.meta` files and trunk's server errors.
- Hot reload: enable bevy's `file_watcher` feature only in the non-wasm target dependencies in `Cargo.toml`, the same way `bevy_mod_scripting` is gated. The wasm build must not pull it in.
- `dist/` is being untracked by sim-ga0; don't commit build output.
- Update CLAUDE.md (module layout and the assets/wasm notes).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `assets/sprites/background.png` exists (900×650), and `cargo run` shows it behind the main menu and the game (dark gradient, not flat black).
- [x] While `cargo run` is live, replacing `assets/sprites/background.png` with a different image updates the window within a few seconds without a restart.
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the same background in the browser, and the devtools console/network shows no failed requests for the PNG or any `.meta` file.
- [x] Renaming the PNG away and running `cargo run` still starts the game without a panic.
- [x] `cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -e features` shows no `file_watcher` feature on bevy (it is native-only).
- [x] `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `trunk build` pass.

title: Brick variety: 7 classes, explosive variants, regen, shield, behaviour outlines, random board
description:
## Problem / goal
Give bricks real variety: seven Steelbreak brick classes with their own hit counts and behaviours, three kinds of explosive, visible outlines that tell the player what a brick does, all on a board that is randomised each run. There is no "level" concept yet. Authored layouts and progression are a future epic; for now every run builds a fresh random board.

## Decisions (user, 2026-09-28)
- Board: fully random each run, 7 rows × 10 columns. Every slot gets a weighted-random class. Exactly 6 power-up (reactor) bricks, as today.
- Hit counts (concept sheet): ceramic 1, titanium 2, tungsten 3, reactor/power-up 2, explosive 1, regen 2, shield glass 1.
- Explosive comes in 3 variants, told apart by outline: charge (8 around, 1 damage, chains), breach (4 orthogonal, destroy outright, chains), demolition (8 around, destroy outright, no chain).
- Regen alloy heals back to full if not finished quickly.
- Shield glass only takes damage from above (ball moving downward); other hits deflect.
- Behaviour outlines: placeholder outlines in code now, plus an art brief for the final look.

## Children
- .1 brick class model + random 7-row board + hit counts + shield rule
- .2 regen rule
- .3 explosive variants (blast + chains)
- .4 behaviour outlines (code placeholders)
- .5 art brief: behaviour outline concepts
close_reason: All children (sim-rdl.7.1-.7.9) closed; brick variety shipped

title: Brick classes with hit counts on a random 7-row board; shield glass breaks only from above
description:
## Problem / goal
Replace the uniform 10×6 grid of 1-hit bricks with a random board of seven Steelbreak brick classes with different hit counts. This is the foundation the regen, explosive and outline tasks build on.

## Behaviour
- The grid becomes 10 columns × 7 rows (it still sits above the paddle's reach with room to play).
- Every run builds a fresh random board. Each slot gets a class by weight: ceramic 30, titanium 20, tungsten 12, explosive 16 (split evenly across charge/breach/demolition), regen 12, shield 10.
- Every run contains at least one brick of each class and each explosive variant. The weighted fill is then patched to guarantee that.
- Exactly 6 bricks are power-up (reactor) bricks, as in sim-rdl.3; they replace random slots.
- Hit counts: ceramic 1, titanium 2, tungsten 3, reactor 2, explosive (all variants) 1, regen 2, shield glass 1. +10 score per hit point removed.
- A brick below full health shows its cracked look (darker variant of its class colour).
- Colours are the class face colours from `art/style.md` → Brick classes; explosive variants share the explosive red.
- **Shield glass:** it takes damage only when the ball is moving downward at contact, i.e. the ball got above it. Any other contact bounces normally, does no damage, and shows a short (~0.15 s) bright flash on the brick.
- Explosive and regen bricks behave as plain bricks with their hit counts in this task; their special rules come in .2 and .3.
- Win condition is unchanged: the run is won when no brick is left.

## Out of scope
Regen healing, explosions, behaviour outlines, sprites, authored levels, difficulty progression.

## Notes for the coder
- Introduce a `BrickClass` enum (`Ceramic, Titanium, Tungsten, Reactor, Explosive(ExplosiveKind), Regen, Shield`) with `max_hits()` and colour lookups in `src/theme.rs` (from sim-rdl.4). Store a grid cell (`BrickCell { row, col }`) on each brick: .3 needs neighbours.
- Board generation should be a pure function (rng in, `[[BrickClass; 10]; 7]` out) so "at least one of each" and "exactly 6 reactor" are unit-testable with a seeded rng.
- Power-up bricks today: `PowerUpBrick` + `BrickHealth` in `src/main.rs` / `src/powerups/mod.rs`. Reactor becomes a class; keep the `BrickDestroyed` drop path.
- Shield direction test: use the ball's `LinearVelocity.y < 0` at `CollisionStart` in `on_ball_collision`.
- Brick layout constants (`BRICK_ROWS`) and the tests that count `BRICK_ROWS * BRICK_COLS` need updating.
- Builds on sim-rdl.4's palette module; sprites come later via the art pipeline (`GameSprites`, sim-rdl.6).

- [x] Ceramic breaks in 1 hit, titanium in 2, tungsten in 3, power-up in 2, regen in 2; each hit adds 10 points; a damaged multi-hit brick shows a cracked (darker) look.

title: Regen alloy bricks heal to full if not finished within 3 s
description:
## Problem / goal
Regen alloy bricks should punish slow play: if not finished quickly, they heal.

## Behaviour
- Regen alloy has 2 hits. After it takes damage, a 3.0 s heal timer starts. Each further non-lethal hit restarts it.
- If the timer runs out before the brick breaks, it heals back to full hits and loses its cracked look.
- The timer pauses while the game is paused.
- Damage from explosions (.3) counts as a hit and restarts the timer.

## Out of scope
Partial healing, heal-rate power-ups, a visual countdown (the outline task may add a cue).

## Notes for the coder
- Component e.g. `Regen { timer: Timer }`, ticked in `Update` with `run_if(in_state(PlayState::Playing))`.
- Keep healing in its own system and module (e.g. `src/bricks/regen.rs`), reacting to a brick-damaged event if .1 introduced one; otherwise add one (`BrickDamaged { entity }`) rather than special-casing regen in `on_ball_collision`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Hitting a regen brick once cracks it; hitting it again within 3 s breaks it.
- [x] Hitting it once and waiting more than 3 s restores it to full (not cracked); it then again needs 2 hits.
- [ ] Pausing for 10 s while a regen brick is cracked does not heal it; after resuming it heals only once the remaining time has elapsed.
- [x] `cargo test` has passing tests for break-in-time, heal-after-timeout and pause-freezes-timer.

title: Explosive brick variants: charge, breach, demolition blasts with chaining
description:
## Problem / goal
Three explosive brick variants, each with a different blast, so explosives feel strategic.

## Behaviour
When an explosive brick is destroyed (by the ball or by another blast), its blast applies to neighbours by grid cell:
- **Charge:** the 8 surrounding bricks each take 1 hit. A neighbouring explosive destroyed this way explodes too (chains).
- **Breach:** the 4 orthogonal neighbours (left, right, above, below) are destroyed outright, whatever their hits left. Explosives destroyed this way explode too (chains).
- **Demolition:** the 8 surrounding bricks are destroyed outright. Explosives caught in it are destroyed without exploding (no chain).

In all variants:
- Blasts ignore shield glass's "from above" rule: a blast damages or destroys shield glass.
- Scoring: +10 per hit point removed by the blast (a 3-hit tungsten destroyed outright = +30).
- Power-up bricks destroyed by a blast drop their power-up as usual.
- Blast damage to a regen brick counts as a hit (restarts its heal timer).
- If a blast clears the last brick, the run is won.
- A short visual burst at the exploding brick (placeholder: a quick expanding flash quad).

## Out of scope
Screen shake, sound, particles, blast damage to the paddle or ball.

## Notes for the coder
- Resolve chains iteratively in one frame (a queue of pending explosions keyed by `BrickCell`), processing each brick at most once, to avoid double-counting and command-flush timing issues. Look bricks up by cell via a grid index resource rebuilt at spawn, or a query filtered by cell.
- Route destruction through the same path as ball destruction (`BrickDestroyed`, score, `broke_brick` signal) so power-up drops and the win check work unchanged. The win check in `ball_movement` relies on `broke_brick` + `brick_query.is_empty()`.
- Own module, e.g. `src/bricks/explosive.rs`, observing brick destruction.

title: Behaviour outlines for special bricks (coded placeholders)
description:
## Problem / goal
The player should be able to tell what a special brick does at a glance, before it matters. Add behaviour outlines as coded placeholders; the final look comes from the art brief (.5).

## Behaviour
Special bricks get an outline drawn around them, on top of the class colour. Plain classes (ceramic, titanium, tungsten) get none.
- **Explosive, charge:** solid red border (`#ff3b3b`), pulsing brightness (~1 Hz).
- **Explosive, breach:** red border bright only at the 4 side midpoints (a "+" read), pulsing.
- **Explosive, demolition:** thick double red border, pulsing faster (~2 Hz).
- **Regen:** green border (`#3dff7a`) that "breathes" slowly. While its heal timer runs it blinks faster the closer it is to healing.
- **Shield glass:** cyan border (`#4fd8ff`), brightest along its top edge (the side that breaks it).
- **Power-up / reactor:** violet border (`#b58cff`), steady glow.
- The outline disappears with the brick. Animation freezes while paused.

## Out of scope
Final outline art (.5), shaders, particles.

## Notes for the coder
- Build outlines as child entities (thin `Sprite` quads or a `Gizmo`-free mesh) so a later sprite swap only replaces the children. Put colours and timings in `src/theme.rs`.
- The regen cue reads the heal timer from .2. If .2 hasn't landed, gate that part behind the component's presence.
- The animation system gates on `PlayState::Playing`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Each special brick type shows its described outline; ceramic, titanium and tungsten have none.
- [x] The three explosive variants are distinguishable from each other by outline alone (checked in a screenshot of the running game).
- [ ] A cracked regen brick's outline blinks faster as its heal time runs out.
- [x] Outline animation stops while paused and resumes after.
- [x] Destroying a brick removes its outline with it; no orphan outline entities remain (test counts them).
- [x] `cargo test`, clippy and `trunk build` pass.

Static art; pulsing and blinking are done in code (alpha/scale). One frame per outline.

Placeholder behaviour and colours in sim-rdl.7.4; `art/style.md` brick-class table; `art/steelbreak_concept.png`.

title: Art: per-material damage steps (cracked + broken) and particle sheets
description:
## Subject
Per-material damage steps for all 7 Steelbreak brick classes (intact → cracked → broken) plus one greyscale particle
sprite sheet per material for the hit/break burst (bevy_enoki).

## Use in game
Brick entities (80x30 game size, sprites at 160x60). Each class decays in its own visual way — user: "Different style
bricks will decay differently, for example Ice is going to look different than fire". Damage is a mix: baked sprite
states (this issue) + a code/particle burst on hit and on break (pm spec, bevy_enoki 0.7 on Bevy 0.19). Particles are
loaded as `SpriteParticle2dMaterial::new(texture, 4, 1)` (sheet animated over the particle lifetime) and tinted by the
effect's `color_curve` in a `.particle.ron`, so the sheets are shape-only greyscale.
Every state must read at 1x against #0a0e15 and in greyscale; intact vs cracked vs broken must be distinct per class.

## Variants
Damage ladder: intact (exists) → `_cracked` (light) → `_broken` (heavy). Same plate silhouette as the intact sprite
(chipped corners allowed as in the existing cracked sprites).
- ceramic — cracked NEW: glaze spalling, small chips; broken NEW: large shards missing, raw fired clay showing.
- titanium — cracked NEW: dents and scoring; broken NEW: deep dents, a popped bolt, bent corner.
- tungsten — cracked NEW: gouges; broken NEW: deep gouges with heat-glowing orange (#ffab4d) edges.
- reactor — cracked NEW: hairline cracks with violet light behind; broken NEW: violet energy leaking out, seam flicker.
- explosive — cracked KEEP sim-rdl.5.4 r4/v4; broken NEW: heavier, "about to go".
- regen alloy — cracked KEEP sim-rdl.5.4 r5/v4; broken NEW: heavier fractures across the veins.
- shield glass — cracked KEEP sim-rdl.5.4 r6/v4; broken NEW: shatter web spread wider, pane pieces missing.
The 4 original classes' shared crack (sim-rdl.5.1 r3/v2) is retired.

Particle sheets (7): greyscale on transparency, horizontal strip of 4 frames, 32x32 each (128x32):
ceramic shard, titanium metal spark, tungsten hot slag, reactor energy wisp, explosive fire puff, regen spore,
shield glass fleck.

## Frames
Brick states static. Particle sheets: 4 frames each (animation over lifetime).

## References
Intact plates: sim-rdl.5.1 (r1/v1 recoloured) and sim-rdl.5.4 (explosive r1/v2, regen r2/v3, shield r3/v4) — use as
--ref. Existing cracked hints: sim-rdl.5.4 r4/v4, r5/v4, r6/v4. art/style.md brick-class table (regen keys on #FF00FF).

title: Particles: per-material hit/break bursts for all 7 brick classes
description:
## Problem / goal
sim-pdp.1 gives every brick the same generic hit sparks and break shatter, tinted by class. The user wants each material to decay and burst in its own way ("Ice is going to look different than fire"). This task gives each of the 7 brick classes its own textured hit and break effect, using the greyscale particle sheets from the art task sim-rdl.7.6.

## Behaviour
- **Per-class effects.** Each brick class has a hit effect and a break effect, loaded from `assets/particles/<class>_hit.particle.ron` and `<class>_break.particle.ron`. Each effect uses that class's sheet `assets/particles/<class>.png` (a 4-frame 128×32 greyscale strip, animated over the particle's lifetime). The effect is tinted with a `color_curve` from the `art/style.md` brick-class colours:
  - ceramic: clay/glaze shards
  - titanium: metal sparks
  - tungsten: hot slag (orange `#ffab4d` glow)
  - reactor: violet energy wisps
  - explosive: fire puffs
  - regen: spores
  - shield glass: glass flecks
- **Hit** (a brick damaged but not broken): the class's hit effect fires at the contact point. This replaces pdp.1's generic hit spark.
- **Break:** the class's break effect fires from the brick's centre. This replaces pdp.1's generic shatter.
  - Explosive bricks: this is the debris *under* the blast. The blast itself stays with sim-pdp.3.
  - Shield glass: the deflect glint (a non-damaging hit from below) also stays with sim-pdp.3. This task only covers the shield brick's real break.
- **Fallback:** if a class's sheet PNG is missing, its effect still plays with enoki's default quad in the class colour (no panic, no invisible effect). If a class's `.particle.ron` is missing, pdp.1's generic effect plays.
- pdp.1's pause freeze, run teardown and live-particle budget apply unchanged to the new effects.
- Web build shows them.

## Out of scope
- Damage sprite ladder (sibling task sim-rdl.7.9).
- Continuous smoke emitters on damaged bricks (they stay as pdp.1 built them).
- Explosion blasts, shield deflect glints, ball and paddle effects (sim-pdp.2, sim-pdp.3).
- Making the particle sheets (sim-rdl.7.6).

## Notes for the coder
- Builds on sim-pdp.1's `src/particles/` (`ParticleEffects` resource, event → effect observers for `BrickDamaged` / `BrickDestroyed`). Turn the single hit and break handles into per-`BrickClass` maps.
  - Explosive variants (Charge/Breach/Demolition) share one explosive effect.
- Load textures as `SpriteParticle2dMaterial::new(tex, 4, 1)`. Enoki effect files hot-reload natively. Keep that working.
- Keep gameplay renderer-free. Headless tests can assert the class → effect path mapping (a pure fn) without a renderer.
- Document the effect file naming in CLAUDE.md under the particles section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Hitting a tungsten brick without breaking it shows orange slag particles at the contact point. Hitting a titanium brick shows metal sparks. The two are visibly different.
- [ ] Breaking each of the 7 classes (ceramic, titanium, tungsten, reactor, explosive, regen, shield) shows its own textured break effect. Seven distinct looks are visible in one run, and none is the old generic shatter.
- [ ] Breaking an explosive brick shows fire-puff debris; its blast behaviour and effects are unchanged
- [ ] Temporarily renaming `assets/particles/ceramic.png` still shows a ceramic-coloured break effect (plain quads) and no panic
- [ ] Editing `assets/particles/tungsten_hit.particle.ron` while the game runs natively changes the tungsten hit effect without a restart
- [ ] Pausing freezes the new effects; going to the main menu leaves no particle spawners (existing pdp.1 test still passes)
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the per-class effects in the browser
- [ ] `cargo test` (including a unit test that every `BrickClass` maps to hit/break effect paths that exist on disk), clippy and `trunk build` pass
close_reason: Per-material hit/break particle bursts for all 7 brick classes (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/58)

title: Brick damage sprite ladder: cracked/broken by hits left, under pdp.1 smoke
description:
## Problem / goal
Damaged bricks currently keep their intact sprite and only smoke (sim-pdp.1). The user wants baked decay art too. Each material decays in its own way, shown by `_cracked` and `_broken` sprites from the art task sim-rdl.7.6, layered under pdp.1's smoke.

## Behaviour
- **Ladder rule:** `_broken` means the next hit destroys the brick.
  - 3-hit bricks (tungsten): 3 hits left → `_intact`, 2 left → `_cracked`, 1 left → `_broken`.
  - 2-hit bricks (titanium, reactor, regen): 2 left → `_intact`, 1 left → `_broken`.
  - 1-hit bricks (ceramic, explosive, shield glass) never show a damage sprite.
- **Sprites:** `assets/sprites/bricks/<class>_cracked.png` and `<class>_broken.png`. They are drawn at the same size and position as the intact sprite, and the behaviour outlines are unaffected.
- **Smoke stays.** pdp.1's damage smoke and spark emitter still runs on top of the damage sprite, heavier as hits run out.
- **Regen heal:** a regen brick healing back to full returns to `_intact` (and its smoke stops, as today).
- **No tint.** No colour darkening or tint is used for damage. Any interim `brick_sprite_tint` / `CRACKED_DARKEN` path left from sim-bu6 or sim-pdp.1 is removed.
- **Fallback:** if a damage sprite file is missing, the brick keeps its intact sprite. If the intact sprite is missing too, the brick keeps the coded class colour. There is no panic and nothing turns invisible.

## Out of scope
- Particle bursts (sim-rdl.7.8) and the smoke emitters (sim-pdp.1).
- Painting the sprites (sim-rdl.7.6).
- Changing any brick's hit count.

## Notes for the coder
- Put the pure mapping in `src/bricks.rs` so it's testable headlessly: e.g. `damage_look(class, hits_left) -> DamageLook { Intact, Cracked, Broken }`.
- Extend `GameSprites` / `SkinPlugin` (`src/sprites.rs`) with per-class cracked and broken handles. Re-skin whenever `BrickHealth` changes, including regen heals, which raise health.
- The intact-sprite skinning comes from sim-bu6 (PR #36). Build on it.
- Existing `*_cracked.png` files in `assets/sprites/bricks/` are older art; sim-rdl.7.6 replaces or keeps them per class. Use whatever is on disk.
- Update CLAUDE.md's `bricks.rs` / `sprites.rs` notes (they still mention `cracked()` darkening).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A tungsten brick shows intact, then cracked after 1 hit, then broken after 2 hits, and it breaks on the 3rd hit
- [x] Titanium, reactor and regen bricks show intact, then broken after 1 hit (never the cracked sprite)
- [x] Ceramic, explosive and shield-glass bricks never show a damage sprite
- [ ] A damaged brick shows its damage sprite *and* pdp.1's smoke on top of it
- [x] A regen brick that heals back to full shows its intact sprite again
- [x] No damaged brick is tinted or darkened (grep: no damage tint or darken path remains)
- [x] Temporarily renaming `titanium_broken.png` makes a 1-hit-left titanium brick show its intact sprite, with no panic
- [ ] `cargo test` (unit test of `damage_look` for every class × hits-left value), clippy and `trunk build` pass

title: Power-up time capsules: top-right gauges showing time left on active timed power-ups
description:
## Problem / goal
Timed power-ups (today: Super-Sizer, which widens the paddle for a while) give no feedback about how long they have left. Show each active timed power-up as a "time capsule" in the top-right corner that drains as its time runs out.

## Behaviour
- Each active timed effect gets one capsule, stacked vertically in the top-right corner, below the HUD's sector label (sim-a7k.2) if present. Space for up to 3 at once, newest at the bottom.
- A capsule shows:
  - the power-up's icon (today the shared `powerup.png`)
  - a pill-shaped gauge whose fill drains left-to-right, in proportion to the remaining time
  - the seconds left, e.g. `6.2s`
- Steelbreak HUD style: cyan `#4fd8ff` fill on a dark `#16202c` pill, thin light outline. The fill turns amber `#ffab4d` and blinks in the last 2 s.
- Picking up the same power-up again refreshes its timer: the capsule refills in place and no duplicate appears.
- When an effect expires, its capsule disappears and the others close the gap.
- **Pause:** capsules freeze while paused (the effect timers already do).
- **New run / level:** capsules clear on a new run and on a level change (they follow `ActiveEffects`).
- Non-timed power-ups (none exist yet) get no capsule.

## Out of scope
New power-ups, per-kind icons (follow-up art), capsule art from the art pipeline (shapes/UI nodes first), sounds.

## Notes for the coder
- Drive everything from `ActiveEffects` (`src/powerups/mod.rs`), which already holds each effect's `kind` and `Timer`. The capsule system reads it every frame, so no extra bookkeeping is needed and expiry is automatic, matching the "recompute from ActiveEffects" pattern in CLAUDE.md.
- Bevy UI (`Node`) anchored top-right, run-scoped (`DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame)`).
- Headless test: insert effects into `ActiveEffects` and assert the capsule count, order and fill fraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Catching Super-Sizer shows a capsule in the top-right with the power-up icon, a full cyan gauge and the seconds remaining; the gauge drains as time passes.
- [ ] In the last 2 s the gauge turns amber and blinks; when the effect ends the capsule disappears.
- [ ] Catching Super-Sizer again while active refills the same capsule (no second capsule).
- [ ] With 2–3 timed effects active (test-injected), the capsules stack top-right in pickup order, and closing a gap works when a middle one expires.
- [ ] Pausing freezes the capsules; a new run starts with none.
- [ ] `cargo test` covers count/order/fill from `ActiveEffects`; clippy and `trunk build` pass.
close_reason: Power-up time capsules shipped (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/57)

title: Parallax background: three downward-drifting space layers and a distant planet, clipped to the playfield well
description:
## Problem / goal
The background is one flat image behind the playfield. This task adds depth with a slow, ambient **deep-space parallax** behind the playfield: three layers that drift downward at different speeds, plus a distant planet. It's built in-house (`bevy-parallax` was rejected: it targets Bevy 0.14/0.15 and is driven by the camera, while our camera is fixed). The art is sim-rdl.10. This task ships the code with placeholder art at the same sizes, so the real art drops in later with no code change.

## Behaviour
- **Area:** the layers fill exactly the **1440×1080 playfield well**. The opaque frame panels cover the sides on every screen. Nothing from the layers may show outside the well: not in the side panels, and not in the letterbox/pillarbox bars that `ScalingMode::AutoMin` leaves on odd window shapes.
- **Layers, back to front** (all drift **downward**; speeds in world px/s, user 2026-10-03 "gentle"):

| Layer | File | Size | Tiling | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 stars | `assets/parallax/space_l0.png` | 1440×2160 opaque | vertical, seamless | 8 |
| L1 gas clouds | `assets/parallax/space_l1.png` | 1440×2160 RGBA | vertical, seamless | 16 |
| L2 near wisps | `assets/parallax/space_l2.png` | 1440×2160 RGBA | vertical, seamless | 28 |
| L3 planet | `assets/parallax/planet.png` | ~640×640 RGBA | none | 2 |

- **Tiling layers** wrap forever: when a tile's top moves past, the next tile continues with no visible seam, gap or jump.
- **Planet:** non-tiling. It starts in the lower right of the well, partly cut off by the right frame edge (its centre about 80–120 px inside the right edge). It drifts down at 2 px/s. Once fully below the well, it re-enters from just above the top at the same x, a cycle of about 14 minutes. Always clipped to the well.
- **Always moving:** the layers drift on every screen (main menu, settings, in game, paused, game over). It's ambient and not gameplay, so it ignores `PlayState` and the physics clock. It survives restarts (global, like the frame).
- **Depth order:** the old `Background` sprite (z −10, kept as the fallback) < L0 < L1 < L2 < planet < `FRAME_Z` (−5) < gameplay. The planet sits in front of the clouds (it's "far", but it reads better unobscured); swapping it behind L1/L2 is a one-line change in the layer table.
- **Missing files:** a layer whose PNG is missing or fails to load is simply not drawn; there's no panic. With every file missing, the game looks as it does today (`background.png`).
- **Placeholders (user 2026-10-03):** the coder commits simple placeholder PNGs at the exact sizes above:
  - L0: dim, sparse star dots on #0a0e15
  - L1 and L2: a few faint outlined blobs, low alpha, seamless top to bottom
  - planet: a plain dim outlined circle
  - Keep them dark (under ~12% contrast behind the bricks) and well under 1 MB. sim-rdl.10's art overwrites them later.
- Works on web.

## Out of scope
- The real art (sim-rdl.10).
- Paddle-follow shift, speed-ups reacting to events, camera-driven parallax.
- Per-level background skins (later, sim-a7k roadmap): keep the layer table in one place so it can be swapped then.
- A RON/asset config file: a Rust table is enough for now.
- Hot-swapping speeds at runtime.

## Notes for the coder
- New module `src/parallax/` with its own `ParallaxPlugin`, one line in `add_game`. It touches the renderer, so headless tests cover only the pure parts.
- One `const LAYERS: &[LayerSpec]` table: path, z, speed, `tiled: bool`, and for the planet its start position.
- **Wrap maths** as a pure fn (e.g. `fn tile_offset(elapsed_secs, speed, period) -> f32` in `[0, period)`, plus the planet's `fn planet_y(elapsed, …)` with re-entry), unit-tested: continuity at the wrap point, no jump, period correct.
- Use **real time** (`Time<Virtual>` or `Time<Real>`), not `Time<Physics>`, so pausing doesn't stop it. Don't gate on `PlayState`.
- **Clipping to the well:**
  - Option A: draw each tiling layer as a sprite sized 1440×1080 that shows a moving 1440×1080 sub-rect of its texture (`Sprite.rect`), using two sprites, or a `SpriteImageMode::Tiled` sprite, across the wrap.
  - Option B: any approach that keeps pixels inside ±720 × ±540.
  - The planet must be clipped at the well's right and bottom edges too. The frame panel covers the right side, but the bottom edge goes into letterbox space, so crop it with `rect` (or an equivalent).
  - Verify in a tall, narrow window.
- Leave the `Background` sprite (`sprites.rs`, z −10) as the fallback under L0. Add the layer handles to `GameSprites` or a `ParallaxImages` resource. Either way, they must be part of any "all handles" iteration.
- Assets ship to web via trunk's `copy-dir` of `assets/`.
- Docs: `//!` for the module, one CLAUDE.md module-index line, and a short cross-cutting note (layers are global, real time, clipped to the well).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `cargo run`: on the main menu, three placeholder layers drift downward at visibly different speeds (stars slowest, wisps fastest), and the planet is lower right, partly cut off by the right frame panel
- [ ] Watching a tiling layer through at least one full wrap shows no seam, gap or jump. Speeding up the clock temporarily, or waiting about 70 s for L2, is fine.
- [ ] The drift keeps going on the pause menu and the game-over screen, and through a restart (Play again) without jumping back
- [x] Resizing the window to tall/narrow and wide/short shapes: no layer pixels appear in the letterbox/pillarbox bars or over the side panels; the planet is clipped at the well edge
- [x] Renaming `assets/parallax/space_l1.png` and restarting: L1 is gone, the others still drift, no panic. With all four renamed, the game shows today's `background.png`.
- [ ] The bricks, ball, paddle and HUD read clearly over the placeholders; nothing in the background looks like a gameplay object
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the drifting layers in the browser
- [ ] `cargo test` includes unit tests for the wrap maths (continuity at the wrap, correct period) and the planet re-entry; clippy and `trunk build` pass; each placeholder PNG is at the contract size and at most 1 MB
close_reason: Parallax deep-space layers and planet behind the playfield well (https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/75)

title: Power-up: Collapse — remaining bricks fall down their columns with a staggered gravity drop
description:
## Problem / goal
A rare wildcard power-up that shakes up the board. The bricks visibly fall rather than teleport.

## Behaviour
- **The power-up:**
  - New `PowerUpKind::Collapse` (working name), a self-contained plugin following the `super_sizer.rs` pattern.
  - Spawn weight 0.5 (Super-Sizer is 1.0), at most once per level. If it was already dropped this level, the drop re-picks another kind.
  - Neutral/chaos: it isn't meant to help or hurt.
- **On pickup, gravity collapse:**
  - In every column of the level grid, the remaining bricks fall down to fill the empty cells below them, stopping at the grid's bottom row. They never leave the grid, and their top-to-bottom order is kept.
  - Columns with no gaps don't move. `BrickCell` is updated.
  - Each brick keeps its class, health, damage look, regen timer, outline/frame and any reactor power-up attachment.
- **Animation (staggered gravity drop):**
  - The lowest bricks start first, and each brick above starts a little later.
  - Each falls with acceleration (ease-in, like gravity) and lands with a small bounce and a dust puff (bevy_enoki effect).
  - The whole collapse takes about 0.6–0.9 s.
- **The ball keeps flying.**
  - While a brick is moving it has no collision (`ColliderDisabled`); it becomes solid again when it lands.
  - If the ball overlaps the landing cell at that moment, the brick waits, still non-solid, until the ball has left.
  - Pausing freezes the animation, and it resumes on unpause.
- **Capsule:** same `powerup.png`, tinted a distinct new theme colour (added to `theme.rs`). The final art comes later through an art brief.

## Out of scope
Other shuffle modes (random permutation, mirror, sort by class), combos (sim-mnt), and the capsule art itself.

## Notes for the coder
- `src/powerups/super_sizer.rs` pattern: register with `PowerUpSpawner` and observe `PowerUpCollected`. The Spawner needs a way to exclude a kind (at most once per level), reset on `LevelStarted`.
- Bricks are `RigidBody::Static`. Move them by Transform while the collider is disabled, then re-enable. The explosive `resolve_blast` reads `BrickCell`, so the cell must be updated before the brick becomes solid.
- The landing check uses the ball's collider AABB against the target cell rect.
- Gate the animation system on `PlayState::Playing`.
