- [ ] Test: health, BrickMaxHits, class and reactor power-up attachment are preserved per brick after the collapse
- [ ] Test: Collapse is never picked twice in one level; it can be picked again after LevelStarted
- [ ] Test: a brick whose landing cell overlaps the ball stays non-solid until the ball leaves, then becomes solid
- [ ] Native run (screen recording or frames): bricks fall staggered from the bottom up with a landing bounce and dust puff, total ≤ ~0.9 s; the ball passes through falling bricks; pausing mid-collapse freezes it

title: Art: titanium (and regen) cracked plates barely differ from intact at 1x
description:
Found while verifying the graffiti brick set in sim-23j (PR #73 art).

## Problem
The sim-rdl.7.9 rule is that each damage state looks clearly worse than the one before. Two cracked plates barely differ from their intact plates at draw size (80×30 world, 1x on #0a0e15):
- **titanium_cracked.png**: one small crack in the top-right corner. Against titanium_intact.png, only **2.8% of pixels change at 1x** (mean luminance difference 4.8/255; 7.2% at 160×60).
- **regen_cracked.png**: fine hairline cracks. **9.2% of pixels change at 1x**, versus 17–22% for most other rungs.

For comparison, the rest of the 1x changed-pixel figures:
- ceramic i→c: 17%
- tungsten i→c / c→b: 18% / 22%
- reactor i→c / c→b: 14% / 21%
- explosive i→c: 21%
- shield i→c: 20%
- titanium c→b: 10.5%
- regen c→b: 21%

## Impact
The default ladders never show these two rungs: titanium and regen have 2 hits, so they go intact→broken. The cracked plates only appear for level bricks with `hits=3` or more (sim-a7k.1). So this doesn't block the default game, but a hand-authored level with `titanium hits=4` would look undamaged after its first hit.

## Ask
Repaint titanium_cracked.png, and optionally regen_cracked.png, so the cracking reads at 1x. A good target is roughly as much visible damage as tungsten_cracked. Keep the 160×60 RGBA contract; `sprites::tests::the_brick_asset_contract_holds` pins it.

## How to reproduce
Composite each `assets/sprites/bricks/<class>_<state>.png` at 80×30 on #0a0e15 side by side (intact | cracked | broken).

- [x] Cracks are bold graffiti keyline cracks with highlight edges, not hairlines; regen's circuit lines stay distinguishable from its cracks

title: Replace GameStatus with Bevy States and pause physics outside play
description:
## Problem / goal
Replace the hand-checked `GameStatus` resource with a real Bevy state machine as the foundation for menus. No new UI in this task.

## Behaviour
- `AppState { MainMenu, InGame, GameOver }` plus an `InGame` sub-state `PlayState { Playing, Paused }`. In this task the initial state is `InGame` (the menu arrives in the next task).
- Ball, paddle, bricks and HUD spawn when entering `InGame` and are removed when leaving it. Walls and camera stay global.
- Avian's physics clock (`Time<Physics>`) is paused whenever the state is not `InGame/Playing`, and resumed when it is. This replaces the manual velocity-zeroing at game end.
- P or Esc toggles Playing <-> Paused; the existing overlay text shows while paused.
- Losing the last life or clearing all bricks goes to `GameOver`, with a won/lost outcome kept in a resource; the existing text is shown; R starts a new run.
- A new run always resets score to 0 and lives to 3 (one constant); the lives label is driven by that constant. `RestartGame` is still broadcast so power-ups reset themselves.
- Remove the unused `QuitGamme` event.

## Out of scope
Any new menu UI (next tasks), settings, audio.

## Notes for the coder
- `GameStatus` checks to replace: `src/main.rs` (`paddle_movement`, `on_ball_collision`, `ball_movement`, `restart_game`, `update_ui`) and `src/powerups/mod.rs` (3 systems, ~lines 103/143/162). Prefer `run_if(in_state(...))`.
- Keep the `PaddleMovementSet` / `TickActiveEffects` ordering sets working.
- The `RestartGame` observer pattern (`reset_on_restart`) must still fire on every new run.
- Power-up timers must not tick while paused: check what clock `ActiveEffects` ticks on, or gate the tick system.
- Lives today: initial 5 (`insert_resource(Lives(5))`), restart 3, label hard-coded "Lives: 3" — unify on 3.
- Must still build for wasm; don't touch the scripting cfg-gates. Update CLAUDE.md's `GameStatus` notes to describe the state machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `cargo build` and `trunk build` both succeed.
- [ ] On launch, the game plays as it does today (ball moves, paddle responds, bricks break, score goes up).
- [ ] Pressing P or Esc while playing freezes the ball, paddle, falling power-ups and active power-up timers and shows the paused text; pressing P or Esc again resumes from the same positions.
- [ ] Losing all lives shows the game-over text and nothing on screen keeps moving.
- [ ] Clearing all bricks shows the win text and nothing on screen keeps moving.
- [ ] Pressing R on the game-over/win screen starts a fresh run: score 0, lives 3, full brick wall, no active power-ups.
- [ ] The HUD shows "Lives: 3" on first launch and after every restart.
close_reason: Bevy States repllace GameStatus; physics paused outside play (PR #7)

title: Add main menu and Settings screen
description:
## Problem / goal
Give the game a title/main menu so the player chooses to start, with a Settings entry that later work will fill in.

## Behaviour
- The app starts in `MainMenu`: title "BREAKOUT" and buttons **Start**, **Settings**, **Quit** (Quit native only; not spawned on wasm). The game world is not visible or simulating behind the menu.
- Start -> `InGame/Playing` with a fresh run (score 0, lives 3).
- Settings -> new `AppState::Settings` screen: heading "Settings", text "Coming soon", a **Back** button returning to the main menu. Esc on Settings also goes back.
- Quit -> exits the app.
- Input: buttons show hover and pressed states under the mouse and respond to clicks. Up/Down or W/S moves a visible focus highlight (wrapping), Enter or Space activates the focused button.
- Button, focus and navigation code lives in a small reusable module `src/menu/` that the pause / game-over task reuses.

## Out of scope
Actual settings, pause menu and game-over screen (next task), gamepad, transitions.

## Notes for the coder
- Bevy UI (`Node`, `Button`, `Interaction`), with screen entities scoped to their state (despawned on exit).
- Quit: `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, write `AppExit`.
- Builds on the AppState from the previous task; change the initial state to `MainMenu`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Launching (native and web) shows the main menu with Start and Settings, plus Quit on native only; no ball moves behind it.
- [x] Clicking Start begins a game with score 0 and lives 3.
- [x] Clicking Settings shows "Settings" / "Coming soon" with a Back button; clicking Back or pressing Esc returns to the main menu.
- [x] Up/Down (or W/S) visibly moves the highlight between buttons and wraps around; Enter or Space activates the highlighted button.
- [x] Hovering a button with the mouse changes its appearance.
- [x] On native, Quit closes the window; the browser build shows no Quit button.
- [x] `cargo build` and `trunk build` succeed.

title: Add pause menu and Game Over / Win screen
description:
## Problem / goal
Turn the text-only pause and end-of-game overlays into real menus so the player can resume, replay, or return to the title screen.

## Behaviour
- Paused: a menu over the frozen game with title "Paused" and buttons **Resume** and **Main menu**. P or Esc still toggles pause. Main menu abandons the run.
- GameOver: shows "GAME OVER" or "YOU WIN!", the final score, and buttons **Play again** and **Main menu**. R still works as a Play again shortcut.
- Both screens reuse the `src/menu/` module (same mouse + keyboard behaviour as the main menu).

## Out of scope
Restart-from-pause, high scores, transitions/animations.

## Notes for the coder
- Replaces the `GameOverText` overlay strings in `update_ui`.
- Main menu -> MainMenu must fully tear down the run so Start begins fresh (RestartGame still reaches power-ups).

- [x] Resume (click, Enter, or Esc/P) continues the game exactly where it was.
- [x] Main menu from pause returns to the title menu; Start from there begins a fresh run (score 0, lives 3, full bricks, no power-ups).

- [ ] Play again (click, Enter, or R) starts a fresh run; Main menu returns to the title screen.

title: Game-producer lane and human-code lane
description:
## Problem / goal
The game works but lacks a professional feel. That is a design and polish problem, not a pipeline one. The owner wants to play a "game-producer" role: research references, playtest, and write extensively about what the game should feel like, so the pm can turn that into epics and specs. The owner also wants to keep their own coding skills sharp through a tests-first lane for small isolated behaviours.

## Behaviour
Two children: (1) a `docs/vision/` area with feel-brief template feeding the pm, (2) a `human-code` label and tests-first workflow.

## Out of scope
- Changing the stage:* pipeline for agent-built work.
- Automating the producer's research or playtesting.

title: docs/vision: vision and feel-brief template that feeds the pm
description:
## Problem / goal
Give the owner a place to write the vision and "feel briefs" (what the player should feel, and how to tell it's right), and make the pm use them when speccing polish work, so approved specs carry the owner's taste.

## Behaviour
- Create `docs/vision/README.md` (how the lane works), `docs/vision/vision.md` (pillars, target feel, references, anti-goals; seeded with prompts for the owner to fill in) and `docs/vision/feel-brief-template.md`.
- Feel-brief template sections: Moment (e.g. brick break), What the player should feel, References (games, clips, sounds), Concrete levers (shake amplitude, hit-stop ms, particle count, easing, SFX variation), How we'll know it's right (observable/measurable checks), Out of scope.
- pm doc: when asked to spec polish/feel work, read `docs/vision/` first, interview against the brief, and turn each brief into a small epic of issues whose acceptance criteria use the brief's concrete levers; never invent taste not in the docs, ask instead.
- Add 3 example brief stubs (paddle hit, brick break, ball trail) for the owner to rewrite.

## Out of scope
- Writing the owner's actual vision content.
- Any gameplay code.

## Notes for the coder
- The pm doc (`~/.claude/agents/pm.md`) is outside the repo; list the edit in the PR description.
- Keep each file short; the owner will grow them.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] The three docs and three stub briefs exist and are linked from docs/agent-workflow.md
- [ ] pm doc says to read docs/vision/ for polish/feel specs
- [ ] A dry run: from one stub brief the pm produces a stage:spec epic whose acceptance criteria use concrete numeric levers

comments.text:
[note] pm: owner's core-gameplay vision (user, 2026-10-04), recorded as seed material for docs/vision/vision.md. The owner writes or edits the final wording (writing vision content is out of scope for this task's coder, but this note should be pointed to as the first candidate pillar).

**"Tetris + Breakout": breaking in the right order, not just breaking.**
- **Bricks fall:** bricks break, and the ones above fall and land in the next available spot, like Tetris.
- **Neighbours transform bricks:** depending on the elements of its new neighbours, a brick takes on an effect or transforms. Examples from the owner: *hot sand + heat → glass*; another combination might produce *steel*.
- **The goal changes:** not just clearing bricks, but breaking them **in an order** to set up falls and combinations.
- **That needs ball-path control.** The player needs ways to steer the ball, e.g.:
  - a **holding pattern** that hits a **rebound point** repeatedly
  - sending the ball into zones or objects that **slow it** or **change its trajectory**

**Related work already in the queue:**
- **sim-rjt** (Collapse power-up, at stage:pr): columns fall with a staggered gravity drop. It's the falling mechanic in power-up form.
- **sim-mnt** (P4 epic idea, 2026-09-30): neighbour combos, where adjacent materials produce effects or power-ups (fire + glass). The transformation rules belong there.
- The brick classes, explosive neighbourhood resolution (BrickCell grid) and the dev console tuning (sim-dj6) are the technical base.

**Open questions for the vision doc / a later interview:**
- Is falling always on, or a mode/level property?
- The element list and the transformation table.
- Which ball-control tools exist (paddle abilities, level objects, power-ups)?
- How is "right order" rewarded (score multipliers, required for clearing, puzzle levels)?

title: human-code lane: tests-first issues the owner implements
description:
## Problem / goal
The owner wants to keep their coding skills sharp. Agents should hand them small, isolated behaviours to implement themselves, tests-first, while the agents do the production coding.

## Behaviour
- New label `human-code`, outside the automated `stage:*` flow. Roles skip issues carrying it when picking work.
- Flow: the pm/owner picks a small isolated behaviour -> the coder agent writes the failing tests and a short brief (what to build, where, the API the tests expect) and opens a draft PR containing only the tests -> the owner implements on that branch until `cargo test`/clippy pass -> the issue moves to `stage:review` and the reviewer reviews it like any other PR.
- Document in `docs/agent-workflow.md` and the `beads-queue` skill; the pm can file `human-code` issues from the owner's design notes.

## Out of scope
- Auto-grading or hinting the owner's implementation.
- Running the tester or pr-manager differently for these PRs.

## Notes for the coder
- Tests must fail for the right reason (compile against the expected API with stubs returning `todo!()` where needed, or `#[ignore]`-free failing assertions).
- `beads-queue` skill is outside the repo; list the edit in the PR description.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] `human-code` issues are never claimed by the coder, reviewer, tester or pr-manager until the owner moves them to stage:review
- [ ] For a sample behaviour, the coder produces a tests-only draft PR whose tests fail and whose brief names the expected API
- [ ] After the owner's implementation the same PR goes green and is reviewed by the reviewer role
- [ ] Documented in docs/agent-workflow.md

title: Serialize native GUI runs on the shared X display (lock script, unique window titles, clean teardown)
description:
## Problem / goal
All agent roles share one X display (WSLg `DISPLAY=:0`), and every native window is titled "Breakout". Concurrent native runs from different roles (the coder's `timeout cargo run` smoke checks, and a duplicate tester session) sent input to and killed each other's windows, and left an orphaned `target/debug/sim` with PPID=1. Testers lost time retrying, and some criteria were only partly verified live. Make native runs exclusive, identifiable and cleanly torn down, and give the tester standard tooling.

## Behaviour
- New `scripts/native-run.sh [--label <text>] [--wait <secs>] [-- <extra cargo args>]`: the only sanctioned way for any agent to launch the native game.
  - Takes an exclusive `flock` on a shared lock file (e.g. `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/breakout-display-0.lock`, keyed by `$DISPLAY`) for the whole run. It writes a holder record next to it: role (`$AGENT_ACTOR`), label/issue, pid, start time.
  - If the lock is held, it waits up to `--wait` seconds (default 0 = fail fast). Otherwise it exits non-zero with a message naming the current holder, e.g. `display :0 busy: tester@tester (sim-rdl.2) pid 1234 since 23:10:05`. A duplicate role instance therefore gets a clear, logged refusal instead of silently cross-talking.
  - The game runs with a unique window title: `Breakout [<actor> <label>]`.
  - It runs the game in its own process group. On script exit, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or `timeout`, it kills the whole group (cargo plus the `sim` child) and releases the lock, so no process is left reparented to init.
  - Prints the window title, and the X window id once mapped (via `xdotool search --sync --name`), so drivers target that exact window.
- The game reads an optional `BREAKOUT_WINDOW_TITLE` env var for the window title, native only. The default stays "Breakout". Wasm is unaffected.
- `.claude/workflow.yaml`, `functional.run`: replace the bare `cargo run` with `scripts/native-run.sh --label <issue-id>`. Add a note that drivers must use xdotool/wmctrl against the printed window id, never a name search for plain "Breakout".
- `docs/agent-workflow.md` (or a short `scripts/README.md`): how to run, drive (`xdotool key --window <id>`, `xdotool mousemove --window`), screenshot (`import -window <id>` / `xwd`) and why. Also note that the coder never launches the native game.

## Duplicate role instances
The `agent-team` launcher already refuses to start a role whose tmux window exists. The duplicate tester that caused the sim-v0i.2/.3 incidents was a session started outside the launcher. In this repo, the display lock above is the guard: a second instance can't drive `:0` and is told who holds it. Changes to the launcher (`~/.local/bin/agent-team`) and to the agent definitions live outside this repo and are out of scope for the coder; the pm tracks them with the user.

## Out of scope
Xvfb / per-worktree X servers, CI GUI runs, changes to `~/.local/bin/agent-team` or `~/.claude/agents/*`.

## Notes for the coder
- Pure tooling plus one tiny code change (`main()` window title from env inside the existing `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` area). No gameplay change.
- Process-group kill: `setsid` the child (or `set -m`), `trap 'kill -- -$pgid' EXIT INT TERM`; `flock -n` / `flock -w` on fd 9.
- `xdotool`, `wmctrl`, `xwd` and `import` are installed on this machine (user, 2026-09-27); the script should still fail with a clear message if xdotool is missing.
- shellcheck-clean if shellcheck is available.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `scripts/native-run.sh --label demo` opens the game with window title `Breakout [<actor> demo]` and prints its X window id.
- [x] While one run is live, a second `scripts/native-run.sh --label other` (from another worktree/shell) exits non-zero immediately with a message naming the holder (actor, label, pid); with `--wait 30` it starts once the first run ends.
- [x] Ending a run by closing the window, Ctrl-C, or `timeout 10 scripts/native-run.sh` leaves no `sim` or `cargo` process behind (`pgrep -f target/debug/sim` is empty) and releases the lock (a new run starts at once).
- [x] `xdotool key --window <printed id> p` pauses that game window, confirmed by `import -window <id>` screenshots before and after.
- [x] Plain `cargo run` still shows the title "Breakout"; `trunk build` succeeds (the env-var title is native-only).
- [x] `.claude/workflow.yaml` `functional.run` uses the script, and the driving/screenshot how-to is documented in the repo.
- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass.
close_reason: Merged: native-run.sh display lock, unique window titles, clean teardown (PR #21, https://github.com/frederickbrock/breakout/pull/21)

comments.author: coder@breakout
comments.text:
[meta] coder — likely source of some of the cross-talk: the coder role's own native smoke runs on DISPLAY=:0.

Evidence:
- Before handing off sim-rdl.6, sim-rdl.2 and sim-rdl.4, the coder ran `timeout 20-25 cargo run` from the coder worktree on the shared DISPLAY=:0, as a quick no-panic check. The runs started at 2026-09-27 21:46:47, 21:47:13, 22:30:22 and 23:27:37 UTC (first log line of each run).
- Three of those overlap the sim-rdl.1 test, whose `[test] pass` was at 22:51.
- Those windows had the same title, "Breakout". A tester script that picks the window by name could send its input to the coder's window, which would explain score, lives or pause changing on their own.
- `timeout` kills the window without a graceful-exit log line when the run ends, so it looks like the window vanished by itself.
- `timeout` signals `cargo`, not necessarily the `sim` child it spawned. The child can then be reparented to init, which would explain the orphaned target/debug/sim process with PPID=1. No stray sim processes remain now.

Not explained by the coder: sim-v0i.2 (tested 17:49-18:19) and sim-v0i.3 (20:55-21:18). The coder made no native runs before 21:46. For those, the more likely cause is a duplicate tester instance: sim-v0i.3's claim log shows tester@breakout reassigned to tester@tester.

Change on the coder side: the coder no longer launches the native game, so live native runs are left to the tester. Its checks stay build, clippy, cargo test and trunk build.

Still worth doing from the issue's list: a display lock (e.g. a lock file around any `cargo run` on :0), or per-worktree Xvfb, to guard against duplicate role instances.

title: Verify graffiti ball, paddle and power-up sprites in game and pin their asset contract
description:
## Problem / goal
The graffiti line-art ball, paddle and power-up sprites (sim-usq.2, PR #70) have merged. They replaced the old files in place, with the same paths and sizes, at 2x art:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `assets/sprites/ball.png` | 60×60 |
| `paddle_prong_left.png` / `paddle_prong_right.png` | 54×40 |
| `paddle_field.png` | 93×40, full-bleed and stretched |
| `powerup.png` | 48×48 |

The skin rules in `src/sprites.rs` should pick them up with no code change. This task confirms that in the running game, pins the asset contract with a test, and fixes code only if something visibly breaks.

## Behaviour
- **Ball:** draws as the graffiti sprite at `BALL_SIZE` (15 design px = 22.5 world). It still reads as a sphere and stays the clearest, highest-contrast object on screen, over every brick class and the background.
- **Paddle:**

The falling one is at `POWER_UP_SIZE` (24 design = 36 world), the capsule one at its icon size. Both read clearly, and the capsule icon reads on its dark backing plate (sim-ylv).

## Out of scope
- Changing the art. If a sprite is wrong (the ball doesn't read, a prong edge doesn't meet the field, wrong size), the coder files an `art` issue under the reskin epic sim-usq (`stage:brief`) with a screenshot, and doesn't patch it in code.

- Changing gameplay sizes.

- Likely no gameplay code change. If a gap or overlap shows, adjust `paddle_pieces` / `place_paddle_pieces` (`src/paddle.rs`) or the sprite `custom_size` in `src/sprites.rs`, and update `paddle_pieces_fit_seamlessly_at_normal_and_super_sized_widths` to match.

title: Painted frame side panels: verify wiring, add dark backing plates behind HUD and capsules
description:
## Problem / goal
The painted (graffiti line-art) side-panel frames landed in asset PR #66 (sim-73n.3): `assets/sprites/frame_left.png` and `frame_right.png`, 480×2160 at 2×. The skin rule already exists on master: `skin_frame` in `src/sprites.rs` draws the image at panel size and hides the coded `FramePiece`s. So the panels should already show the art. This task:
- confirms the art is wired correctly;
- makes the HUD (left panel) and the power-up capsules (right panel) readable on top of it.

They currently sit on the busy outlined linework. The art's dark recessed channel is only ~47 world px wide, too narrow for them.

## Behaviour
- **Frames:** both side panels show the painted art at 240×1080 world units on every screen (menu, game, pause, game over). The art isn't stretched, and the right panel is the mirror of the left.
  - The art's playfield-facing edge meets the playfield well with no gap or overlap. The ball still bounces on the physics wall at that line.
  - The coded girder, tie plates and edge lip are hidden once the art loads.
- **Fallback:** if a frame PNG is missing, that panel shows the coded frame, as it does today, with no panic.
- **HUD backing plates (left panel):** each HUD block (SCORE and LIVES) has a dark, semi-transparent rounded plate behind its label and value.
  - Plate colour is a new `theme` constant (e.g. `theme::HUD_PLATE`, a near-black steel at about 75–85% alpha).
  - The plate covers the text with a small padding and doesn't move with it as the value grows. It's sized to fit the widest value up to 6 digits.
  - The plates appear and disappear with the HUD (run-scoped, like the HUD text).
- **Capsule backing plates (right panel):** each active power-up capsule row (icon, gauge pill and seconds text) has the same kind of plate behind it.
  - The plate comes and goes with its capsule, moves with it when slots shift, and blinks with it in the warning phase only if that's natural; otherwise it stays solid.
- **Layering:** frame art < plates < HUD text and capsule contents. Plates are drawn whether or not the art has loaded; they look fine on the coded frame too.
- The web build shows all of the above.

## Out of scope
- New or changed frame art, and the graffiti reskin of other sprites (sim-usq).
- Moving the HUD or capsules into the art's channel, or changing HUD font sizes or layout.
- Menu screens' own panels.

## Notes for the coder
- The wiring is already done. Check it rather than rewrite it:
  - `FramePanel` spawns with `Sprite::from_color(.., panel_size())`, so `custom_size` is already 240×1080, and `apply()` only swaps the image and untints it.
  - `skin_frame` hides `FramePiece` children.
  - Asset paths live in `sprites.rs` (`FRAME_LEFT_PATH` / `FRAME_RIGHT_PATH`).
- Z: `FRAME_Z` = −5 (panel, with pieces at +0.01·i), HUD text at z 1.0. Put plates in between (e.g. z 0.5), and give the constant a name.
- HUD: `run.rs` `spawn_hud_line` (`HUD_X`, `HUD_MARGIN`, `HUD_BLOCK_SPACING`, `HUD_FONT_SIZE` = 36). The plate can be a sibling sprite spawned in the same place, carrying the HUD's `DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame)`.
